| A6,A8 | LayoverInput | LayoverInput\_1\_plainxml.xml | $CARMUSR/etc/programs/ioservice\_single1.xml |

###### 6.3.2. Integrator Camel routes and queue names

The infrastructure described here assumes that communication with ACES is done via an external ActiveMQ broker (refered to as *externalBroker* in the Camel route
configuration snippets below). Queue names should be reviewed in cooperation with API Hotels on a project configuration basis. The internal ActiveMQ queue names
basically match with those generated as IOServices configuration templates by the IOService builder based on the configuration
in [IOService builder and IOServer configuration](#stdif-api-hotels-ioservice-builder-configuration). However, for interfaces having both a batch and an on-event output, the sinks should be directed to a
common output queue. This applies to the interfaces sending crew and trip data to ACES:

| Interface | IOService name | Sink names | Output queues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | CrewDataHotel\_1\_requested\_plainxml | from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel\_1\_requested\_plainxml from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel\_1\_requested\_plainxml.error | from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel\_1\_plainxml from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel\_1\_plainxml.error |
| A1 | CrewDataHotel\_1\_event\_plainxml | from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel\_1\_event\_plainxml | from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel\_1\_plainxml |
| A2,A4 | CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_requested\_plainxml | from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_requested\_plainxml from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_requested\_plainxml.error | from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_plainxml from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_plainxml.error |
| A3 | CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_event\_plainxml | from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_event\_plainxml from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_event\_plainxml.error | from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_plainxml from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel\_1\_plainxml.error |

All Camel routes should be placed in the *‘clusterroutes’* Camel context.

####### 6.3.2.1. Interface A1 - Crew data sent to ACES

```
<route id="export_CrewDataHotel_1_plainxml">
  <from uri="internalBroker:queue:{{env:CCF_PREFIX}}from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel_1_plainxml" />
  <to uri="bean:LogMetrics" />
  <to uri="bean:FilehubReadAsStream" />
    <convertBodyTo type="java.lang.String"/>
    <removeHeaders pattern="JMS_AMQP*"/>
  <to pattern="InOnly" uri="externalBroker:queue:JCMS.V1.JMS.ACES_CREW_OUTBOUND"/>
  <toD uri="msglog:${routeId}:file:{{env:INTEGRATOR_LOG_MSG_DIR}}" />
  <to uri="bean:FilehubDelete" />
</route>
```

```
<route id="CrewDataHotel_1_plainxml_error">
  <from uri="internalBroker:queue:{{env:CCF_PREFIX}}from.ioservice.CrewDataHotel_1_plainxml.error" />
  <to uri="bean:LogMetrics?method=error" />
  <to uri="bean:FilehubReadAsStream" />
  <toD uri="msglog:CrewDataHotel_1_plainxml:file:{{env:INTEGRATOR_LOG_MSG_DIR}}?logAlways=true&amp;suffix=error" />
  <to uri="bean:FilehubDelete" />
</route>
```

####### 6.3.2.2. Interface A2, A3 and A4 - Trip data sent to ACES

```
<route id="export_CrewOnTripHotel_1_plainxml">
  <from uri="internalBroker:queue:{{env:CCF_PREFIX}}from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel_1_plainxml" />
  <to uri="bean:LogMetrics" />
  <to uri="bean:FilehubReadAsStream" />
    <convertBodyTo type="java.lang.String"/>
    <removeHeaders pattern="JMS_AMQP*"/>
    <choice>
        <!-- Messages should be routed to current/next queue according to header attributes. -->
        <when>
            <simple>${header[JMSType]} == &quot;Load-Pairings&quot;</simple>
            <to pattern="InOnly" uri="externalBroker:queue:JCMS.V1.JMS.ACES_OPS_NEXT_PAIRINGS_OUTBOUND"/>
        </when>
        <when>
            <simple>${header[current_pp]} == &quot;True&quot;</simple>
            <to pattern="InOnly" uri="externalBroker:queue:JCMS.V1.JMS.ACES_OPS_CURRENT_PAIRINGS_OUTBOUND"/>
        </when>
        <when>
            <simple>${header[next_pp]} == &quot;True&quot;</simple>
            <to pattern="InOnly" uri="externalBroker:queue:JCMS.V1.JMS.ACES_OPS_NEXT_PAIRINGS_OUTBOUND"/>
        </when>
        <otherwise>
            <to pattern="InOnly" uri="externalBroker:queue:JCMS.V1.JMS.ACES_OPS_NEXT_PAIRINGS_OUTBOUND"/>
        </otherwise>
    </choice>
    <toD uri="msglog:${routeId}:file:{{env:INTEGRATOR_LOG_MSG_DIR}}"/>
  <to uri="bean:FilehubDelete" />
</route>
```

```
<route id="CrewOnTripHotel_1_plainxml_error">
  <from uri="internalBroker:queue:{{env:CCF_PREFIX}}from.ioservice.CrewOnTripHotel_1_plainxml.error" />
  <to uri="bean:LogMetrics?method=error" />
  <to uri="bean:FilehubReadAsStream" />
  <toD uri="msglog:CrewOnTripHotel_1_plainxml:file:{{env:INTEGRATOR_LOG_MSG_DIR}}?logAlways=true&amp;suffix=error" />
  <to uri="bean:FilehubDelete" />
</route>
```

###### 6.3.3. Rave Definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the API Hotels interfaces:

* interfaces\_core.%trip\_out\_duty\_layover\_station%: Defines duty layover station.
* interfaces\_core.%duty\_sched\_start\_utc%: Defines the scheduled duty start time in UTC, excluding briefing time if any.
* interfaces\_core.%duty\_sched\_end\_utc%: Defines the scheduled duty end time in UTC, excluding debriefing time if any.
* interfaces\_core.%next\_duty\_sched\_start\_utc%: Defines the scheduled duty start time of next duty in UTC, excluding briefing time if any.
* interfaces\_core.%next\_duty\_sched\_end\_utc%: Defines the scheduled duty end time of next duty in UTC, excluding debriefing time if any.
* interfaces\_core.%duty\_is\_first\_in\_trip%: True if duty is first in trip.
* interfaces\_core.%duty\_is\_last\_in\_trip%: True if duty is last in trip.
* interfaces\_core.%duty\_start\_station%: Defines the station at start of the duty.
* interfaces\_core.%duty\_end\_station%: Defines the station at end of the duty.
* interfaces\_core.%leg\_sched\_end\_utc%: Defines the scheduled end time of the activity in UTC.
* interfaces\_core.%leg\_end\_station%: Defines the end station of the activity.
* interfaces\_core.%next\_leg\_sched\_start\_utc%: Defines the scheduled start time of the next activity in UTC.
* interfaces\_core.%leg\_is\_sick\_transport%: True if flight is assigned for sick transport.
* interfaces\_core.%requested\_hotel\_id\_after\_duty%: If not void, provides a ‘default’ requested hotel for a layover.
* interfaces\_core.%api\_hotels\_estimated\_time\_threshold%: If not void, specifies the number of minutes estimated times must change in JCT for sending update messages to ACES.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the expected behavior of each individual airline.

###### 6.3.4. Configuration options

The interfaces have the following pre-defined configuration options. Customization is done by overriding the initializations of the associated Python class variables
according to the table below. In addition to the pre-defined options, a lot of the mapping logic is easily customized by overriding exposed methods in the
various classes of module **std\_interfaces.api\_hotels\_1**.

Confiuration options








| Interface | Option | Default value | Class | Variable | Comment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A6 | Booking status codes to ignore | PENDING CANCELLED, CANCELLED | std\_interfaces.api\_hotels.LayoverInterfaceHandler | ignore\_states | The inteface ignores reservations with these statuses. |
| A6 | Ignore unknown reservations | True | std\_interfaces.api\_hotels.LayoverInterfaceHandler | ignore\_unknown\_layovers | False means booking records are created in JCT. |
| A1,A2,A3 | Tenant | ‘AS’ | std\_interfaces.api\_hotels.HotelInterfaceHandler | tenant | Airline code reported in messages to ACES. |

###### 6.3.5. Tenant specific schemas

If the external (ACES) schemas need to be extended as part of the airline specific configuration, API Hotels should release schemas with an airline
specific target namespace, e.g. *http://ws.apihotels.com/transactions/v1/NZ/v1*.
Airline specific schemas should be placed in *$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/api\_hotels\_1/schema* using the original names (see [Schemas, services and operations](#stdif-api-hotels-schemas)).
If airline specific xslt transform stylesheets are required, they should likewise be placed in this directory under their original names.
Interfaces look for schemas and stylesheets first in this directory and if not found there they fall back to *$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/api\_hotels\_1/schema*.
The custom target namespace, as specified by the ‘targetNamespace’ attribute is automatically used by outbound interfaces when creating messages to be sent to ACES.

##### 6.4. Trouble shooting

###### 6.4.1. Error messages

All errors are logged by the IOServices with loglevel ERROR in the log file of the respective IOServer that hosts the service, e.g. errors from service
*LayoverInput* are logged in $CARMTMP/logfiles/ioserver\_single1.log. Errors reported by inbound services are generally fatal and result in discarding of the
processed message.

###### 6.4.2. Logging

In addition to error messages, there are also a number of situations where messages are logged with loglevels WARNING and INFO:

| Interface | Level | Message | Comment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A6 | INFO | Ignored reservation for non-matching layover. Trip: {ref} layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} for crew {id} | A booking from ACES doesn’t match the trip, and option *ignore\_unknown\_layovers* =True. |
| A6 | INFO | Ignored reservation for non-matching layover before or after trip: {ref} layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} for crew {id} | A booking from ACES for a layover before or after the trip doesn’t match the trip, and option [\*](#id17)ignore\_unknown\_layovers\*=True. |
| A6 | INFO | Created trip\_event for trip {ref}, non-matching layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} | A trip\_event was created for a booking from ACES that doesn’t match the trip, because option [\*](#id19)ignore\_unknown\_layovers\*=False. |
| A6 | INFO | Created trip\_event for trip {ref}, layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} | A trip\_event was created for a booking from ACES that matches the trip. |
| A6 | INFO | Created hotel\_booking for transport information related to layover night {from}-{to} for trip {ref}, multi-night layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} for crew {id} | Created a copy of the hotel\_booking record to store transport info specific to an individual layover night in a multi-night layover. |
| A6 | INFO | Removed obsolete trip\_event for trip {ref}, {layover type} layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} | Detected and rempved unused trip\_event record. |
| A2,A3 | WARNING | No duty found for crew {id} assigned to trip {ref} for duty starting with activity {ref} and ending with activity {ref} | No Rave duty was found on crew members roster that matches the trip duty chain. The interface is unable to handle any hotel overrides associated with this crew member. |
| A6 | INFO | Ignored {booking status} reservation. Trip: {ref} layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} for crew {id} | Booking from ACES ignored because booking status should be ignored according to option *ignore\_states*. |
| A6 | INFO | Created hotel\_booking for {booking status} reservation for trip {ref}, {layover type} layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} for crew {id} | Created a hotel\_booking record for a booking from ACES. |
| A6 | WARNING | Trip does not exist: dor={trip\_date} name={trip\_name} | ACES sent a booking for a trip that does not exist in JCT plan. |
| A6 | WARNING | Crew {id} not found | ACES sent a booking for a crew that does not exist in JCT plan. Booking is still processed and any existing crew are booked. |
| A6 | WARNING | Booking {before/after} trip {ref} missing forced layover event on trip level. | ACES sent a booking for a layover before/after the trip but no corresponding FORCED\_HOTEL trip\_event was found (expects layover forced on trip level since trip is in open time). Booking from ACES for this layover is ignored. |
| A6 | WARNING | Booking {before/after} trip {ref} missing forced layover event on trip or roster level | ACES sent a booking for a layover before/after the trip but no corresponding FORCED\_HOTEL trip\_event nor roster\_event was found. Booking from ACES for this layover is ignored. |
| A6 | INFO | Dayroom booking initiated by ACES for trip {ref} between ‘{act}’ and ‘{act}’ | ACES sent a booking for a dayroom and no corresponding FORCED\_HOTEL trip\_event or roster\_event was found, indicating that the reservation was initiated by a long stop booking rule in ACES. |
| A6 | INFO | Removed duplicate referenced trip\_event for trip {ref}, layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} | While looking for existing trip\_event for a booking from ACES: Identified and removed duplicate trip\_event. |
| A2,A3,A6 | INFO | Removed duplicate trip\_event for trip {ref}, layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} | Identified and removed what appeared to be an obsolete duplicate trip\_event. |
| A6 | INFO | Removed trip\_event for trip {ref}, layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} while handling orphan bookings. | While handling orphan bookings: Detected and removed trip\_event connected to an obsolete booking. |
| A6 | INFO | Created hotel\_booking clone with ‘New’ status for trip {ref}, layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id} for crew {id} | While handling a transient booking state: Created a clone of the booking and associated trip\_events with the new clone. See also [Handling of intermediate booking states](#stdif-api-hotels-intermediate-booking-states). |
| A6 | INFO | Removed trip\_event for trip {ref}, layover: {from} - {to} at {stn} hotel {id}. | While handling obsolete bookings: Detected and removed trip\_event connected to an obsolete booking. |
| A6 | INFO | Cancelled hotel\_booking for trip {ref}, layover: {from} {to} at {stn} hotel {id} for crew {id} at {stn} hotel {id} | While handling obsolete bookings: Marked obsolete hotel\_booking as cancelled. |
| A5 | WARNING | Ignoring contract for hotel with id ‘{id}’ due to invalid contract period validfrom={from}, validto={to} | Invalid hotel contract period, validto >= validfrom. |
| A5 | WARNING | Ignoring contract for hotel transport company with id ‘{id}’ due to invalid contract period validfrom={from}, validto={to}. | Invalid hotel transport company contract period, validto >= validfrom. |

##### 6.5. Use cases

###### 6.5.1. Crew on a layover split up at different hotels

This example illustrates a case where not all crew on a layover are booked at the same hotel, e.g. due to hotel availability.

Bookings are received from ACES for a trip (TRIP\_1) with two layovers:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | crew composition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24MAR2014 | TRIP\_1 | 24MAR2014 | CPH | 1FC/1AH |

containing the following activity assignments:

| flight | dep | arr | sobt | sibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | CPH | FRA | 11:00 | 13:00 |

| JJ 103 25MAR2014 | DUS | FRA | 12:00 | 14:00 |
| JJ 104 26MAR2014 | FRA | CPH | 10:00 | 12:00 |

###### 6.5.2. Splitting and slicing a trip

In this scenario a trip is split in JCT. The new trip segment is then sliced.
It demonstrates that an intermediate state of bookings is maintained by the interface until complete feedback has been received from ACES
on all the affected trip segments.

The original trip have the following activity assignments:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | crew composition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24MAR2014 | TRIP\_2 | 24MAR2014 | CPH | 1FC/1AH |

| flight / ground task | dep | arr | sobt | sibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | CPH | FRA | 11:00 | 13:00 |
| TQ 25MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 08:00 | 15:00 |
| JJ 202 25MAR2014 | FRA | DUS | 16:00 | 18:00 |
| JJ 203 26MAR2014 | DUS | CPH | 12:00 | 13:00 |

The trip has two crew members assigned in two different positions, AH and FC:

| crew.alias | name | base | assigned position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 123 | Lola Montez | CPH | AH |
| 124 | Elroy Jeppesen | CPH | FC |

Next, the trip segment ‘TRIP\_2x’ is sliced off for crew ‘124’ to a new trip slice named ‘TRIP\_2xx’.

###### 6.5.3. Forced hotel after trip

This scenario illustrates a case where a layover is forced after the trip, and the trip is in open time. In addition to just requesting a placeholder for the
extra layover, there is also a request for a specific hotel to be booked. The id of the requested hotel in this example is 222.
Note that in reality, the use case for forcing a layover after a trip is normally to keep already existing bookings in trip split scenarios. However for the sake of
simplicity, the example shown here does not involve a trip split.

Assume the following trip and activity assignments:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | crew composition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24MAR2014 | TRIP\_1 | 24MAR2014 | CPH | 1FC/1AH |

| flight | dep | arr | sobt | sibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | CPH | FRA | 11:00 | 13:00 |
| JJ 102 25MAR2014 | FRA | DUS | 09:00 | 10:00 |
| JJ 103 25MAR2014 | DUS | FRA | 12:00 | 14:00 |
| JJ 104 26MAR2014 | FRA | CPH | 10:00 | 12:00 |

Creating the forced hotel request in the Tracking Editor in JCT results in the following **trip\_event** records. The end time ‘et’ of the layover needs to be
provided when creating the request:

| trip.name | trip.dor | typ.id | st | et | station | hotel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TRIP\_1 | 20140324 | FORCED\_HOTEL | 20140326 12:00 | 20140327 08:00 | CPH |  |
| TRIP\_1 | 20140324 | HOTEL\_OVERRIDE | 20140325 14:00 | 20140327 08:00 | CPH | 222 |

###### 6.5.4. Multi-night layover

A series of ground duties at a remote station may be reported as one multi-night booking by ACES.
In this example it is demonstrated that a multi-night layover is mapped to several **trip\_event** records, one per layover,
but that there is only one **hotel\_booking** record representing the entire multi-night booking.
This illustrates a basic multi-night use case where there are only local transport bookings from airport to
the hotel on the day of arrival and from the hotel to the ground duty venue on the day of departure. There are no
additional transports from/to ground duty venues on the rest of the duty days.

The trip have the following activity assignments:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | crew composition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24MAR2014 | TRIP\_3 | 24MAR2014 | CPH | 1FC/1AH |

| flight / ground task | dep | arr | sobt | sibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | CPH | FRA | 11:00 | 13:00 |
| TQ 25MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 08:00 | 15:00 |
| TK7 25MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 16:00 | 17:00 |
| TQ 26MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 09:00 | 18:00 |
| TQ 27MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 07:00 | 16:00 |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | FRA | CPH | 19:00 | 21:00 |

The trip has two crew members assigned in two different positions, AH and FC:

| crew.alias | name | base | assigned position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 123 | Lola Montez | CPH | AH |
| 124 | Elroy Jeppesen | CPH | FC |

Bookings for the trip are received from ACES:


###### 6.5.5. Multi-night layover with multiple transports

This example demonstrates how multi-night layovers with multiple transport bookings are represented in the JCMS data model.
In addition to local transport bookings to/from the hotel on the days of arrival and departure of the multi-night layover,
in this example there are additional transports from/to ground duty venues on intermediate duty days.

Also, in this use case bookings are sent as separate hotel-reservations for each crew member because they have
different pickup times from the hotel. The layover properties and their hotel-reservations are otherwise
identical. In this case there are multiple **hotel\_booking** records created in order to correctly represent the individual
transports and pick-up times.

| TK7 25MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 16:00 | 17:00 |
| TQ 26MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 09:00 | 18:00 |
| TQ 27MAR2014 | FRA | FRA | 07:00 | 16:00 |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | FRA | CPH | 19:00 | 21:00 |

| crew.alias | name | base | assigned position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 124 | Elroy Jeppesen | CPH | FC |

### Catalog data output


This chapter describes the interface that can be used for extracting catalog data (static data) from JCMS.
Catalog data typically involves enumerations of short names or codes with specific business meaning, for example
codes used for aircraft types, activity types, bases, crew qualifications etc.

The set of codes in the catalog data, and their business meaning, are typically shared between systems exchanging information with JCMS.
Most standard interfaces either provides or requires information matching the catalog data available in JCMS.

The purpose of this interface is to provide external systems, and keep them up to date, with set of catalog data used by JCMS.
The set of catalog data is rather stable, usually loaded once initially and updated only rarely.

Latest version of this interface is 1.beta.

[Link to CatalogDataOutput\_1\_beta.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.catalog_data_output_1/CatalogDataOutput_1_beta.xsd)

[Link to CatalogDataOutput\_1\_beta.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.catalog_data_output_1/CatalogDataOutput_1_beta.wsdl)

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* getAllCatalogData
  :   Requests the full set of catalog data provided by this interface.

##### 7.1. Scope of exported data

This interface includes most, but not all, catalog data types in JCMS. See the service definition for full list of data that is exported.
The exported data is provided based on the current state of the catalog data in JCMS, including all values currently available.
The exported data doesn’t contain old, deleted values.
Some values might only be valid for a certain time period.
Such temporal values are always exported together with a validity period, and might not currently be valid.
Some airlines adds additional catalog data types in JCMS database. This interface can be configured for also exporting such airline specific catalog data.

##### 7.2. Use cases

The examples below use the plain XML service, the same use cases can be executed in the SOAP service
but then a SOAP envelope and the SoapAction header are required.

The following request is used for requesting the full set of catalog data.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<getAllCatalogDataRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CatalogDataOutput/v1.beta" version="1.beta" source="DailyTrigger" created="2020-06-25T09:31:54Z" />
```

All catalog data provided by this interface is included in the response:

The following request is used for requesting the set of catalog data, limited to specific time period.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<getAllCatalogDataRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CatalogDataOutput/v1.beta" version="1.beta" source="DailyTrigger" created="2020-06-25T09:31:54Z"
    periodStart="2012-01-01T00:00:00Z" periodEnd="2012-06-01T00:00:00"/>
```

### Crew Check-in service


This chapter describes the JCMS standard interface for crew member check-in. The service is typically available through
some back-end application where crew members are logged in and authenticated. The back-end application establishes a
session with the JCMS *Integrator* and performs the check-in on behalf of the crew member. The back-end application
itself is not provided by JCMS but is part of a customer solution based on e.g. a smart phone/tablet application or
card reader terminals.

The Crew Check-in is an on-line service. This means that any check-in request is assumed to be issued in conjunction
with the actual duty that the crew member is about to perform. As a consequence, the Crew Check-in service cannot be
used e.g. in a post operational step to register check-in events to the JCMS system in retrospect.

In the JCMS system context, the Crew Check-in standard interface is a complement to the check-in service available
in Crew Access. In a specific implementation project it may be decided to use this service, the Crew Access
check-in service or a combination of both, depending on the business processes and systems infrastructure available
with the actual airline. In addition to these services there is also a check-in feature available to trackers for
assisted check-in through the JCMS Crew Tracking user interface. Using this feature, a tracker may register a check-in
event on behalf of any crew member at any time.

##### 8.1. Interface capabilities

The Crew Check-in standard interface supports the following operations:

* checkIn
  :   A request to check-in one crew member to a trip. The request always contains the Id of the crew member and a UTC
      timestamp when the operation was registered at the client terminal/system. It may also contain an optional airport where
      the check-in was taking place. JCMS records the check-in event and returns a response message containing the following
      information:

      + returnCode with success/fail status of the checkIn operation (result of operation: 0=check-in OK, -1=already checked in,
        1=check-in failed)
      + checkInStatus with the crew member’s check-in status after the operation is processed (0=not checked-in, 1=checked in,
        2=checked in (assisted))
      + a list of unacknowledged notifications that the crew member may have at the time of check-in
      + the identity of the trip to which the crew member checks in
      + the identity of the first activity of the trip to which the crew member checks in

      The JCMS standard version of the checkIn operation first checks the feasibility of the check-in by verifying
      that the check-in timestamp is inside a valid time window. The valid check-in time window is defined by business rules
      in Rave and may differ between cockpit and cabin crew. If validation fails, a description of the reason for failure is also
      provided in the response message.
* checkInWithoutValidation
  :   Identical to the ‘checkIn’ operation but without the feasibility checking. Be aware if using this operation that
      feasibility checking should instead be implemented on the back-end/client side. At least a validation of the check-in
      time window must be implemented and be in accordance with tracking rules in JCMS.
* getNotifications
  :   Delivers a list of all unacknowledged notifications for the crew member.
* acknowledgeNotifications
  :   A request to acknowledge all unacknowledged notifications for the crew member, if any.

The current version of this interface is 2.

[Link to CrewCheckIn\_2.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.crew_checkin_2/CrewCheckIn_2.xsd)

[Link to CrewCheckIn\_2.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.crew_checkin_2/CrewCheckIn_2.wsdl)

Previous versions of this interface is 1.0.

[Link to CrewCheckIn\_1\_0.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.crew_checkin_1_0/CrewCheckIn_1_0.xsd)

[Link to CrewCheckInSoap\_1\_0.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.crew_checkin_1_0/CrewCheckInSoap_1_0.wsdl)

###### 8.1.1. Context for check-in

In the standard version of the checkIn operation, the only check done by the system is that check-in is done
within an accepted time frame. No other legality checks are performed as prerequisites for the check-in operation
to succeed. Nor is it checked that the activity to which the crew member checks in actually requires checking in,
or that the role to which he/she is assigned is eligible for check-in. The standard behavior is to look up
the next trip on the crew members roster and verify the accepted check-in time window against the start time
of that trip. Note that check of accepted check-in time window is not performed if using the checkInWithoutValidation
operation.

As for all standard interfaces, the Crew Check-in service is designed to be highly customizable. In particular,
the feasibility check of the checkIn operation is exposed as a Python function that can easily be overridden
and implement any airline specific business level checks and validations. If the validation function returns
a negative result, then the checkIn operation fails.

###### 8.1.2. Session handling

A session consistency mechanism is used in JCMS to synchronize the getNotifications and acknowledgeNotifications
operations in order to guarantee that only those notifications are acknowledged that the crew member has
actually seen.

This mechanism utilizes a *jcms\_state* reference header attached to the request message. When set, the IOServer
will make sure that the sub-process that handles the request is based on at least that referenced state (i.e.
the same state or a newer one). The given state is also used as reference point for conflict detection
when storing the acknowledgments to the data model. A data entity level conflict trigger will then cause the
operation to fail if the crew member has more recent notifications in the current state compared to the
ones he/she has viewed. The *jcms\_state* header is set by the IOServer on the getNotifications response
message to the state upon which that operation was based. The same state reference must then follow the
acknowledgeNotifications request message.

There are basically two ways to ensure that the correct *jcms\_state*
reference is attached to the acknowledgeNotifications request. Either the back-end application handles the
state reference or it is handled by the JCMS *Integrator*.

**Session handling using integrator**

The built-in support in JCMS *Integrator* for handling
state references can only be used in cases where the front-end client only handles one crew member
per session. Each client must authenticate it self, i.e. by logging in using the crew member ID to initiate the session.

![../_images/crew_check_in_integrator_sessions.png](../_images/crew_check_in_integrator_sessions.png)

**Session handling using back-end client**

If instead the back-end application handles requests on behalf of many crew members, and using a
stateless session for the communication with JCMS, then the back-end application itself must handle the *jcms\_state*
references for each front-end client. In this case it is required that acknowledgeNotifications request for a crew member
contains the *jcms\_state* reference previously received in the getNotifications response for that crew member,
i.e. the back-end application must handle *jcms\_state* references separately per crew member.
Also note that the conflict trigger mentioned above is not included in
the standard JCMS data model but must be added as part of a CARMUSR implementation.

![../_images/crew_check_in_back_end_sessions.png](../_images/crew_check_in_back_end_sessions.png)

In the standard version of the Crew Check-in service, no synchronization is required between acknowledgeNotifications
and checkIn though because check-in should succeed regardless if there are unacknowledged notifications.
For that reason, the conflict trigger mentioned above is not active when saving the result of the checkIn
operation.
One way to enforce acknowledgement before check-in, is simply that the back-end application never sends
a checkIn request before receiving the response from a successful acknowledgeNotifications operation. Also,
the registered check-in timestamp should be set to the time of the acknowledgeNotifications request or
earlier, e.g. the time when the crew member logged in to the back-end application.

###### 8.1.3. Supported protocols

The interface supports requests using SOAP or plain xml. The service itself doesn’t implement the actual communication
protocol. As a part of a customer solution it typically relies on the JEE based *Integrator* to expose the
service over HTTP.

##### 8.2. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Crew Check-in standard interface:

* interfaces\_core.%start\_of\_check\_in\_time\_window\_utc%
* interfaces\_core.%end\_of\_check\_in\_time\_window\_utc%
* interfaces\_core.%leg\_requires\_check\_in%
* interfaces\_core.%crew\_is\_checked\_in%
* interfaces\_core.%crew\_checked\_in\_time%
* interfaces\_core.%is\_assisted\_check\_in%

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline. Note that the *start\_of\_check\_in\_time\_window\_utc* is per
definition included in the valid check-in time window whereas the *end\_of\_check\_in\_time\_window\_utc*
is excluded.

##### 8.3. Error Handling

When a checkIn operation fails due to a validation error, an ordinary checkInResponse message is returned
but with returnCode set to 1, and the errorDescription field containing detailed information about the
actual validation error. In the standard Crew Check-in interface, the only validation that is actually
carried out is to check that the check-in timestamp is inside a valid time window.

All other kinds of errors will result in an error message (of type *ServiceError*). See following
sub-sections for details.

###### 8.3.1. Check-in validation errors

| Error | Response message type | returnCode | errorDescription |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Check-in too early | CheckInResponseMsg | 1 | Check-in time ‘DDMONYYYY hh:MM’ is outside valid time window (DDMONYYYY hh:MM - DDMONYYYY hh:MM) |
| Check-in too late | CheckInResponseMsg | 1 | Check-in time ‘DDMONYYYY hh:MM’ is outside valid time window (DDMONYYYY hh:MM - DDMONYYYY hh:MM) |
| Check-in trip not found (version 2 only) | CheckInResponseMsg | 1 | Cannot find activity to check in to |

###### 8.3.2. Other errors

| Error | Response message type | code | subCode | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Crew member not found | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | CrewCheckInHandler, could not find any Crewmember with key ‘(‘XXXXXX’,)’ |
| Check-in trip not found (version 1.0 only) | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectNotFound | CrewCheckInHandler: Cannot find activity to check in to for crew member ‘XXXXXX’ |
| Invalid airport specified at check-in | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | airport, could not find any Airport with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| New notification have been created for the crew member after getNotificationsRequest was sent but before acknowledgeNotificationsRequest was sent | ServiceError | TransientMessageError | DatabaseConflictError | 0: Ioserver error. IOSError: Problem saving the plan. N4dave12conflict\_errE: CONFLICT\_ERR: Conflict detected for as\_crw\_not (id: <some uuid>, <etc…>) |

##### 8.4. Detailed use cases

###### 8.4.1. Acknowledge notifications for crew member and verify

Client sends initial getNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the initial request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=0*.

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<SOAP:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2" xmlns:jaxb="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/jaxb" xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/" xmlns:SOAP="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <SOAP:Body>	
		<ns1:getNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" crewId="12345A" source="BB" version="2"/>	
	</SOAP:Body>
</SOAP:Envelope>
```

Service responds with three notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains *jcms\_state=325*.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2">
  <soap:Body>
    <getNotificationsResponse version="2" source="CrewCheckIn" crewId="12345A">
      <notification startTime="2016-01-01T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-02T00:00:00Z" type="AAA" text="not 1"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-05T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-10T00:00:00Z" type="BBB" text="not 2"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" type="CCC" text="not 3"/>
    </getNotificationsResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Client sends acknowledgeNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A. The client must set
*jcms\_state* to the value received in the getNotificationsResponse for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=325*, this guarantees that only
the three notifications previously received for this crew member are acknowledged.

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<SOAP:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2" xmlns:jaxb="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/jaxb" xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/" xmlns:SOAP="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <SOAP:Body>	
		<ns1:acknowledgeNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" crewId="12345A" source="BB" version="2"/>
	</SOAP:Body>
</SOAP:Envelope>
```

Service responds with three acknowledged notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains *jcms\_state=331*.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2">
  <soap:Body>
    <acknowledgeNotificationsResponse version="2" source="CrewCheckIn" crewId="12345A">
      <notification startTime="2016-01-01T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-02T00:00:00Z" type="AAA" text="not 1"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-05T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-10T00:00:00Z" type="BBB" text="not 2"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" type="CCC" text="not 3"/>
    </acknowledgeNotificationsResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Client sends a second getNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A to verify the acknowledged
notifications.
The HTTP header of the initial request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=0*.

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<SOAP:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2" xmlns:jaxb="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/jaxb" xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/" xmlns:SOAP="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <SOAP:Body>	
		<ns1:getNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" crewId="12345A" source="BB" version="2"/>	
	</SOAP:Body>
</SOAP:Envelope>
```

Service responds with empty getNotificationsResponse for crew member 12345A.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>
<SOAP:Envelope xmlns:tns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2" xmlns:jaxb="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/jaxb"
	xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"
	xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/" xmlns:SOAP="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
	<SOAP:Body>
		<tns:getNotificationsResponse version="2" source="CrewCheckIn" created="2016-01-25T12:42:12Z"
			crewId="12345A"/>
	</SOAP:Body>
</SOAP:Envelope>
```

###### 8.4.2. Acknowledge notifications for crew member and check in crew member

Client sends initial getNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the initial request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=0*.

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<SOAP:Envelope xmlns:tns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2" xmlns:jaxb="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/jaxb" xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/" xmlns:SOAP="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <SOAP:Body>
		<ns1:getNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" crewId="12345A" source="BB" version="2" xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2"/>
	</SOAP:Body>
</SOAP:Envelope>
```

Service responds with three notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains *jcms\_state=325*.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2">
  <soap:Body>
    <getNotificationsResponse version="2" source="CrewCheckIn" crewId="12345A">
      <notification startTime="2016-01-01T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-02T00:00:00Z" type="AAA" text="not 1"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-05T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-10T00:00:00Z" type="BBB" text="not 2"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" type="CCC" text="not 3"/>
    </getNotificationsResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Client sends acknowledgeNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A. The client must set
*jcms\_state* to the value received in the getNotificationsResponse for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=325*, this guarantees that only
the three notifications previously received for this crew member are acknowledged.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>
<SOAP:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2" xmlns:jaxb="http://java.sun.com/xml/ns/jaxb" xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/" xmlns:SOAP="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <SOAP:Body>	
		<ns1:acknowledgeNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" crewId="12345A" source="BB" version="2"/>
	</SOAP:Body>
</SOAP:Envelope>

	
```

Service responds with three acknowledged notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains *jcms\_state=331*.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2">
  <soap:Body>
    <acknowledgeNotificationsResponse version="2" source="CrewCheckIn" crewId="12345A">
      <notification startTime="2016-01-01T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-02T00:00:00Z" type="AAA" text="not 1"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-05T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-10T00:00:00Z" type="BBB" text="not 2"/>
      <notification startTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" endTime="2016-01-15T00:00:00Z" type="CCC" text="not 3"/>
    </acknowledgeNotificationsResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Client sends checkInRequest specifying the check in time for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the check in request should contain *jcms\_state=0* since this operation
doesn’t depend on previous operations for the crew member.

```
    </SOAP:Body>
</SOAP:Envelope>
```

Service responds with checkInResponse, checkInStatus=1 (checked in), returnCode=0 check in time for crew member 12345A

###### 8.4.4. Acknowledge notifications for crew member fails due to database conflict

Client sends initial getNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the initial request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=0*.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2"
  xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <ns1:getNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00"
      crewId="12345A" source="CheckInClient" version="2" />
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Service responds with two notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains *jcms\_state=125*.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2">
  <soap:Body>
    <getNotificationsResponse version="2" source="CrewCheckIn" crewId="12345A">
      <notification startTime="2015-09-17T07:01:00Z" endTime="2015-09-18T06:59:00Z" type="DEASSIGNED_ACTIVITY" text="Deassigned activity Reserve Off Duty - 1 day, 17SEP 00:01 - 23:59"/>
      <notification startTime="2015-09-17T15:16:00Z" endTime="2015-09-19T13:51:00Z" type="ASSIGNED_TRIP" text="Assigned trip 000008 - 3 days, 17SEP 08:16 - 19SEP 06:51"/>
    </getNotificationsResponse>
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Client sends acknowledgeNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A. The client must set
*jcms\_state* to the value received in the getNotificationsResponse for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=125*, this guarantees that only
the two notifications previously received for this crew member are acknowledged.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2"
  xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <ns1:acknowledgeNotificationsRequest
      created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" crewId="12345A" source="CheckInClient"
      version="2" />
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Service responds with a database conflict error for crew member 12345A. This error response indicates that
there are new notifications that the crew member has not yet seen and the acknowledgement operations was aborted.
This type of error response, with **subcode=DatabaseConflictError**, is returned when new notification
have been created for the crew member after getNotificationsRequest was sent but before acknowledgeNotificationsRequest
was sent.
The HTTP header of the error response for this crew member contains *jcms\_state=131*.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<ns1:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:ns2="http://crew_checkin_soap_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
 <ns1:Body>
  <ns1:Fault>
   <faultcode>
    SOAP:Server
   </faultcode>
   <faultstring>
        Server Error
   </faultstring>
   <detail>
    <ns2:error code="TransientMessageError" created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" requestId="1" source="CrewCheckInSoap" subcode="DatabaseConflictError" version="1.0">
     <reason>
            0: IOServer database conflict error. DatabaseConflictError: PlanHolderMave2Impl failed to save plan. Reason: dave::conflict_err:  CONFLICT_ERR:  Conflict detected for as_crw_not (id: O/qN6YW5QgyrLfw6gtWuiQ==, period_start: 10851, branchid: 1).
     </reason>
     <sourceMessage>
      <ns2:acknowledgeNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00" crewId="12345A" source="CheckInClient" version="1.0"/>
     </sourceMessage>
    </ns2:error>
   </detail>
  </ns1:Fault>
 </ns1:Body>
</ns1:Envelope>
```

In order to resolve the error, we must start over by sending a new getNotificationsRequest.
The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=131*, this guarantees that the response
contains the new notifications which caused the conflict error.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewCheckIn/v2"
  xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
  <soap:Body>
    <ns1:getNotificationsRequest created="2015-01-01T00:00:00"
      crewId="12345A" source="CheckInClient" version="2" />
  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Service responds with three notifications for crew member 12345A.
The HTTP header of the response for this crew member contains *jcms\_state=134*.

```

      <notification startTime="2015-09-17T07:01:00Z" endTime="2015-09-18T06:59:00Z" type="DEASSIGNED_ACTIVITY" text="Deassigned activity Reserve Off Duty - 1 day, 17SEP 00:01 - 23:59"/>
      <notification startTime="2015-09-17T15:16:00Z" endTime="2015-09-19T13:51:00Z" type="ASSIGNED_TRIP" text="Assigned trip 000008 - 3 days, 17SEP 08:16 - 19SEP 06:51"/>
      <notification startTime="2015-09-17T20:35:00Z" endTime="2015-09-17T21:03:00Z" type="POSITION" text="Changed flight YY123: assignment DH (FA)"/>

  </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

Client sends acknowledgeNotificationsRequest for crew member 12345A. The client must set

The HTTP header of the request for this crew member must contain *jcms\_state=134*, this guarantees that only
the three notifications previously received are acknowledged.

```
      <notification startTime="2015-09-17T15:16:00Z" endTime="2015-09-19T13:51:00Z" type="ASSIGNED_TRIP" text="Assigned trip 000008 - 3 days, 17SEP 08:16 - 19SEP 06:51"/>
```
