### Crew Messages service


This chapter describes the Crew Messages standard interface. It is used internally in JCMS
when sending messages to crew members over various communication channels such as email or SMS. The service
itself doesn’t implement the actual communication protocol sending the messages to crew. Instead it relies on some communication gateway as
part of a specific customer solution. Such a gateway may be an external system or a Camel route
in the *Integrator*, depending on customer solution.
External systems can also use this service for providing information about crew messages that has been sent, for example indicating
that a specific message has been read by a crew member.

In JCMS, two typical use cases exist for the Crew Message service:

* As soon as there is a new crew roster change notification, the system sends a message to the crew member
  if he/she has agreed to subscribe to such notifications. The message informs crew to log in to Crew Access
  to view the actual changes to the roster. This feature requires a trigger service to be
  configured inside JCMS. The trigger needs to react on new publication notification items in the data model
  and send corresponding request messages to the Crew Messages service. Such triggers are not provided out
  of the box by the standard interface but must be added as part of the customer project implementation.
* Tracker free text messages to crew members.

The receiving gateway may distinguish different use cases by looking at a special `source` attribute
in the output message. The content of the `source` attribute is copied from that of the request message.
Therefore, all output messages are typically sent to the same queue although other routing solutions can
be configured for specific customer implementations.

The current version of this interface is 3.

[Link to CrewMessages\_3.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.crew_messages_3/CrewMessages_3.xsd)

Previous versions of this interface

[Link to CrewMessages\_2\_0.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.crew_output_2_0/CrewMessages_2_0.xsd)

##### 11.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

* generateCrewMessages
  :   Used internally by JCMS for sending messages for one or more crew members. For each message, zero or
      more `channelTypes` may be specified. The `channelTypes` are identical to the crew contact types defined
      as base data in the JCMS data model, ‘email’ and ‘phone’ are typical examples of contact types.
      For each `channelType` the service looks up the actual crew contact address for the corresponding
      contact type and inserts it into the output message. If the crew member has more than one contact
      of the specified type, then the one with highest priority (lowest priority number) is selected.
* updateCrewMessages
  :   Used by external systems to provide information about crew messages that has been sent, for example indicating
      that a specific message has been read by a crew member.

###### 11.1.1. Content of the output message

One output message is produced per request to generateCrewMessages operation. The structure of the produced output message is the same as the request,
i.e. it may contain several crew members and more than one CrewMessage structure per crew member. In analogy
with the request, each CrewMessage can also specify more than one destination `channel`.
The following fields are included in the CrewMessage structure:

* `subject` (optional). Copied from request. Not applicable for some channel types like land line or mobile
  phones.
* `body` If body is missing in the request, `<UNDEFINED MESSAGE>` is used as output.
* messageId (optional). Copied from request. Should be used
* `channel` (optional). If no ‘channelType’ is specified in the request then the receiving gateway is
  assumed to know where to send the crew message. The channel consists of the following sub-elements:
  + `type`. Copied from `channelType` in the request.
  + `contact`. The actual contact as looked up by the service, e.g. email address or phone number.

As already mentioned above the `source` attribute on the root element of the output message is copied
from the request message in order to identify the origin of the message. There exists two pre-defined
sources in JCMS corresponding to the two typical use cases described above: `Access` for the roster
change notifications and `JCMS` for tracker free text messages.

###### 11.1.2. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most interfaces, i.e. to reject a request message
if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. Concretely for the Crew Messages service it means that if
it fails processing any part of a request, an error message is generated and the entire request is discarded.
The following errors can occur when processing a request:

* Crew member not found. A crew member with the specified alias doesn’t exist.
* Specified ‘channelType’ does not exist as contact type in JCMS base data.
* Unknown contact address. Crew member doesn’t have any contact of the specified type.

Note that the ‘source’ attribute of the error message is always set to the service name, ‘CrewMessages’.
However, the origin can be identified through the request message which is also enclosed in the error
message.

##### 11.2. Use cases

In this example a message is sent to two crew members with individual sets of channels.
The `generateCrewMessagesRequest` below is used internally in JCMS when sending messages to crew.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<generateCrewMessagesRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewMessages/v3" version="3" source="JCMS" created="2021-05-03T15:43:32Z">
  <messageParameters crewId="222222" messageId="80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb">
    <subject>Test 1</subject>
    <body>Hello, this is a test.</body>
    <channelType>email</channelType>
    <channelType>phone</channelType>
  </messageParameters>
  <messageParameters crewId="333333" messageId="80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb">
    <subject>Test 1</subject>
    <body>Hello, this is a test.</body>
    <channelType>email</channelType>
    <channelType>mobile</channelType>
  </messageParameters>
</generateCrewMessagesRequest>
```

this leads to the following `sendCrewMessages` output message.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<sendCrewMessages xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewMessages/v3" version="3" source="JCMS">
  <message crewId="222222" messageId="80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb">
    <subject>Test 1</subject>
    <body>Hello, this is a test.</body>
    <channel type="email" contact="some.address@example.com"/>
  </message>
  <message crewId="333333" messageId="80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb">
    <subject>Test 1</subject>
    <body>Hello, this is a test.</body>
    <channel type="email" contact="another.address@somehere.com"/>
    <channel type="mobile" contact="3456789"/>
  </message>
</sendCrewMessages>
```

The output message above is forwarded to some communication gateway that is responsible for sending actual messages to crew using
appropriate communication channels.
The communication gateway and other external systems can also provide feedback to JCMS on messages that has been sent, by using the `updateCrewMessages` request.
The example message below can be sent to indicate what crew members that actually received and read the sent messages.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<updateCrewMessagesRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewMessages/v3" version="3" source="External system" created="2021-05-03T14:26:23Z">
    <messageStatus crewId="222222" messageId="80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb" isRead="true"/>
    <messageStatus crewId="333333" messageId="80048064-fbcf-4e25-be5b-a48ac8eee1cb" isRead="false"/>
</updateCrewMessagesRequest>
```

##### 11.3. IOService builder configuration

Service CrewMessages version 3

```
<smog-service name="CrewMessages" version="3" protocol="plainxml">
  <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_messages_3/services.xml"/>
  <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_messages_3/protocol.xml"/>
  <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_messages_3/mapping.xml"/>
</smog-service>
```

### Crew On Flight


This chapter describes the interface that can be used to get flight and related crew information from JCMS.
The flight and crew information is normally sent when explicitly requested by an external user or system
(request/response pattern). The information can also be published to external systems by JCMS, either triggered by database changes or
on a scheduled basis (publish/subscribe pattern). The latter requires however a service trigger to be
configured inside JCMS. Such triggers are not provided out of the box by the standard interface but must
be added as part of an implementation project. In addition, it is also possible, as a part of
implementation project customization, to add mechanisms to enable e.g. a Tracking user to manually request
crew list information to be sent out to predefined destinations.

The current version of this interface is 4

[Link to CrewOnFlight\_4.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/CrewOnFlight_4.xsd)

[Link to CrewOnFlight\_4.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/CrewOnFlight_4.wsdl)

Previous versions of this interface

[Link to CrewOnFlight\_3\_1.xsd (version 3.1)](contract/std_interfaces.flight_output_3_1/CrewOnFlight_3_1.xsd)

[Link to CrewOnFlightSoap\_3\_1.wsdl (version 3.1)](contract/std_interfaces.flight_output_3_1/CrewOnFlightSoap_3_1.wsdl)

##### 12.1. Interface capabilities

The interface supports three operations:

* The operation “ping” pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* The operation “crewOnFlight” delivers the list of crew members that are assigned to the flights
  matching the given criteria of the request.
* The operation “getFlightSummary” delivers the information about the flights matching the request along with a
  summary, e.g. number of crew on the flight along with other information. The response doesn’t provide information about specific crew members.

###### 12.1.1. Scope and content of returned crew list

A request must contain a date range (startDate and endDate), specifying the dateOfOrigin (udor) of the requested flights.
Other fields in the request (flightNumber, startStation, etc.) are optional, but can be used for specifying more details about the flights that should be returned.
The response contains all (non-deleted) flight leg instances with a dateOfOrigin in the date range that matches the values of the request, including return-to-ramp and wait-at-gate events.
The request should use same date as startDate and endDate when requesting information for flights on a specific dateOfOrigin.

###### 12.1.2. Rave Definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Crew On Flight interface:

* interfaces\_core.%cof\_min\_connection\_time%: Minimum connection time needed by crewmember for next flight.
* interfaces\_core.%cof\_leg\_crew\_competences%: Comma separated string containing all relevant competences for a crew member on this flight. Empty string if crew member has no relevant competences or void if competences should not be communicated for a crew member.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the expected behavior of each individual airline.

###### 12.1.3. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most interfaces, i.e. to reject the message
if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. Concretely for the CrewOnFlight interface it
means e.g. that if it fails to find or process any of the flights or crew matching a “crewOnFlight” request, it
will respond with an error message.

##### 12.2. Use cases

The examples below all use the plain XML service, the same use cases can be executed in the SOAP service
but then a SOAP envelope and the SoapAction header are required.

Request a single flight, identified by (startDate, carrier, flightNumber, startStation and endStation).

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<crewOnFlightRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewOnFlight/v4" version="4" created="2014-08-30T12:00:00" source="TEST" startDate="2014-03-24" endDate="2014-03-24" flightNumber="101" carrier="JJ" startStation="MUC" endStation="CPH"/>
```

this will lead to an output like the following

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<crewOnFlightResponse xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewOnFlight/v4" version="4" source="CrewOnFlight">
  <flight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24" flightNumber="101" startStation="MUC" endStation="CPH" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-24T07:13:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-24T08:55:00Z" startTimeOffset="PT1H" endTimeOffset="PT1H" seqNumber="1" operationalStatus="S" scheduleStatus="N">
    <assignedCrew>
      <crew crewId="123" position="AH" deadheadInd="false" surName="Montez" givenName="Lola">
        <trip name="humbug" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24"/>
        <minorAddition>
          <nextActivity minConnectionTime="PT30M">
            <leg dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24" carrier="JJ" flightNumber="101" startStation="CPH" endStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-24T09:30:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-24T11:05:00Z"/>
          </nextActivity>
        </minorAddition>
      </crew>
      <crew crewId="124" position="FC" deadheadInd="false" surName="Jeppesen" givenName="Elroy">
        <trip name="humbug" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24"/>
        <minorAddition>
          <nextActivity minConnectionTime="PT30M">
            <leg dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24" carrier="JJ" flightNumber="101" startStation="CPH" endStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-24T09:30:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-24T11:05:00Z"/>
          </nextActivity>
        </minorAddition>
      </crew>
    </assignedCrew>
  </flight>
</crewOnFlightResponse>
```


this will lead to an output like the following

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<crewOnFlightResponse xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewOnFlight/v4" version="4" source="CrewOnFlight">
  <flight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-25" flightNumber="202" startStation="GOT" endStation="MUC" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-25T12:40:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-25T14:55:00Z" startTimeOffset="PT1H" endTimeOffset="PT1H" seqNumber="1" operationalStatus="S" scheduleStatus="N">
    <assignedCrew/>
  </flight>
  <flight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-25" flightNumber="303" startStation="GOT" endStation="MUC" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-25T22:40:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-26T00:55:00Z" startTimeOffset="PT1H" endTimeOffset="PT1H" seqNumber="1" operationalStatus="S" scheduleStatus="N">
    <assignedCrew/>
  </flight>
  <flight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-25" flightNumber="303" suffix="A" startStation="GOT" endStation="MUC" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-25T12:40:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-25T14:55:00Z" startTimeOffset="PT1H" endTimeOffset="PT1H" seqNumber="1" operationalStatus="S" scheduleStatus="N">
    <assignedCrew/>
  </flight>
</crewOnFlightResponse>
```

### Crew On Flight import to JOC


This chapter describes the interface that can be used for importing crew flight connections into an Ops Control (JOC) system.

The current version of this interface is 4

[Link to CrewOnFlightJOC\_4.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/CrewOnFlightJOC_4.xsd)

[Link to CrewOnFlightJOC\_4.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/CrewOnFlightJOC_4.wsdl)

##### 13.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* updateCrewOnFlight
  :   The operation “updateCrewOnFlight” creates and updates crew assignment and connection information for JOC.

The purpose of the CrewOnFlightJOC service is for a JOC system to import flight crew assignments and connections from JCT or
a third party Crew Tracking system. It takes as input the same message structure as produced by the ordinary CrewOnFlight service
(struct CrewOnFlightResponse), although only a subset is actually imported and used by JOC.

The following records or sub-structures are not used by JOC:

* **annotation** - annotations to crew for a flight leg
* **passengers** - number of passengers booked on the flight leg
* **aircraft** - the aircraft assigned to the flight leg
* **trainingTag** - set of tags to indicate training characteristics of the flight leg if used for training
* **trip** - the trip to which crew is assigned
* **nextActivity** - only next connecting flight leg is used by JOC, next activities of type groundTransport or groundTasks are ignored.

The crew assignments and relevant qualifications (a.k.a. crew competences) for a flight is imported as a state,
i.e. the interface expects all assigned crew members to be included, and for each crew member all qualifications for that flight leg to be listed.

For `nextActivity`, the flight number of the leg must be specified as a minimum. A fuzzy search is conducted trying
to identify the best-match flight leg. With more information provided, the match accuracy increases.

* It’s strongly recommended to provide `scheduledStartTime` for the next flight leg, especially when the depature time of the current flight leg
  is approaching. In this case, the search allows connection to go **backwards** within **allowed deviation** from the provided start time.
  Otherwise, it assumes that the best known departure time of next flight leg must be after the best known arrival time of the current flight leg.
* If neither `startStation` nor `scheduledStartTime` is provided for the next flight leg, and the next flight leg belongs to a multi-leg flight,
  the matching logic assumes that the start station of the next flight leg must match the end station of the current flight leg.
  Therefore, it’s recommended to provide `startStation` of the next flight leg for co-terminal scenarios.

The **allowed deviation** is configurable by setting value for `scheduledTimesMatchSlack` of `RequestHolder` class.
The default value is `60` mins.

Example: to change allowed deviation to `90` mins

```
<!-- use custom service-mapping for CrewOnFlightJOC in ioservice_builder.xml -->
<ioservice pattern="subscriber">
  <description>Create/Update crew connections and qualifications.</description>
  <smog-service name="CrewOnFlightJOC" version="4" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.ext/mapping_joc.xml"/>
  </smog-service>
</ioservice>
```

```
<!-- use a different "common" module in .../std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.ext/mapping_joc.xml -->
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" language="Python" target="air2_mave2">
  <include href="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping_joc.xml"/>

  <input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightResponse">
    <import alias="common" name="datafeeds.crew_on_flight_4.crew_on_flight_helper"/>
  </input-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

```
#### set value for RequestHolder.scheduledTimesMatchSlack in crew_on_flight_helper.py
from std_interfaces.common import RequestHolder as core_request_holder


class RequestHolder(core_request_holder):

    scheduledTimesMatchSlack = 90
```

###### 13.1.1. Identification of flight legs

When looking up a leg for processing the interface uses all the provided flight and leg key elements. If dateOfOrigin is not provided,
a best match is performed based on the scheduled start and end stations and times. The scheduled times are allowed to deviate from those
stored in JCMS in accordance with the `scheduledTimesMatchSlack` parameter as explained earlier. If no matching leg is found an error
message is logged but processing of other flights in the message continues.

###### 13.1.2. Error handling

If the interface encounters a flight leg that it cannot identify in the JOC data model it skips that flight record with a log error
message and continues processing the next flight record in the message. If a connecting flight (next leg) cannot be identified based
on the specified properties, then that crew connection is skipped with a warning message. If some other part of the connection information,
e.g. the specified crew position or a crew competence type, then the crew connection is still stored but without that piece of information.
A warning log message is also issued. If a crew member cannot be identified by it’s crewId, the interface creates the crew member ad hoc
in the JOC data model using the specified surname and given name, if available.

##### 13.2. Use cases

The examples below all use the plain XML service, the same use cases can be executed in the SOAP service
but then a SOAP envelope and the SoapAction header are required.

The example below illustrates the usage of the client implementation for importing flight crew connection information into JOC.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<crewOnFlightResponse xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/CrewOnFlightJOC/v4" version="4" source="AIMS" created="2014-03-25T07:10:45Z">
  <flight carrier="JP" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-25" flightNumber="942" startStation="CCU" endStation="BLR" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-25T06:15:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-25T08:15:00Z">
    <assignedCrew>
      <crew crewId="12345" position="FC">
        <minorAddition>
          <!-- provide all qualifications relevant in JOC for this crew member -->
          <qualifications>
            <qualName>LVTO</qualName>
            <qualName>ILS-CAT3</qualName>
          </qualifications>
          <!-- only provide next connecting flight leg of crew member if it's within same duty -->
          <nextActivity minConnectionTime="PT45M">
            <leg flightNumber="435" />
          </nextActivity>
        </minorAddition>
      </crew>
      <crew crewId="54321" position="AH">
        <minorAddition>
          <!-- provide empty <qualifications> element if there are no relevant qualifications for this crew member -->
          <qualifications />
          <!-- only provide next connecting flight leg of crew member if it's within same duty -->
          <nextActivity minConnectionTime="PT45M">
            <leg flightNumber="123" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-26T10:00:00Z"/>
          </nextActivity>
        </minorAddition>
      </crew>
    </assignedCrew>
  </flight>
</crewOnFlightResponse>
```

The following records are stored in the JOC data model as a result of processing the message:

*Crew flight Assignments*
:   | crew.alias | leg.FlightNumber | role.Id |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | ‘12345’ | ‘435’ | ‘FC’ |
    | ‘12345’ | ‘942’ | ‘FC’ |
    | ‘54321’ | ‘123’ | ‘AH’ |
    | ‘54321’ | ‘942’ | ‘AH’ |

*Flight Crew Competences*
:   | crew.alias | leg.FlightNumber | typ.id |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | ‘12345’ | ‘942’ | ‘ILS-CAT3’ |
    | ‘12345’ | ‘942’ | ‘LVTO’ |

*Flight Crew Connections*
:   | crew.alias | prev\_leg.num | next\_leg.num | min\_conn\_time |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | ‘12345’ | ‘942’ | ‘435’ | ‘0:45’ |
    | ‘54321’ | ‘942’ | ‘123’ | ‘0:45’ |

##### 13.3. Configuration

For information on how to configure JCT to produce messages for CrewOnFlightJOC, please refer to chapter [Crew On Flight Events](crew_on_flight_events.html#stdif-crew-on-flight-updates).

```
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping_joc.xml"/>
  </smog-service>
</ioservice>
```

### Crew On Flight Events


This chapter describes the standard interface for publishing crew on flight information
to external systems when changes to these assignments occur in JCMS.
Crew On Flight messages are published by the interface
when crew flight assignment information is updated in the JCMS database.
For details about the native format, please refer to the Crew On Flight interface
(see [Crew On Flight](crew_on_flight.html#stdif-crew-on-flight)).

This interface utilizes the message receivers pattern (see [Message Receivers](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-receivers-pattern))
to enable configuration of different logical receivers with different format expectations,
and the Subscription Management pattern (see [Message Receivers](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-receivers-pattern)) to
enable runtime configuration of the subscription filter.
The default receiver is the *CrewOnFlightFormatter* which supports splitting the
message per flight. The following separate receivers can be configured to produce
event messages for CrewOnFlightJOC and AOCMessageCrew services. The CrewOnFlightJOC
using the *CrewOnFlightFormatterJOC* and AOCMessageCrew using the *AOCMessageFormatter\_Crew*.
The CrewOnFlightJOC service is a service running in JOC that consumes CrewOnFlight events produced by JCT
or a third party Crew Tracking system. See also chapter [Crew On Flight import to JOC](crew_on_flight_joc.html#stdif-crew-on-flight-joc).
The AOCMessageCrew service can be any service that support consuming the Jeppesen
AOC bookshelf messages. See also chapter [Jeppesen AOC bookshelf Maintenance message input](jeppesen_aoc.html#stdif-jeppesen-aoc-dp-in)

The default subscription configuration
is a *gliding subscription* with a *PeriodFilter* covering 30 days back and 60 days forward,
see `std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.generators`.
The core mapping for this interface is based on the mappings for the request/response service,
but adds the formatting and subscription features.

```
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="crew_on_flight_delta" language="Python">
  <include href="./mapping.xml"/>

  <!-- add subscription manager and postprocess to the default server mapping -->
  <server-impl service_name="CrewOnFlight" service_version="4">
    <runtime-parameters>
    <parameter name="manager" desc="Subscription Manager."/>
    </runtime-parameters>
    <post-process name="format" module="std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.generators" function="CrewOnFlightMessageGenerator.format" operation="getCrewOnFlight" process_struct="true"/>
  </server-impl>

  <input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest">
    <!-- imports and other stuff ... -->

    <!-- initialize the generator and formatter -->
    <assign name="generator" expr="generators.CrewOnFlightMessageGenerator(@{service}, plan, service_logger, now_time)"/>
    <assign name="formatter" expr="formatters.CrewOnFlightFormatter(service_logger, split_msg=True)"/>
    <call name="add_formatter" expr="generator.add_receiver('from.ioservice.crew_on_flight_4', formatter)"/>

    <!-- initialize the default subscription if empty -->
    <call name="default_subscription" expr="generators.default_subscription(manager,planholder,service_context)">
        <condition expr="manager.configuration_empty()"/>
    </call>

    <!--prepare the subscription phase -->
    <call name="prepare" expr="manager.prepare_delta_phase(now_time)"/>
    <!-- find affected flights-->
    <call-last name="find_flights" expr="flights.extend(generator.find_affected_flights(changeset,manager.filter))"/>

  </input-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

Crew information is by default communicated using the `LIVE` dataset, but
the service can be configured to use `PUBLISHED` or `ACKNOWLEDGED` dataset instead.
This is achived by using a custom SMOG mapping, overriding the `dataset` variable.

```
<input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest">
  <assign name="dataset" expr="'PUBLISHED'"/>
</input-mapping>
```

Note that one SMOG mapping file is needed for each dataset name, and each smog mapping
file must have a unique `target` attribute in the `<service-mapping>` element.

##### 14.1. Formatter CrewOnFlightFormatter

This formatter generates messages on the native SMOG protocol format of the CrewOnFlight service (i.e. plainxml, soap, plainjson etc.).

**Sink**: `from.ioservice.crew_on_flight_4`

**Class**: `std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.formatters.CrewOnFlightFormatter`

**Options**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| split\_msg | bool | Whether to split the message per flight, default True |

###### 14.1.1. IOService builder configuration

Example for the ‘plainxml’ protocol

Service CrewOnFlight\_4\_plainxml\_trigger

```
<ioservice name="CrewOnFlight_4_plainxml_trigger" pattern="trigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.trigger">
  <description>Trigger for crew on flight changes.</description>
  <subscription allow_requests="true" />
    <delta-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml">
      <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml"/>
      <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml"/>
      <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping.xml"/>
  </delta-service>
</ioservice>
```

##### 14.2. Formatter CrewOnFlightFormatterJOC

This formatter generates messages on the native SMOG protocol format of the CrewOnFlightJOC service (i.e. plainxml, soap, plainjson etc.).

**Sink**: *defined in configuration* (see ‘add\_receiver’ in the ‘SMOG configuration’ section below)

**Class**: `std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.formatters.CrewOnFlightFormatterJOC`

**Options**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| split\_msg | bool | Whether to split the message per flight, default True |
| service\_module | string | The python module containing the service class to use when formatting. Default ‘ioservice\_impl.air2\_mave2.CrewOnFlightJOC\_4\_server’. |
| service\_class | string | The name of the service class to use when formatting. Default ‘ServiceCrewOnFlightJOC\_plainxml’. |

###### 14.2.1. SMOG configuration

SMOG configuration required to add a receiver for the CrewOnFlightJOC service.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
  <include href="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping_trigger_delta.xml"/>

  <input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest">
    <assign name="formatter_joc" expr="formatters.CrewOnFlightFormatterJOC(service_logger, split_msg=True)"/>
    <call name="add_formatter_joc" expr="generator.add_receiver('from.ioservice.CrewOnFlight_4_event.joc', formatter_joc)"/>
  </input-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

###### 14.2.2. IOService builder configuration

Example for the ‘plainxml’ protocol:

Service CrewOnFlight\_4\_plainxml\_trigger

```
<ioservice name="CrewOnFlight_4_plainxml_trigger" pattern="trigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.trigger">
  <description>Trigger for crew on flight changes.</description>
  <subscription allow_requests="true" />
  <delta-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping.xml"/>
  </delta-service>
  <dependencies>
    <smog-service name="CrewOnFlightJOC" version="4" protocol="plainxml">
      <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml" />
      <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml" />
      <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping_joc.xml"/>
    </smog-service>
  </dependencies>
</ioservice>
```

##### 14.3. Formatter AOCMessageFormatter\_Crew

This formatter generates messages on the AOC bookshelf message format for crew assignments, see also stdif-aoc-crew-asmt-formatter.
Note that this formatter suppresses any events concerning deleted flight leg instances (represented internally as *implicitly cancelled*).

**Sink**: default sink, typically `from.ioservice.JeppesenAoc_event`

**Class**: `jeppesen_aoc.aoc_formatters.AOCMessageFormatter_Crew`

###### 14.3.1. SMOG configuration

SMOG configuration required to add a receiver for the AOCMessageCrew service.

For the delta subscription:

mapping\_aoc\_delta.xml

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
   <include href="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping_trigger_delta.xml"/>

   <input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest">
      <!-- Default values for configurable values parameters, set the correct value on the configuration layer -->
      <import alias="formatters_aoc" name="std_interfaces.jeppesen_aoc.aoc_formatters"/>
      <!-- String, Message Owner, use JetPlanId on the configuration layer, use owner name or function to determine>
      < owner name which will be used by JSI to filter messages -->
      <assign name="owner_value" expr="'owner'"/>
      <!-- String, HiMin Qualification name defined in configuration, the system will look for this qualification on the list>
      < of Crew Competencesfrom the std message and send the XML element with the value "True" if the qualification exists -->
      <assign name="hi_min_qual_name" expr="'HiMin'"/>
      <call name="add_formatter_aoc" expr="generator.add_receiver('from.ioservice.JeppesenAoc_event', formatters_aoc.AOCMessageFormatter_Crew(service_logger, owner_value, hi_min_qual_name))"/>
   </input-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

For load subscription:

mapping\_aoc\_load.xml

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
  <include href="./mapping_aoc_delta.xml"/>

  <input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest">
     <!-- find affected flights-->
     <call-last name="find_flights" expr="flights.extend(generator.find_all_flights())"/>
  </input-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

### Crew Roster Input


This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to provide roster data to the JCMS. Roster data usually has a shared ownership model,
where the data for different time periods is owned by different systems at different times in the planning process.

The current version of this interface is 3.

[Link to RosterState\_3.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.roster_input_3/RosterState_3.xsd)

[Link to RosterState\_3.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.roster_input_3/RosterState_3.wsdl)

Previous versions of this interface is 2.1.

[Link to RosterState\_2\_1.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.roster_input_2_1/RosterState_2_1.xsd)

##### 15.1. Interface capabilities

The source system may send updates for several updates in one message. The interface then treats the complete
message as one transaction. Should an error occur for one of the roster updates, the others will be discarded too.
The general error handling strategy is to store any incoming data if possible, even if it is considered illegal.
Data that cannot be stored, e.g. assignments referring to a non-existing station, will always yield an exception
and the message will be rejected. This is true regardless if the faulty data is required or not.

Available operations are:

* **ping**
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* **setRosters**
  :   Updates rosters in JCMS with information from the provided message (one-way request without any response message).
* **setRostersWithAck**
  :   Same as setRosters but with an acknowledge response on successful operation (request/response).

The interface handles crew assignments to trips and tasks.

* **trip**:
  + Assigned trips are expected to be already existing in the system before being assigned to crew members by this interface.
  + This interface doesn’t support assignment information of activities within a trip, e.g. assigned training tag/roster tag on a flight leg within a trip is not supported.
* **task**:
  + Tasks are created by the interface together with the assignment to that activity.
  + Internally in JCMS a task may be classified as either a “ground task”, e.g. a training task, or a “personal activity” (pact), e.g. a vacation.
    - A ground task is “wrapped” inside a trip internally in JCMS, and the crew member is assigned to the wrapper trip instead of to the activity
      directly. The interface creates the wrapper trip automatically for ground task.
    - A personal activity is directly assigned to the crew member without being “wrapped” inside a trip.

JCMS will use the current state (at time of the message evaluation) of the trip or task to fill the assignment attributes (stations and times).

Additiona crew assginment information can be provided in the form of assignment training tags and roster tags.
The information is updated as a state, i.e. the assigned training tags/roster tags in JCMS are updated to match the information in the inbound message.
Tags are removed from the roster in JCMS if the inbound message doesn’t have any tag for the assignment respectively, even if the existing tags
were added by some other user or process.

Changes are saved in the live dataset and normally published automatically. It is possible to configure
the interface so that changes are also acknowledged automatically.

The picture below illustrates the logical flow when the interface handles a roster update request. The remainder
of this chapter provides more details on various aspects of the functionality.

![../_images/Roster_update.png](../_images/Roster_update.png)

Activity diagram for roster updates

###### 15.1.1. Matching of trips and tasks

For the matching of trips and tasks in the roster interface first of all the general rules described in the
introduction apply, see [Matching of Planning Objects](introduction.html#stdif-intro-matching-objects). The purpose of the matching is to find existing trips
or activities on the roster on which the roster update operations should be applied.

For trips, if no matching trip is found or if the match is ambiguous, then the operation fails and an error response message is returned.
By default, only “name” and “dateOfOrigin” in TripMatch elements are used for trip matching, other attributes (“category”, “homeBase”
“startStation”, “endStation”, “startTime”, “endTime”) are not used for matching and will be removed in future version of this interface.

Tasks are only looked up within the given crew member’s roster. The matching requires the activityType as well as the stations to
be identical and for the start/end the same fuzzy matching as for flights is used. The interface creates
new tasks on the roster if necessary.
If no stations are provided for a task, the most recent valid homebase of the crew member, relative to the activity’s start time,
are used as default stations.

Generally, if an existing assignment is found it is updated with the role attribute and addtional information that is available on the
assignment in the message.

Note that if an existing trip assignment is not found, then a role must be specified in order for a new assignment
to be created, otherwise the operation will fail. For ground tasks and (non-personal) ground transports on the other hand,
role is not required. If a role is specified, it is used when assigning the wrapper trip that contains the task. If a role
is not specified, then a default role is derived from the crew member’s function. For personal activities, a role is not
required, therefore no default role is used if not specified.

If no role is specified when updating an existing ground task or (non-personal) ground transport assignment, then
the role will fall back to the default role. If no role is specified when updating an existing personal activity
assignment, then the role will be removed if a role existed in the JCMS data model before the update.

The picture below illustrates the process of matching trips and tasks from a logical point of view.

![../_images/Match_with_existing_model.png](../_images/Match_with_existing_model.png)

Activity diagram for matching existing trips and tasks

If the best match is ambiguous then the operation will fail. If no matching task is found the interface will create one.
Tasks that are no longer assigned will be completely deleted (not only de-assigned). For a found match, the
activity times will be updated if they differ from those specified in the message.

As mentioned earlier, wrapper trips are created when adding a new ground task or a (non-personal) ground transport activity.
The homebase of the wrapper trip is derived in the following way (in priority order):

* The base associated with the activity’s start station, if any
* The base associated with the activity’s end station, if any
* The base whose id is identical to the id of the activity’s start station, if exists
* The base whose id is identical to the id of the activity’s end station, if exists
* The most recent valid homebase of the crew member, relative to the activity’s start time

The interface does not enforce that this homebase corresponds
to the start station of the activity. A deviation will result in an illegal trip that will have to be manually
repaired, e.g. by adding deadhead transports to and from the activity station. Furthermore, the crew composition of the
wrapper trip is set to reflect the role that is used for the assignment, whether it is provided in the message or a derived
default role.

Time offset, i.e. time zone difference to UTC, checking is performed on all specified times, if the offsets are provided. The picture below illustrates
the process of checking time offsets. Note that in the baseline version of roster intput interfaces, offsets can
only be provided for tasks. In the figure below, it means only the lower left corner is in effect.

![../_images/Check_start_and_end_time_offsets.png](../_images/Check_start_and_end_time_offsets.png)

Activity diagram for checking start and end time offsets

###### 15.1.2. Roster State Input

Roster state input (setRosters operation in RosterState service) is suitable for loading initial rosters or big updates.
It provides complete state of some crew members roster for a given time period.
The given period for updates must be guaranteed to cover all potential changes, so if the source system doesn’t have
fine grained change detection it should send with fixed coarse granularity.
All assignments that might exist in this time period before the message is applied will be removed if no
longer present in the provided data. Assignments that are present both in the message and in the existing roster
will be updated to match the data in the message.

Note that also locked assignments may be updated by the interface, but they are not removed even if the message
doesn’t contain them.

This kind of message is generally sent in batch mode and no two messages about the same crew are expected within the
same time interval (of a few minutes). If it is decided to use this kind of messages in online mode or in combination
with other flows that could touch the same crew in parallel, then conflict detection must be secured. Either all
involved flows use a consistent state reference mechanism (e.g. the JCMS cid) or a conflict trigger must be implemented
that fits the message granularity. Note that this method is not well suited for frequent incremental roster updates
since it requires a coarse granularity of conflict detection and is thus prone to temporary “data-to-old” errors.
It might still be the only valid method depending on the capabilities of the source system(s), but note that frequent
messages about the same crew member will lead to many transient errors and thus bad overall performance.

Annotations that are intended to be shared with crew members can be provided over the interface, such annotations
are internally stored with code PUBLIC.

####### 15.1.2.1. Roster layer concept

Some sending system might not be aware of the full state of a roster, but only of a selected set of assignments.
We call that selection the “roster layer” which the source system is responsible for.
The setRosters operation can also be used in this case as long as the assignments in each roster layer can be clearly
identified inside JCMS. The layer is identified by the source name in the message. The message is then interpreted as
replacement for the set of all assignments in the affected roster layer inside the time period.

A typical case is a vacation system which only knows about absences for crew.
The standard interface implementation supports this kind of layer by associating a selection of activity types with
a given source. If a source has a list of activity codes associated with it, then its layer consists of all assigned
activities with any of the codes.
A source that has no definition attached is expected to be the “remaining” and its layer consists of all
assignments that do not have any of the activity codes associated with any other source. By definition this
layer contains all assigned trips because a trip doesn’t have an activity code. This does of course not apply to
the wrapper trips mentioned above.

Since the core implementation doesn’t contain any predefined sets of activity codes, by default all sources will
affect the full roster.

Customization can define sets of activity codes for different sources by adding them to the (default empty)
dictionary defined in the python module that provides the business functions for this interface.
Where more complex logic is needed (e.g. to define a layer that contains a subset of trip assignments) the layer
identification function must be overwritten.

####### 15.1.2.2. Matching of trips and tasks within the roster period

A roster state header shall always give the actually delivered period per roster, but not covering the full carry-out.
If any requested assignment doesn’t start in the specified period the operation will fail, but ending outside the period is ok.
Report time is taken as start time for an assignment, if report time is within the specified period then the operation will succeed.
Note that existing assignments that are found based on the provided information are not dropped even if they
violate these consistency requirements, e.g a trip will stay assigned even if it isn’t fully within the period.

For each provided assignment, the trip or task is looked up according to the principles described above,
see [Matching of trips and tasks](#stdif-roster-input-matching-objects).

An activity that does not start in the period can only be assigned by providing Task times in the message that are within the
period. Since the activity times are required there is always a check that the actual activity times don’t deviate
too much from the Task times specified in the message. These times are supposed to reflect the source systems view
of the activity state. The actual activity (and wrapper trip if applicable) is updated to reflect this state.

The roster update is supposed to contain the complete state of the crew members roster for the specified layer
and within the specified time period. Any existing assignments that are not included in the message, are removed
unless they are locked.
For ground tasks, the interface not only removes the assignment but also the associated wrapper trip.
Likewise for personal activities the interface removes the assignment. However for technical reasons the activity object itself
is not dropped from the data model, although no crew is assigned to it.

The picture below illustrates the process of removing existing assignments and activities that don’t belong to the
updated roster state.

![../_images/Remove_non_matched_asmts.png](../_images/Remove_non_matched_asmts.png)

Activity diagram for removing non-matched assignments

##### 15.2. Use cases

###### 15.2.1. Example scenario

For the examples we assume an installation of JCMS and the crew rosters are fed in from other systems.
The Rostering system for cockpit crew has been updated recently to deal with the full state, including planned absences,
while for cabin crew the vacation and long term absences are handled in a separate system still.

For process reasons Holiday seasons are planned separately,
we assume the next planning period to load is from 28th of November to 20th of December 2009.
The rosters are already available for November, and now we are about to load the next month.

The base for the following examples is the state of the roster for a Flight Officer and a Purser, to demonstrate the difference in layer handling.
For cockpit crew the Rostering system is the only source and all assignments are owned by it until the Tracking period starts.
For cabin crew all activities in the activity groups “VAC” (vacation) and “LOA” (leave of absence) are provided and maintained in the vacation system
while all other activities are owned by the Rostering system until the Tracking period starts.

From a technical perspective we have a layer setup like this:

* Cockpit has just one layer for all assignments. (Default layer)
* Cabin has two layers. One for vacations and one for the rest.

The last assignment in the roster of our Flight Officer is

| typ | id | dep | arr | start | end | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trip | 51470 | CPH | CPH | 26NOV2009 07:10 | 29NOV2009 06:25 | FP | 26NOV2009 07:10 | 29NOV2009 06:25 |

Notice that the trip ends after the start of the next planning period, it is a carry-in.
The last assignment on the Purser is two days off

| typ | id | dep | arr | start | end | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| task | S-FRE | TRD | TRD | 24NOV2009 23:00 | 26NOV2009 23:00 |  | 24NOV2009 23:00 | 26NOV2009 23:00 |

####### 15.2.1.1. Initial load

The following example represents the initial roster for December for the Flight Officer.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setRostersRequest xmlns="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                    version="2.1" source="Rostering" created="2009-11-15T23:13:44"  >
<roster crewId="04873" start="2009-11-28T00:00:00" end="2009-12-28T00:00:00" >
  <assignment role="FP" >
    <trip name="7771" />
  </assignment>
  <assignment>
    <task activityType="IN" startStation="GOT" endStation="GOT" 
          startTime="2009-12-05T00:00:00" endTime="2009-12-28T00:00:00" />
  </assignment>
</roster>
</setRostersRequest>
```

Note that the end of period for this roster is set to 28DEC 00:00 even though the loaded period is defined to end at 20th.
This is due to the fact that the vacation doesn’t end earlier, so the effective loaded period for this crew member is extended.
The carry-in trip is not replaced since it starts before the request period, the resulting illegality must be resolved as a normal planning problem.
The resulting roster looks now like this.

| typ | id | dep | arr | start | end | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trip | 51470 | CPH | CPH | 26NOV2009 07:10 | 29NOV2009 06:25 | FP | 26NOV2009 07:10 | 29NOV2009 06:25 |
| trip | 7771 | CPH | CPH | 29NOV2009 07:45 | 29NOV2009 15:10 | FP | 29NOV2009 07:45 | 29NOV2009 15:10 |
| task | VAC | CPH | CPH | 05DEC2009 00:00 | 28DEC2009 00:00 |  | 05DEC2009 00:00 | 28DEC2009 00:00 |

The following example represents the initial roster for December for the Purser from the vacation system.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setRostersRequest xmlns="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                    version="1.0" source="VAC" created="2009-11-15T23:13:44"  >
<roster crewId="02905" start="2009-11-28T00:00:00" end="2009-12-21T00:00:00" >
  <assignment>
    <task activityType="IN" startStation="TRD" endStation="TRD" 
          startTime="2009-12-01T00:00:00" endTime="2009-12-15T00:00:00" />
  </assignment>
</roster>
</setRostersRequest>
```

The resulting roster now looks like this:

| typ | id | dep | arr | start | end | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| task | S-FRE | TRD | TRD | 24NOV2009 23:00 | 26NOV2009 23:00 |  | 24NOV2009 23:00 | 26NOV2009 23:00 |
| task | VAC | TRD | TRD | 01DEC2009 00:00 | 15DEC2009 00:00 |  | 01DEC2009 00:00 | 15DEC2009 00:00 |

The following example represents the initial roster for December for the Purser from the Rostering system.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setRostersRequest xmlns="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                    version="2.1" source="Rostering" created="2009-11-15T23:13:44"  >
<roster crewId="02905" start="2009-11-28T00:00:00" end="2009-12-21T00:00:00" >
  <assignment role="AP" >
    <trip name="44590" />
  </assignment>
</roster>
</setRostersRequest>
```

The resulting roster now looks like this:

| typ | id | dep | arr | start | end | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| task | S-FRE | TRD | TRD | 24NOV2009 23:00 | 26NOV2009 23:00 |  | 24NOV2009 23:00 | 26NOV2009 23:00 |
| trip | 44590 | TRD | TRD | 29NOV2009 15:25 | 30NOV2009 20:35 | AP | 29NOV2009 15:25 | 30NOV2009 20:35 |
| task | VAC | TRD | TRD | 01DEC2009 00:00 | 15DEC2009 00:00 |  | 01DEC2009 00:00 | 15DEC2009 00:00 |

Note that the vacation has not been dropped even though it lies within the delivered period.
It belongs to the vacation systems ownership and not to the Rostering systems layer.

####### 15.2.1.2. Update roster

The following example represents another message that updates roster for December for the Flight Officer.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setRostersRequest xmlns="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                    version="2.1" source="Rostering" created="2009-11-15T23:13:44"  >
<roster crewId="04873" start="2009-11-28T00:00:00" end="2009-12-28T00:00:00" >
  <assignment role="FP" >
    <trip name="39567" />
  </assignment>
  <assignment>
    <task activityType="IN" startStation="GOT" endStation="GOT" 
          startTime="2009-12-05T00:00:00" endTime="2009-12-28T00:00:00" />
  </assignment>
</roster>
</setRostersRequest>
```

The resulting roster looks now like this.

| typ | id | dep | arr | start | end | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trip | 51470 | CPH | CPH | 26NOV2009 07:10 | 29NOV2009 06:25 | FP | 26NOV2009 07:10 | 29NOV2009 06:25 |
| trip | 39567 | CPH | CPH | 28NOV2009 07:20 | 30NOV2009 09:55 | FP | 28NOV2009 07:20 | 30NOV2009 09:55 |
| task | VAC | CPH | CPH | 05DEC2009 00:00 | 28DEC2009 00:00 |  | 05DEC2009 00:00 | 28DEC2009 00:00 |

Only the trip assignment from initial load above is replaced with the new trip.

###### 15.2.2. UC: Basic update of trip assignments

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip assignments.

Actor: A person with role tracker, that changes a trip and locks it.

As there is no coupling between different crew member’s rosters, even though the data can come in the same in message,
this UC only needs to consider one crew member’s roster.
Precondition: we need to have to trips that we can assign.

First the rostering system sends us a msg that contains two assignments of trips, asmt1 & asmt2.
We process the msg and assign them to the crew member with the specific role for each asmt.
Then the tracker actor updates the asmt1, changing the role, and then locks it, preventing it from being deleted by incoming msgs.
The external system sends an update that deletes asmt1 & updates asmt2 with a different role.
This results in no changes for asmt 1, since it is locked, and updates of the asmt 2.
Note that the asmt 2 object should be updated not recreated, so it should still contain the same untouched data as before.
Assignment 2 has new role as FC.

In messages:

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-05T00:00:00" start="2009-11-05T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:trip name="51470" />
		</ns1:assignment>
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:trip name="7771" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-01T00:00:00" start="2009-11-10T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FC" >
			<ns1:trip name="7771" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

Gantt view result:

```
in msg   |--------|===asmt1====|----------|===asmt2===|---------|
lock              |===asmt1====|
in msg          |-------------------------|===asmt2===|---------|
db after  --------|===asmt1====|----------|===asmt2===|------------
```

###### 15.2.3. UC: Carry in/out assignments in message

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip assignments.

Any assignment in message that start outside the update window are considered faulty and will give an error.

In the example below, both the messages contains assignments that are partly outside the update window.
The first one starts outside the update window, this is an error so nothing will be committed to db.
The second one starts in, adn ends outside the update window, this an is ok so it will be committed to db.

In messages:

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-11-29T11:00:00" start="2009-11-27T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:trip name="51470" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-11-29T11:00:00" start="2009-11-27T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:trip name="7771" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

Gant view result:

```
upd window          |--------------------------------|
in msg     |=======asmt1=======|
in msg                                    |=======asmt2=======|
db after            |---------------------|=======asmt2=======|
```

###### 15.2.4. UC: Update of existing assignments carry in/out

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip assignments.

Any existing assignments in the db that themselves stick out of, i.e. start in, the update period are consider to be targets for update.

In the example below we have two assignments, in the db, that are partly inside the update period,
but only the one starting inside will be considered for update.
As a result the asmt starting in the update period will be deleted.

In messages:

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-01T00:00:00" start="2009-11-01T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP" >
			<ns1:trip name="39410" />
		</ns1:assignment>
		<ns1:assignment role="FP" >
			<ns1:trip name="35481" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-11-21T00:00:00" start="2009-11-15T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:trip name="16117" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

Gantt view result:

```
prereq  ---|====trip1====|--------------|===trip2===|----
prereq  ---|====asmt1====|--------------|===asmt2===|----
in msg                 |---|===asmt3===|---|
db after --|====asmt1====|-|===asmt3===|------------------
```

###### 15.2.5. UC: Update separation in 2 layers for separate activities.

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip or personal activity assignments.
:   This is considered to be in the layer 1.

Actor: A second external system that sends messages containing only crew ground task assignments.
:   This is considered to be in the layer 2.

The first message sends assignments that will be committed to db.
The second message has an update period that covers the previous assignment,
but they are in layer 1 so they are ignored, since the message is layer 2.
So, the result is that asmt1 and asmt2 are left in the db and the asmt3 is added.

In messages:

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-28T00:00:00" start="2009-10-28T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP" >
			<ns1:trip name="7771" />
		</ns1:assignment>
		<ns1:assignment>
			<ns1:task activityType="VY12" endStation="CPH"
				endTime="2009-12-05T00:00:00" startStation="CPH" startTime="2009-12-04T00:00:00" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="TRAINING" version="2.1"
	xmlns:ns1="http://roster_state_input_1.service.jcms.jeppesen.com">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-10T00:00:00" start="2009-11-20T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:task activityType="E" endStation="CPH" endTime="2009-12-02T09:00:00"
				startStation="CPH" startTime="2009-12-02T05:00:00" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

Gantt view result:

```
in layer 1 |----|===trip=asmt1====|------------------|===pact=asmt2===|-----|
in layer 2    |-----------------------|=grnd=asmt3=|----------------------|
db after  ------|===trip=asmt1====|---|=grnd=asmt3=|-|===pact=asmt2===|-------
```

###### 15.2.6. UC: Updates in each of 2 layers while keeping separation.

Actor: An external system that sends messages containing only crew trip or personal activity assignments.
:   This is considered to be in the layer 1.

Actor: A second external system that sends messages containing only crew ground task assignments.
:   This is considered to be in the layer 2.

The first message send layer 1 assignments that will be committed to db.
The second message has an update period that covers the previous assignment,
and add two ground assignments.
This results is all assignments committed to the db since they are separate layers.

Now two new messages are sent in, one for each layer, with updates to the assignments.
The result is that the updates delete assignments for their layer only,
leaving two modified assignments in the db.

In messages:

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="3"
	xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/RosterState/v3">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-28T00:00:00" start="2009-10-28T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP" >
			<ns1:trip name="7771" />
		</ns1:assignment>
		<ns1:assignment>
			<ns1:task activityType="VY12" endStation="CPH"
				endTime="2009-12-05T00:00:00" startStation="CPH" startTime="2009-12-04T00:00:00" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="VACATION" version="3"
	xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/RosterState/v3">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-30T00:00:00" start="2009-10-30T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:task activityType="TQ" endStation="CPH" endTime="2009-12-02T09:00:00"
				startStation="CPH" startTime="2009-12-02T05:00:00" />
		</ns1:assignment>
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:task activityType="TQ" endStation="CPH" endTime="2009-12-05T00:00:00"
				startStation="CPH" startTime="2009-12-04T00:00:00" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
</ns1:setRostersRequest>
```

```
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<ns1:setRostersRequest created="2009-12-01T00:00:00"
	source="ROSTER" version="3"
	xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/RosterState/v3">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-25T00:00:00" start="2009-10-28T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment>
			<ns1:task activityType="VY12" endStation="CPH"
				endTime="2009-12-04T05:00:00" startStation="CPH" startTime="2009-12-03T05:00:00" />
		</ns1:assignment>
	</ns1:roster>
```

```
	source="VACATION" version="3"
	xmlns:ns1="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/RosterState/v3">
	<ns1:roster crewId="04873" end="2009-12-25T00:00:00" start="2009-10-30T00:00:00">
		<ns1:assignment role="FP">
			<ns1:task activityType="TQ" endStation="CPH" endTime="2009-12-02T05:30:00"
```

### Crew Roster Output


This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to get roster information from JCMS.
Roster information is normally sent when explicitly requested by an external user or system
(request/response pattern). The information can also be sent spontaneously by JCMS, either on changes or
on a scheduled basis (publish/subscribe pattern). The latter requires however a service trigger to be
configured inside JCMS. Such triggers are not provided out of the box by the standard interface but must
be added as part of an implementation project. In addition, it is also possible, as a part of
implementation project customization, to add mechanisms to enable e.g. a Tracking user to manually request
roster information to be sent out to predefined destinations.

The current version of this interface is 5.

[Link to RosterStateOutput\_5.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.roster_output_5/RosterStateOutput_5.xsd)

[Link to RosterStateOutput\_5.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.roster_output_5/RosterStateOutput_5.wsdl)

Previous versions of this interface

[Link to RosterState\_4.xsd (version 4)](contract/std_interfaces.roster_output_4/RosterState_4.xsd)

[Link to RosterStateSoap\_4.wsdl (version 4)](contract/std_interfaces.roster_output_4/RosterStateSoap_4.wsdl)

[Link to RosterState\_2\_0.xsd (version 2.0)](contract/std_interfaces.roster_output_2_0/RosterState_2_0.xsd)

[Link to RosterStateSoap\_2\_0.wsdl (version 2.0)](contract/std_interfaces.roster_output_2_0/RosterStateSoap_2_0.wsdl)

##### 16.1. Interface capabilities

The interface supports the following operations:

* **ping**
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* **getRosters**
  :   It allows to request all rosters for a group of crew selected by crew category or base.
      If neither category nor base is specified, then rosters of all crew are returned.
      It is also possible to specify both category and base in which case the interface returns rosters of
      all crew matching both the specified category and base.
* **getRostersByCrewid**
  :   It allows to request rosters for a list of crew members, identified by
      their crew id (alias). At least one crew id must be specified in the request.

###### 16.1.1. Scope of returned roster state

In both request types it is required to specify a request period. The interface responds with the state of
all matching rosters for the requested time period. Note that roster elements, with some basic crew
attributes, are included for all matching crew members, even if they don’t have any assignments within the
requested period.

All activities (trips or personal tasks) overlapping the
requested time period are included in the response, i.e. the trip or task must start before the end of the requested period
and end after the start of the requested period. The task and trip start/end times must be defined by specific
Rave variables, see [Rave definitions](#rave-definitions).

Assigned trips are always included in their entirety such that also duties and/or activities outside the
requested period are included as long as some piece of the trip is inside the period. In order to
guarantee that trips are always complete, while still maintaining good operating performance, the system
has a built-in assumption about maximum trip length. This is by default set to 10 days, but can be
customized if needed.

###### 16.1.2. Content of the roster state

The following types of activities, and any combination of them, are included:

* Trip, including the following activities:
  + Flight Leg (including return-to-ramp and wait-at-gate events)
  + Air Transport
  + Ground Task
  + Ground Transport
* Ground Task
* Ground Transport
* Crew Activity (e.g. vacation, sickness…)

In accordance with the interface schema, the crew complement of each trip included in the roster state
must contain at least one role. If however crew for some reason would be assigned to a trip with
undefined or empty crew complement, then the interface will output a crew complement item with the
role to which crew is currently assigned, and with the crew count set to 1.

In roster response, the start time is aligned with the start time of the first activity if
it is lower than the period start time in the request.
The end time is however not aligned with the end time of the last activity if it is greater than
the period end time in the request, as it is valid to have carry out activities.

Note that for Air Transports normally very limited information is available. Although represented
by the same data type as normal Flight Legs in the interface schema, some of the fields like e.g.
effectiveEndStation, estimatedStartTime and actualStartTime are never included for Air Transports.

Export of annotations is limited to annotations that are intended to be shared with crew members, such annotations
have an annotation code that is internally tagged with the attribute ‘is\_public’ set to True.

All Ground Tasks outside trips are technically “wrapped” inside a trip internally in JCMS. However, in the
roster state messages produced by this interface they are represented as plain tasks without the wrapper
trip. Conversely, a Ground Task that has explicitly been wrapped in a real trip is represented as a trip
on the roster and it contains the Ground Task as a task element. The system distinguishes wrapper trips from
real trips by using a special trip category reserved exclusively for internal usage.

###### 16.1.3. Supported protocols

The interface supports requests using both plain XML and SOAP. The SOAP service is primarily intended for
supporting external WEB services. For use with internal triggers the plain XML form of the service is
normally used.

###### 16.1.4. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Crew Roster Output standard interface:

* `interfaces_core.%roster_out_trip_start_utc%`: Defines the start time of a trip or task, used for output of
  trip report time and for identifying whether the trip or task is in the requested period or not.
* `interfaces_core.%roster_out_trip_end_utc%`: Defines the end time of a trip or task, used for output of
  trip release time and for identifying whether the trip or task is in the requested period or not.
* `interfaces_core.%crew_trip_training_tags%`: Defines the trip-level crew\_asmt\_trng\_tag.
  It is used to populate <assignedTrainingTag> of the trip. Multiple tags should be concatenated into a single string
  separated by “,”. Empty string should be returned if no tag is found. If the Rave variable is not configure in CARMUSR,
  the interface will fall back to use ARA API which only works for LIVE dataset.
* `interfaces_core.%crew_trip_roster_tags%`: Defines the trip-level roster\_tag.
  It is used to populate <rosterTag> of the trip. Multiple tags should be concatenated into a single string
  separated by “,”. Empty string should be returned if no tag is found. If the Rave variable is not configure in CARMUSR,
  the interface will fall back to use ARA API which only works for LIVE dataset.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a **CARMUSR** to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline.

###### 16.1.5. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most interfaces, i.e. to reject the message
if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. Concretely for the Roster State Outbound interface it
means that if it fails to generate roster for any of the crew members matching the request, it will respond
with an error message.

##### 16.2. Use cases

The examples below all use the plain XML service, the same use cases can be executed in the SOAP service
but then a SOAP envelope and the SoapAction header are required.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<getRostersRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/RosterStateOutput/v5"
                    version="5" source="BB" created="2013-11-25T23:13:44"
                    periodStart="2014-03-24T00:00:00" periodEnd="2014-03-26T00:00:00"/>
```

this will lead to an output like the following

```
                  periodEnd="2014-03-25T08:00:40" periodStart="2014-03-24T07:00:00" source="BB" version="5"/>]]></sourceMessage>
</error>
```
