### Flight Events


This chapter describes the standard interface for publishing flight information to external systems when flight related events occur in JCMS.
The interface publish event messages for updates of scheduled flights, before day of operation, as well as aircraft movements,
diversions, return-to-ramp events etc. during day of operation.
Event messages are published by the interface when flight information is updated in the JCMS database.

One aspect of external systems, receiving the published event messages, is that they usually expect different type of event messages for the same event occurring in JCMS.
For example, some systems might expect IATA messages while others expects messages on xml or other format.
Another aspect of the receiving systems is that they are interested in different subsets of flight events occurring in JCMS. For example, some systems might
only expect messages for changes of scheduled flights when others expects messages for only operational flights.

The interface handles these two aspects, message format and events of interest, by supporting a concept of *receivers*,
see [Message Receivers](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-receivers-pattern).
Multiple receivers can be configured in the Flight Events interface where each receiver is associated with a specific message format, events of interest and other options.

The interface generates event messages for each *receiver* when flight events occur in JCMS.
A *receiver* should rather be seen as a “logical receiver”, and is not necessarily the same as an external system receiving the event messages since
there might be several external systems receiving same event messages for one and the same *receiver*.

Default receivers:

* Native (FlightInput version 5)
* IATA (ASM, MVT, DIV)

The following table provides an overview of message types published by this interface for different types of events.

| Event in JCMS | Native Receiver (FlightInput request) | IATA message type |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flight created | X | ASM NEW |  |
| Leg added to multi-leg flight | X | ASM RPL |  |
| Leg cancelled or deleted | X | ASM CNL |  |
| Leg re-instated | X | ASM RIN |  |
| Flight or leg(s) renamed | X | ASM FLT |  |
| Planned aircraft type updated | X | ASM EQT |  |
| Service type updated | X | ASM EQT |  |
| Tail assignment updated | X | ASM EQT |  |
| Scheduled times updated | X | ASM TIM |  |
| Scheduled departure station updated | X | ASM RPL |  |
| Scheduled arrival station updated | X | ASM RRT |  |
| Onward flight updated | X | ASM ADM\*\* |  |
| Passenger terminal updated | X | ASM ADM |  |
| Code sharing updated | X | ASM ADM |  |
| Seat configuration updated | X | ASM CON |  |
| Estimated departure times updated | X | MVT ED |  |
| Delay information updated | X | MVT ED or MVT AD/EO |  |
| Next Information time updated | X | MVT ED\*\*\* |  |
| Actual departure times updated | X | MVT AD |  |
| Return to ramp | X | MVT AD/RR |  |
| Estimated arrival times updated | X | MVT EA or MVT AA/EB |  |
| Actual arrival times updated | X | MVT AA |  |
| Internal times updated | X |  |  |
| Return from airborne (forced return) | X | MVT FR |  |
| Diversion | X | DIV |  |

\*\* For onward flight changes, ASM ADM is only sent for flights as long as they don’t have an aircraft assigned.

\*\* ASM NEW/EQT/RPL will also be sent when neither PRBD nor ACV exists, even though the SSIM requires that (from March 2012) at least one of them need to be included.

\*\* MVT AA and MVT EA are also generated when estimated/actual arrival times are updated for return-to-ramp or return-to-land events.
:   Such MVT messages contains the departure airport as Airport of Movement and are only generated when when times of the most recent
    return event are updated, in case multiple returns has occurred for same flight leg.

[\*\*](#id1)\* If a Next Information time is set or updated, a separate MVT ED message is published only containing the changed Next Information time.

On certain combinations of events, only one of the message types are generated. The following applies:

* If any of the events triggering an ASM RPL message occurs, and at the same time the flight is rescheduled, rerouted, has a change
  in tail assignment or onward flight information, then the TIM, RRT, EQT and ADM messages are suppressed and only the RPL message is generated.
* If the scheduled arrival station is updated and at the same time the flight is rescheduled, has a change in tail assignment or onward
  flight information, then the TIM, EQT and ADM messages are suppressed and only the RRT message is generated.

##### 17.1. Configuring message receivers

It’s possible to configure the receivers this interface should use when sending event messages by updating the default SMOG service-mapping
and call the `generator.add_receiver` method.

```
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
  <include href="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/mapping_client.xml"/>

  <output-mapping struct="flight_input.FlightsUpdateMsg">
    <call name="add_receiver_iata_asm_local" expr="generator.add_receiver('from.ioservice.FlightInput_5_event.iata_local', iata.IATAFormatterASM(service_logger, local_time=True))"/>
    <call name="add_receiver_iata_asm" expr="generator.add_receiver('from.ioservice.FlightInput_5_event.iata', iata.IATAFormatterASM(service_logger, local_time=True))"/>
    <call name="add_receiver_iata_mvt" expr="generator.add_receiver('from.ioservice.FlightInput_5_event.iata', iata.IATAFormatterMVT(service_logger))"/>
  </output-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

The `generator.add_receiver` method registers a new a receiver for messages on a specific format.
Each receiver is associated with a specific message queue and a formatter that determines the format
and formatting options of the generated messages for that receiver.

The example above shows how the formatter `IATAFormatterASM` is added twice, for different message queues with different formatting options.
It also shows that both formatters `IATAFormatterASM` and `IATAFormatterMVT` are added with the same message queue, specifying that
both ASM and MVT messages should sent to same message queue.

###### 17.1.1. Native formatter

This formatter generates messages on the native SMOG protocol format of the FlightInput service (i.e. plainxml, soap, plainjson etc.).

*Class*

```
std_interfaces.common.NativeProtocolFormatter
```

*Options*

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |

###### 17.1.2. IATA ASM formatter

This formatter produces IATA Ad Hoc Schedules Messages (ASM) for relevant flight updates.

Formatted AMS messages does not contain the following information:

* DEI 1 - Joint Operation Airline Designators
* DEI 2 - Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
* DEI 9 - Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation
* Creator Reference
* Secondary Action
* Change Reason, except for ASM CNL where cancellation codes are provided as Change Reason.
* Meal Service Note

*Class* `std_interfaces.iata.formatters.IATAFormatterASM`

*Options*

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| windows\_line\_endings | bool | If True, ASM messages are produced with ‘\r\n’ line endings instead of ‘\n’. Default False. |
| local\_time | bool | If True, all times in produced ASM messages are in local time. Default False (= all times in UTC). |
| new\_instead\_of\_rin | bool | If True, ASM/NEW messages are produced in place of ASM/RIN when a leg is reinstated. Default False. |
| new\_cnl\_instead\_of\_flt | bool | If True, an ASM/NEW followed by an ASM/CNL message is produced in place of ASM/FLT when a flight or sub-segment of a flight is renamed. If legs already exist with the new flight identifier, then ASM/RPL is produced instead of ASM/NEW. Default False. |
| rpl\_instead\_of\_rrt | bool | If True, ASM/RPL messages are produced in place of ASM/RRT when the scheduled arrival station is updated. Default False. |
| rpl\_instead\_of\_adm | bool | If True, ASM/RPL messages are produced in place of ASM/ADM when code share or terminal information is updated. Default False. |
| suppress\_eqt\_if\_cancelled | bool | If True, ASM/EQT messages are not produced for flight being cancelled. Default True. |
| suppress\_con\_if\_cancelled | bool | If True, ASM/CON messages are not produced for flight being cancelled. Default True. |

###### 17.1.3. IATA MVT/DIV formatter

This formatter produces IATA Aircraft Movement (MVT) and Aircraft Diversion (DIV) messages for relevant flight updates.

Formatted MVT messages does not contain the following information:

* DEI 8.1, Reclearance Information
* DEI 8.5, Crew Report Time
* DEI 8.6, Movement After Pushback
* DEI 8.8, Take Off Fuel
* DEI 8.9, Take Off Weight
* DEI 8.10, Zero Fuel Weight
* DEI 8.11, Category of Operation
* DEI 11, Next information

Formatted DIV messages does not contain the following information:
\* DEI 6, Reason for Diversion

*Class* `std_interfaces.iata.formatters.IATAFormatterMVT`

*Options*

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| windows\_line\_endings | bool | If True, MVT and DIV messages are produced with ‘\r\n’ line endings instead of ‘\n’. Default False. |

###### 17.1.4. Custom formatter

It’s possible to configure new message formatters by adding a subclass of the `MessageFormatter` to the configuration layer and implementing
the `format` method.

```
from std_interfaces.common import MessageFormatter

class MyMessageFormatter(MessageFormatter):
    """
    Formatter generating messages containing the flight number of updated flights.
    """

    def format(self, payload, headers):
        """
        @param payload: Object containing updated flight data.
        @type payload:  ioservice_impl.air2_mave2.FlightInput_5_client.FlightsUpdateMsg
        @param headers: Dictionary of headers passed with the incoming request message
        @type headers:  dict
        @return:        Tuple of two lists of equal length, one with output messages content and one with message header attributes
        @rtype:         (list of string, list of dict)
        """
        contents = list()
        headers = list()
        for action in payload.action:
              contents.append(str(action.setFlight.flightNumber))
              headers.append(dict())
        return contents, headers
```

Receivers can be configured for messages generated by the custom formatter by passing instances of it to the `generator.add_receiver` method as described in [Configuring message receivers](#configuring-message-receivers).

<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5" version="5" source="FlightInput_5_event" created="2020-10-19T10:10:30Z" timeModeIsUTC="true">
    <action>
        <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24" flightNumber="101">
            <setLegs>
                <setLeg startStation="OSL" endStation="CPH" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-24T07:13:00Z" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-24T08:55:00Z" startTimeOffset="PT1H" endTimeOffset="PT1H" seqNumber="1">

### Flight Input


This chapter describes the standard Flight Input interface that can be used for updating the information about flights stored in JCMS. It supports
updating and maintaining the flight schedule *before* day of operation as well as capturing aircraft movements, diversions, return-to-ramp
events etc. during day of operation. Before this interface was introduced, schedule changes were handled by the Flight Based Schedule Input interface
and day-of-operation changes were handled by the Operational Flight Input interfaces. The new Flight Input interface replaces both these interfaces.
Note that this interface does not replace the Flight Schedule State interface, which is used for initial creation of flights from time tables.

When it comes to changes short before and during operation there will usually be frequent updates to the flight information, capturing the
estimated or actual movements of the aircraft or any disturbances to the planned flow. The picture of clearly identified planned legs is no longer
valid since all atomic events that affect the aircraft, crew and passengers must be taken care of. The JCMS system has a quite pragmatic view on the
leg entities that focuses on the actual events and not on the question which movements or events belong to “the same official leg”. Groupings of
events into legs or flights are only relevant to determine the initial assignment of potential new items to resources - e.g. a return to ramp event
is assigned to the same aircraft and crew as the leg that was attempted. To change crew or equipment before the actual take off of the “main leg” is
then an explicit operational decision. The interface reflects the pragmatic view of leg identity by using the scheduled departure as optional part
of the key (to avoid issues with uniqueness in case of re-routing back to departure airport) and formulating some operations in term of “atoms” rather
than legs.

In general the systems providing flight information are regarded master relative to JCMS and the interface is implemented as publish/subscribe.

The current version of this interface is 5.

[Link to FlightInput\_5.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/FlightInput_5.xsd)

Previous versions of this interface

[Link to FlightInput\_1\_0.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.flight_input_4_0/FlightInput_1_0.xsd)

##### 18.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* updateFlights
  :   Create or update the information for the provided flights. May be used for updating schedule as well as operational flight information (one-way request without any response message).
* updateFlightsWithAck
  :   Create or update the information for the provided flights. May be used for updating schedule as well as operational flight information (with acknowledge response on successful update).
* getFlights (deprecated - please use service FlightState instead [Flight State](flight_state.html#stdif-flight-state))
  :   Get complete flight information as a state for all flights within a given period.

These operations can be used in batch (or periodic) mode to provide sets of updates at once or in online mode
to immediately publish schedule changes when they occur (similar to SSM messages).
In online mode it must be considered that the scope of messages that occur close to each other might overlap;
so normally it is assumed that ordering per flight is relevant when using this interface in online mode (but not in batch mode).
An ‘updateFlights’ request message may contain multiple actions on the same flight as well as on several different flights. All actions
within a message are applied in the order they appear in the xml and they are all committed to the JCMS data model together in one single
transaction.

The interface do not normally check that information arrive in the order that would be expected during normal operation.
It is for example OK to send an actual landing time even though no take off time is present (yet) and the actual departure is accepted
even though a landing is already present. This allows the source system to also send corrected or lacking information later,
e.g. based on manual flight log handling. Any constraints that are implemented are described together with the affected use cases, e.g. for
return to ramp and rescheduling.

Normally, only flights (and legs) that match the keys listed in a message are manipulated by this interface. However, in accordance with the
general semantics of the Standard Interfaces described in [Naming Conventions](introduction.html#stdif-intro-naming-conventions), it is possible to provide flight information
as a complete “state” for creating new flights or replacing existing ones. When replacing an existing flight (i.e. using ‘replaceFlight’ or
‘putFlight’ actions), any leg that exists previously in the data model, but don’t exist in the new provided flight “state”, is marked as
deleted (a state represented internally as *implicitly cancelled*). The interface can of course also be used for explicitly canceling specific flights or individual legs by means of the
‘cancelFlight’ and ‘cancelLeg’ elements respectively.

The interface takes care of already existing assignments of flight legs when changes to the flights are coming in.
Existing assignments are kept even when flights are renamed, and new legs (and operational events) in existing flights are assigned
to the same crew and trips as the original legs.
If a multi-leg flight contained a change of crew, then the system will assume that the change shall happen at the same station as planned
if that station is still touched.

##### 18.2. Supported time modes

The interface supports both UTC and Local Time modes. Each incoming message has a flag ‘timeModeIsUTC’ indicating whether or not
times are specified in the UTC time zone. Internally in JCMS all times are stored in the UTC time zone, so any Local times are
converted to UTC by the interface before storing them in the JCMS model.
There are two aspects of this time conversion that need further clarification:
One is the handling of “day of origin” as part of the flight key.
IATA standard prescribes it to be the UTC day of departure of the first leg; that is not strictly required by the JCMS system.
The value is never interpreted as time-zoned, it is used purely for identification purpose.
As long as all connected systems use the same date to identify the flight it will work, no time-zone conversion for 0:00 UTC is needed.
The other aspect is with the scheduled departure time if a sending system is working completely local time based.
Since the JCMS has its own storage of the time-zone information to be able to fix the data without help from external vendors
there is a risk that the local time offset that the external system uses is not the same as what JCMS has.
That would lead to the fact that the transferred times do not match in local time in reality.
To be able to detect that situation the interface contain optional fields for time-zone offsets for scheduled departure and arrival times.
It is recommended to set these values if the data is transferred from a local-time based system to JCMS.
If the values are provided and if they differ from the values that JCMS has for the same airport at the same UTC time,
then this is regarded as an error and the data is not stored to the database.

##### 18.3. Identification of flights and legs

In JCMS a dated flight is the set of all atoms that share the same IATA flight key (dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix).
A single leg is the set of atoms that share the extended IATA leg key
(dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix, startStation, endStation, scheduledStartTime, scheduledEndTime).
Within each leg the leg\_atom\_number is expected to be unique and the number 0 identifies the “main atom” - performing the actual flight segment.
Other atoms can be Return or Wait events.
During the scheduling phase we do not expect to see any atoms with non-zero atom number.
When looking up a leg for processing the interface always first identifies all atoms of the flight, then filters them with the
matching properties given in the leg element. Although none of the matching properties are strictly mandatory, both stations (if provided)
must be matched identical. Also scheduledStartTime and scheduledEndTime are optional.
If provided, they are used for identification as well but there is an accepted deviation for the provided times to allow for robustness in the
face of rescheduling. Schedule times are however only used for matching in case there are more than one main atom with matching startStation and
endStation. The accepted deviation is not applicable for the ‘addLeg’ action, as it is assumed that if the source system issues an ‘addLeg’
action, the leg should be added, unless there already exist a leg, with the exact same scheduled times. The same logic applies when an existing
flight is replaced by means of issuing ‘replaceFlight’ actions. With the ‘putFlight’ action however, the ‘accepted deviation’ approach is applied
and furthermore the schedule times of the matched leg are updated in accordance with the provided scheduledStartTime/scheduledEndTime.
In case a unique best match cannot be identified based on the provided matching properties, then the leg with the most recent
scheduledStartTime is selected. The reasoning behind that is for operational flight update (MVT/MVA) messages to address the correct leg e.g. in
case of return from airborne scenarios, where a new leg may have been scheduled.

##### 18.4. Rescheduling

For a rescheduling message the original stations must be specified, as a minimum, in order to identify the affected leg.
If a source system is not able to provide these the matching algorithm can be customized to cater for this, for example only using the IATA key.

When rescheduling in the operational time frame, the flag ‘isOperational’ should be specified in order for JCMS to mark the flight leg as
rescheduled in the JCMS model. Legs that get updated departure or arrival stations/times during the scheduling phase are not marked as rescheduled.
If scheduled departure/arrival times are updated, any existing aircraft assignment times are updated too, to reflect the new
schedule times of the leg.

##### 18.5. Renaming flights

When a flight is renamed, the new flight identifier of the renamed leg(s) must not be in conflict with an already existing operating leg with the
same flight identifier.

##### 18.6. Adhoc flight changes

In the context of IATA standard flight messages, an Adhoc Schedule Message (ASM) cannot be modified by a subsequent Standard Schedule Message (SSM)
unless an explicit ASM withdrawal indicator is provided. Furthermore IATA messages provide the possibility to re-instate the original schedule
of a flight, hence accepting any subsequent SSM messages updating that flight without the need to provide the ASM withdrawal indicator.
The standard Flight Input interface supports these mechanisms by means of three flags that may be specified on each flight action in a request message:

* isAdhoc: Indicates that the action is an adhoc change to the flight. Sets the internal adhoc indicator for the flight in the JCMS data model. Default false.
* isAdhocOverride: Indicates that the action should override any previous adhoc change to the flight.
  This flag does not however reset the internal adhoc indicator in the JCMS data model. Default false.
* isAdhocReset: Resets the adhoc indicator for the flight in the JCMS data model. It has precedence over isAhoc if both of them are true.
  Any updates on the flight are carried out according to the content of the message, in addition to resetting the adhoc indicator. Default false.

Note that the blocking of a Flight Input message due to a preceding adhoc change is part of the normal functionality and therefore not handled as an error.

##### 18.7. Adjustment of Flight Times

###### 18.7.1. Adjustment of Arrival Times

If the message contains no estimated or actual departure times, the estimated and actual landing and in-block times will be checked and
adjusted if necessary. If the landing or in-block times are earlier than the best known start time of the leg, they will be increased
in steps of 24 hours until they are later than the start time. This is because some sources are known to have insufficient information
to be able to set the date part of arrival times correctly. This will be the case for the following IATA movement messages, as specified
in the IATA Airport Handling Manual, sections AHM 780 and AHM 781:

> * DIV
> * The following MVA/MVT message subtypes:
>   + Return from Airborne
>   + Revised Estimated Time of Arrival

###### 18.7.2. Calculation of estimated times

If a new actual or estimated time is provided, the interface derives/adjusts all subsequent estimated times.
The same calculation is applied regardless if times are provided from ACARS/ARINC or IATA MVT messages. Note that
for native format messages this feature is switched off by default.
Calculation of an estimated time does not take place if a subsequent estimated time is provided in the message.
Calculation of an estimated time does not take place if a corresponding or subsequent actual time exists or is
provided in the message.

Estimated times are calculated slightly differently depending on whether or not a value already exists in the model:

If an estimated time doesn’t exist, the value is derived based on the best known preceding time and the nominal
difference between these times:

![../_images/est_calculator1.png](../_images/est_calculator1.png)

If an estimated time exists, the value is adjusted based on the delta of provided preceding time:

![../_images/est_calculator2.png](../_images/est_calculator2.png)

In the native format, calculation of estimated times is switched off by default. It can be switched on on a per
message basis by setting attribute `enableEstimatedTimeCalculation` on ‘[\*](#id2)Flight’ element of the message.

###### 18.7.3. Resetting of Internal times

Internal times of a leg is no longer needed when actual times become available.
Thus, the interface removes any Internal times when receiving actual times for a leg.

###### 18.7.4. Resetting of Next Information time

Upon receiving of an actual off-block time, any Next Information time of the flight leg is cleared.

##### 18.8. Aircraft flight assignment locks

The interface respects “tail locks” that may be active for flight legs. As long as a “tail lock” exists for a flight leg, the interface
will suppress any instruction from incoming messages to assign, reassign or deassign the aircraft of the flight leg. If a message contains
other information (in addition to the tail assignment), that information will however be processed as normal.

##### 18.9. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Flight Input standard interface:

* interfaces\_core.%default\_taxi\_out\_time%: Defines default taxi time at departure airport
* interfaces\_core.%default\_taxi\_in\_time%: Defines default taxi time at arrival airport

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline.

##### 18.10. Error Handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most standard interfaces, i.e. to reject a request message if it cannot be
entirely and completely processed. If processing of any flight action fails for whatever reason, an error message is generated and the request is discarded
in its entirety. The following errors can occur when processing a request:

| Error | Response message type | code | subCode | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flight not found | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectNotFound | Flight doesn’t exist in <XXXXXXX> |
| Flight leg not found | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | Leg with context <XXXXXXX> not found |
| Flight is cancelled | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectNotFound | Leg is cancelled in <XXXXXXX> |
| Flight already exists | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectExists | Leg already exists in <XXXXXXX> |
| Invalid departure, arrival or diversion airport specified | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | …, could not find any Airport with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| Invalid aircraft owner or crew employer specified | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | …, could not find any Airline with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| Invalid aircraft type specified | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | …, could not find any AircraftType with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| Invalid aircraft specified | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | …, could not find any Aircraft with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| Invalid delay code specified | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | delay\_code with key ‘%XXX’ not found in <XXXXXX> |
| Invalid schedule times | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid period (XXX -> XXX): scheduled end time is earlier than scheduled start time |
| Invalid schedule times for reschedule | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | FlightInterfaceHandler.reschedule invalid period (XXX -> XXX): scheduled start time is earlier than scheduled end time |
| Attempt to update outside the open plan period | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | StartTime XXX and EndTime XXX for XXXXXX must be within planning period start ‘XXX’ and end ‘XXX’ |
| Flight rename target identifier in conflict with existing leg | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectIllegalUpdate | Rename target (XXXXXX) is already used in <XXXXXX> |
| Return to ramp event missing operational times | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectIllegalUpdate | No operation time found for return event |
| Infeasible time specified for return to ramp leg | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectIllegalUpdate | … best of ACT/EST inBlock, landingTime, takeOfftime, offBlock (XXX) > best of ACT inBlock, landingTime (XXX) |
| Illegal return to ramp leg | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectIllegalUpdate | Cannot create return event XX, existing return events XXX collide in <XXXXXX> |
| Illegal return to ramp leg | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectIllegalUpdate | Cannot create return event XX, no previous return exists in <XXXXXX> |
| Flight leg delay with specified sequence number already exists | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectIllegalUpdate | Cannot create delay XX, existing delay items XXX collide in <XXXXXX> |
| Illegal update on flown leg | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectIllegalUpdate | Cannot XXX a leg with actual times in XX |

##### 18.11. Using IATA flight messages

This interface support receiving IATA flight messages of types SSM, ASM, MVT/MVA and DIV. IATA messages are automatically converted into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface.
The usage of airline name in plain text (DEI 113/114/115) with letter “X” for aircraft owner/cabin crew employer/cockpit crew employer is not supported.
A letter “X” as airline identifier in DEI 2/3/4 is ignored.

###### 18.11.1. Supported message sub-types

The following message sub-types are supported:

| SSM | ASM | MVT/MVA | DIV |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TIM | TIM | AD (Departure message) | DIV |
| NEW | NEW | AA (Arrival message) |  |
| RPL\* | RPL\*\* | ED (Delay message) |  |
| CNL\* | CNL | AD/EO (Delayed take-off message) |  |
| EQT | EQT | AD/RR (Return-to-ramp message) |  |
| CON | CON | FR (Return from Airborne message) |  |
| ADM | RIN | EA (Revised estimated time of arrival message) |  |
|  | RRT | AA/EB (Arrival taxi time variance information message) |  |
|  | FLT |  |  |

`*` An SSM/CNL results in flights being deleted (a state represented internally as *implicitly cancelled*) as opposed to an AMS/CNL which results in a normal cancellation.
:   Also an SSM/RPL may result in flight legs being deleted in case e.g. the routing of a multi-leg flight is changed.

\*\* Note that ASM/RPL is mapped to a ‘putFlight’ action when converted to the internal xml equivalent message. See [Identification of flights and legs](#identification-of-flights-and-legs) for more information on what this means in terms of how existing legs are matched and updated.

###### 18.11.2. ASM/SSM sub-message separation

Separation of sub-messages by means of ‘//’ is supported both when sub-messages are repeated from ASM/SSM Action and from Message Heading. However in the latter
case, all sub-messages must have the same time mode. Furthermore, also for sub-messages repeated from Message Heading, blank line is supported as alternative
separator.

###### 18.11.3. SSM day of operation threshold

There is a threshold for the minimum allowed days between day of operation and the period of imported SSM messages. It is used to safeguard
that incoming SSM messages (also applies to SSIM) do not impact flight legs too close to the day of operation. The default threshold is 7 days.
The minimum value is 1 day, which means schedule changes starting the day after the day of operation can be imported. Schedule changes which
start earlier than that cannot be imported, regardless what the threshold is set to. To change the threshold, change Rave parameter `interfaces_core.ssim_min_days_until_dop_p`.

###### 18.11.4. Support for MVT/MVA correction messages

MVT/MVA messages with a correction (COR) identifier on the first line are handled as any other MVT/MVA messages
except that the ‘eventType’ field is set to ‘COR-MVT’/’COR-MVA’ which allows for customization of the mapping
logic, in case it needs to be differentiated from ordinary MVT/MVA messages.

###### 18.11.5. Identifying the flight in MVT/MVA messages

In IATA MVT/MVA messages the flight date is only given as a day, e.g. 14, without explicitly stating the month or year.
Normally, a message addresses a flight on the current day or a few days in the past. The standard behavior is to select
a flight date, using the given day, such that it is no more than a configurable number of days in the future. In the
core implementation the method `std_interfaces.iata.mvt_parser.MVTParser.max_allowed_days_in_future()` yields **1** for
Departure messages (sub-type = **AD**) and **3** for other MVT/MVA sub-types. See next section for information on how to override this method.

###### 18.11.6. Customization patterns

**Inject custom parsing and mapping logic**

In situations where certain aspects of the core mapping logic needs to be modified, it is possible to subclass any of the core
IATA parsers or mappers classes and override any of their methods. The core IATA classes are available in package **std\_interfaces.iata**, modules are:

* asm\_parser.py
* div\_parser.py
* mvt\_parser.py
* ssm\_parser.py
* asm.py
* div.py
* mvt.py
* ssm.py

The parser classes are:

* ASMParser
* DIVParser
* MVTParser
* SSMParser

The master mapper classes are:

* ASMMapper
* DIVMapper
* MVTMapper
* SSMMapper

Furthermore, for ASM and SSM there are action mapper classes for each type of sub-message, e.g. **ASM\_NEW\_Mapper**, **ASM\_EQT\_Mapper** etc.

Below is an example that illustrates how to customize the mapping logic. The same principles apply also for parser customization. The
only difference is the class and method to override, e.g. in steps 1-2 below it would override class `std_interfaces.iata.asm_parser.ASMParser`
and in step 3 method `get_ASM_Parser()`.

1. In the core mapper (e.g. std\_interfaces.iata.asm.py), identify the method you want to override.
2. Create a subclass of the core action mapper with an implementation of the overridden method.
   E.g. if you want to override how onward flight data is mapped in ASM/NEW messages, create a class that inherits from the core `ASM_NEW_Mapper`
   and implement your version of method `map_onward_flight()`:

```
class MyASM_NEW_Mapper(std_interfaces.iata.asm.ASM_NEW_Mapper):

    def map_onward_flight(self, of, equipment, eqp):
      ...
```

3. Create a subclass of `std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler` and override e.g. class method `get_ASM_mapper()`:

```
class MyFlightInterfaceHandler(std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler):

    @classmethod
    def get_ASM_mapper(cls, service, plan):
        return std_interfaces.iata.asm.ASMMapper(service, plan, NEW=MyASM_NEW_Mapper())
```

4. Override the service mapping to use your custom `MyFlightInterfaceHandler` class for the pre-processor `from_iata`.
   Create a custom mapping, e.g. `$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.ext.flight_input_5/my_mapping.xml` with the following content
   (assuming your custom classes were placed in a module called `mymodule`):

```
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" language="Python" target="air2_mave2">
  <include href="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/mapping.xml"/>
  <server-impl service_name="FlightInput" service_version="5">
    <pre-process name="from_iata" module="mymodule" function="MyFlightInterfaceHandler.from_iata"/>
  </server-impl>
</service-mapping>
```

5. In `$CARMUSR/data/config/ioservice_builder.xml`, make sure your custom `my_mapping.xml` is used by the `FlightInput` service:

```
<ioservice pattern="subscriber" default_exception="TransientMsgError">
  <description>Create/update flight information.</description>
  <smog-service name="FlightInput" version="5" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.ext.flight_input_5/my_mapping.xml"/>
  </smog-service>
</ioservice>
```

**Append custom mapping logic**

In situations where logic needs to be added after each message of a certain IATA type, it is possible to override the pre-defined customization
point method custom\_msg() that is called by the core mapper class after the parsing and mapping of the message is finalized.
This is similar to the previous example except that in this case a subclass is created of the core master mapper, e.g. `std_interfaces.iata.mvt.MVTMapper`.

1. Create a subclass of the core master mapper with an implementation of the `custom_msg()` method, e.g.:

```
class MyMVTMapper(std_interfaces.iata.mvt.MVTMapper):

    def custom_msg(self, inmsg, outmsg):
      ...
```

2. Create a subclass of `std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler` and override e.g. class method `get_MVT_mapper()`:

```
class MyFlightInterfaceHandler(std_interfaces.flight_types_mave2.FlightInterfaceHandler):

    @classmethod
    def get_MVT_mapper(cls, service, plan):
        return MyMVTMapper(service, plan)
```

3. See steps 4. and 5. in the previous example.

###### 18.11.7. Ignored fields in SSM/ASM messages

Some information in the SSM/ASM messages is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is therefore
not passed on to the Flight Input interface.

**Message reference**

* Message Sequence Reference
* Creator Reference

**Flight Information**

* Joint Operation Airline Designators
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share

**Period/Frequency Information**

* Joint Operation Airline Designators
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation

**Equipment Information**

* Passenger Reservations Booking Modifier
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation

**Routing or Leg Information**

* Scheduled Time of Passenger Departure
* Scheduled Time of Passenger Arrival
* Joint Operation Airline Designators
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
* Meal Service Note
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation

**Segment Information**

* Traffic Restriction Note
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Code Share
* Operating Airline Disclosure - Shared Airline or Wet Lease Designation
* Other Segment Information except the following:
  + Duplicate Leg Cross Reference—Duplicate Leg Identification (DEI 10)
  + Passenger Terminal Identifier (DEI 98/99)
  + Passenger Reservations Booking Designator Segment Override (DEI 101)
  + Departure/arrival Passenger Terminals Segment Overrides (DEI 198/199)

**Sub-message Supplementary Information**

* *all fields*

**Supplementary Information for Whole Message**

* *all fields*

**Reject Information**

* *all fields*

**Repeat of Rejected Message**

* *all fields*

###### 18.11.8. Ignored fields in MVT/MVA messages

Some information in the MVT/MVA messages is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is therefore
not passed on to the Flight Input interface.

* Aircraft Registration
* Passenger Information Per Destination
* Reclearance Information
* Crew Report Time
* Movement After Pushback
* Take Off Fuel
* Take Off Weight
* Zero Fuel Weight
* Category of Operation
* Supplementary Information

###### 18.11.9. Ignored fields in DIV messages

Some information in the DIV messages is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is therefore
not passed on to the Flight Input interface.

* Aircraft Registration
* Reason for Diversion
* Number of Passengers on Board
* Supplementary Information

(Even though the message contains some information about a possible continuation, no continuation flight leg will be created.)

##### 18.12. Using ACARS ARINC 620-8 OOOI messages

This interface also supports receiving a subset of the ACARS OOOI messages from the ARINC 620-8 standard. These messages are transmitted by aircrafts on major events,
such as out of gate, off the ground, on the ground and into gate. It is assumed that ACARS messages are provided to this interface from some external source.
The actual transmission of messages via datalink or ground stations are not in the scope of this interface.
The interface automatically interpret supported ACARS messages and converts them into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface.

###### 18.12.1. Supported ACARS messages

The following messages from the ARINC 620-8 standard are currently supported:

| SMI | Label | Description | Remark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ARR | QR | ON Report (ICAO Airport Code) |  |
| ARR | QS | IN Report (ICAO Airport Code) | Captain/first officer identifier (LA) and landing category (LA) TEI items are not supported. |
| DEP | QP | OUT Report (ICAO Airport Code) |  |
| DEP | QQ | OFF Report (ICAO Airport Code) |  |
| RTN | QT | OUT/Return IN report (ICAO Airport Code) |  |

The ARINC standard specifies that the TEI items of a message can be split on multiple lines. This is currently not handled.

###### 18.12.2. Ignoring ACARS messages

The interface contains logic for identifying ACARS messages that might be invalid or redundant
and should be ignored, without doing any updates in JCMS.
The logic is based on the `event time`, `received time` and `now time` of each ACARS message together
with a set of parameters that can be re-configured for each installation.

* `Event time`: Time of the main event in the message, for example the take-off time in an Off message.
* `Received time`: Time message was received by the ACARS server, before being sent to JCMS.
* `Now time`: The current time in JCMS.

| Parameter | Description | Default value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| max\_event\_time\_deviation | `Event time` may not be older than this limit compared to the `received time`. | 08:00 |
| max\_event\_time\_age | `Event time` in messages may not be older than this limit compared to `now time`. | 24:00 |
| lower\_limit\_out\_time | Out time may not be more than this much before the estimated/scheduled departure time. | 02:00 |
| upper\_limit\_out\_time | Out time may not be more than this much after the estimated/scheduled departure time. | 12:00 |
| lower\_limit\_off\_time | Off time may not be more than this much before the latest known offblock time. | 00:00 |
| upper\_limit\_off\_time | Off time may not be more than this much after the latest known offblock time. | 04:00 |
| lower\_limit\_on\_time | On time may not be more than this much before the estimated/scheduled onblock time. | 01:30 |
| upper\_limit\_on\_time | On time may not be more than this much after the estimated/scheduled onblock time. | 03:00 |
| lower\_limit\_in\_time | In time may not be more than this much before the actual landing time. | 00:00 |
| upper\_limit\_in\_time | In time may not be more than this much after the actual landing time. | 05:00 |
| lower\_limit\_return\_time | Return-to-gate time may not be more than this much before the latest known offblock time. | 00:00 |
| upper\_limit\_return\_time | Return-to-gate time may not be more than this much after the latest known offblock time. | 06:00 |

###### 18.12.3. Removal of invalid existing actual times

When receiving actual times from an ACARS OUT, OFF, ON or IN message the interface checks for subsequent existing actual times that
are inconsistent with the provided times. As an example, an existing actual landing time is removed if it is earlier than an actual
takeoff time provided in the ACARS message.

##### 18.13. Using FAA SFDPS messages

This interface supports receiving FAA SFDPS (System-Wide Information Management (SWIM) Flight Data Publication Service)
messages in FIXM format.
The interface automatically interprets supported SFDPS messages and converts them into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface.

###### 18.13.1. Supported FAA SFDPS messages

There are various FAA SFDPS messages defined in FIXM format.
This interface currently supports EDCT (Estimated Departure Controlled Time) messages.

###### 18.13.2. Identifying the flight

Estimated departure time in EDCT message is used for identifying flights in the database. There is a also a time window defined
around estimated departure time when trying to find the matching candidate. If no matching candidate is found, the message is discarded.

###### 18.13.3. Clearing EDCT info

When a cancellation of EDCT is received, the interface clears the previously saved EDCT and set the EDCT status being “cancelled”.

##### 18.14. Use cases for schedule updates

As a starting point for the following use cases we assume that no flight information for the given period is available.
To see the effect of update messages to existing trips, look in the section for operational input.
The result of the operations is described in tabular form as shown below.

* dep = departure airport
* arr = arrival airport
* sobt = scheduled departure time
* sibt = scheduled arrival time
* state = type/status of the flight atom
  + sched : scheduled leg
  + canc : cancelled leg
  + rertd : rerouted leg (changed scheduled arrival station)
  + retim : retimed leg (changed scheduled times)
* tail id = the assigned aircraft

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | ac-type | tail id |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

This section provides examples how typical scheduling situations would be reflected using the flight based communication pattern.
That pattern uses the updateFlights operation and its subtypes, most often “updateFlight”, “setFlight” or “replaceFlight”.
In that case the source system only makes very few assumptions about the previous state in JCMS,
which is most suited for the publish/subscribe style.

###### 18.14.1. Initial load

The initial load provides flight information for a certain scope for the first time. Note that for initial creation of flights
based on a given time table normally the [Flight Schedule State](flight_input_schedule_state.html#stdif-flight-input-schedule-state) interface is used. However, the Flight Input
interface may be better suited in cases where the source system holds each occurrence of a flight as individual objects.
This will normally be for a given time period, so the system will receive a set of messages listing flights
that occur at a certain date or (normally small) date range. For this purpose, the addFlight and putFlight message types would be used.
Special care must be taken for multileg flights if not all legs of the flight are always transferred together
(e.g. if the flight is not falling completely in the provided time period).
In that situation putFlight cannot be used, it would cancel the already transferred leg instead of just adding a new one.
A addFlight message for a flight with an existing leg will fail, so then updateFlight (or setFlight) can be used for the second leg.
Only setFlight can be used to transfer new legs separately for the same flight without relying on the existence of the others.

The following messages all create the same legs:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="FLIGHTSCHEDULE" created="2014-03-14T03:05:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true"
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-05-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T07:40:00" startTimeOffset="PT2H"
                endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T09:05:00" endTimeOffset="PT2H">
          <equipment aircraftType="737" />
        </setLeg>
        <setLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T09:35:00"  startTimeOffset="PT2H"
                endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T10:13:00" endTimeOffset="PT2H">
          <equipment aircraftType="737" />
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="FLIGHTSCHEDULE" created="2014-03-14T03:05:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true"
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <putFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-05-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <leg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T07:40:00" startTimeOffset="PT2H"
           endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T09:05:00" endTimeOffset="PT2H">
           <equipment aircraftType="737" />
      </leg>
      <leg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T09:35:00"  startTimeOffset="PT2H"
           endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T10:13:00" endTimeOffset="PT2H">
           <equipment aircraftType="737" />
      </leg>
    </putFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | ac-type | tail id |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | sched | B747 |  |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched | B747 |  |

Sending legs in separate messages works as above if setFlight is used. In The next example
the legs of same flight are sent in different messages. This works also if the second leg starts
the day after.

First message:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="FLIGHTSCHEDULE" created="2014-03-14T03:05:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true"
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-05-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T21:00:00"  
                endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T23:00:00">
          <equipment aircraftType="737" />
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

Second message:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<updateFlightsRequest
	xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
	source="FLIGHTSCHEDULE" created="2014-03-14T03:05:44" version="5" timeModeIsUTC="true">
  <action>
	<setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-05-14" flightNumber="101">
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="MUC" endStation="GOT" 
                scheduledStartTime="2014-05-15T00:35:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-15T02:35:00">
          <equipment aircraftType="737" />
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

Result:

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | ac-type | tail id |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | FRA | MUC | 14MAY2014 21:00 | 14MAY2014 23:00 | sched | B737 |  |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | MUC | GOT | 15MAY2014 00:30 | 15MAY2014 02:35 | sched | B737 |  |

###### 18.14.2. Cancellation

The following examples show the effect of cancellations.

If the whole flight is cancelled at once all legs in the flight are cancelled.
Any trips containing them become infeasible as they contain NOP (not operational) activities.
A message that contains explicit cancellation of all legs in the flight has the same effect.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="FLIGHTSCHEDULE" created="2014-03-24T07:03:55"
                      version="5"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-05-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <cancelFlight />
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

The trip will look as follows:

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (infeasible) | dep | arr | sobt | sibt |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | NOP |  |
| JJ 202 15MAR2014 | GOT | MUC | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK |  |

If the legs are cancelled one by one, then the change occurs in several steps but the final effect is the same.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="FLIGHTSCHEDULE" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      version="5"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-05-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <cancelLegs>
        <cancelLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T07:40:00" 
                   endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T09:05:00" />
      </cancelLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

The trip will look as follows:

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (infeasible) | dep | arr | sobt | sibt |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | MUC | CPH | 07:13 | 08:55 | NOP |  |
| JJ 101 24MAR2014 | CPH | GOT | 09:30 | 11:05 | OK |  |
| JJ 202 24MAR2014 | GOT | MUC | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK |  |

###### 18.14.3. Rename Flight

The following example shows how to rename a flight.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="SSM" created="2014-03-14T07:21:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="FLT" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="202" >
      <renameFlight flightNumber="210" suffix="Y" />
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id before | flight id after |
| --- | --- |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | JJ 210 Y 14MAR2014 |

###### 18.14.4. Rename Leg

The following example shows how to rename a segment (one or more consecutive legs) of a multileg flight.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="SSM" created="2014-03-14T07:21:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="FLT" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24" flightNumber="101" >
      <renameFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-24" flightNumber="101" suffix="Z" >
        <minorAddition>
          <renameLegs>
            <renameLeg startStation="KRS" endStation="TRD"/>
          </renameLegs>
        </minorAddition>
      </renameFlight>
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight legs before | flight legs after |
| --- | --- |
| JJ101 24MAR2014 OSL-SVG | JJ101 24MAR2014 OSL-SVG |
| JJ101 24MAR2014 SVG-KRS | JJ101 24MAR2014 SVG-KRS |
| JJ101 24MAR2014 KRS-TRD | JJ101Z 24MAR2014 KRS-TRD |

###### 18.14.5. Reschedule Flight Leg

The following example shows how to reschedule a leg in a flight.

We start with a flight which looks like this:

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | ac-type | tail id |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | sched | B747 |  |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched | B747 |  |

Then we apply this message to reschedule one leg.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="FLIGHTSCHEDULE" created="2014-03-14T03:05:44"
                      version="5"
                      eventType="TIM"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-05-14" flightNumber="101">
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="GOT" endStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T07:40:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T09:05:00" startTimeOffset="PT2H" endTimeOffset="PT2H" >
          <reschedule isOperational="false" startStation="ARN" endStation="MUC" scheduledStartTime="2014-05-14T07:46:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-05-14T09:23:00" startTimeOffset="PT2H" endTimeOffset="PT2H" />
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

The flight will now look like this. Note that it is infeasible.

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | ac-type | tail id |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | ARN | MUC | 07:46 | 09:23 | sched | B747 |  |
| JJ 101 14MAY2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched | B747 |  |

##### 18.15. Use cases for operational updates

The base for the following examples is a two-leg flight that has the following state before operation:

* dep = departure airport
* arr = arrival airport
* sobt = scheduled departure time
* sibt = scheduled arrival time
* state = type/status of the flight atom
  + sched : scheduled leg
  + canc : cancelled leg
  + rertd : rerouted leg (changed scheduled arrival station)
  + retim : retimed leg (changed scheduled times)
  + div : diverted (changed effective arrival)
  + ret#n : a return event with atom nuber n
  + wt#n : a wait event (change crew at gate) with atom number n
* earr = effective arrival station
* eobt = estimated offblock time
* eibt = estimated inblock time
* aobt = actual offblock time
* atot = actual take off time
* atol = actual touch down time
* aibt = actual inblock time

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

and is scheduled in a trip like this

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (legal) |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | OK |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | OK |  |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK |  |

###### 18.15.1. State oriented communication

This section provides examples how typical operational situations would be reflected when using a state-oriented communication pattern.
That pattern uses the “setFlight(cancelLeg|setLeg)” messages and provide all available information.
The variation lies in how much information is provided in a single message and examples of this variation are given where relevant.

####### 18.15.1.1. Regular operation

In the regular operation case JCMS receives a flow of updates to the legs that reflect the current state of operation.
The examples show the flow for the first leg GOT-FRA.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="SSM" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="TIM" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
                endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
          <operation>
            <estimatedTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T07:41:00" />
          </operation>
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

####### 18.15.1.2. Return to Ramp

The following flow shows a scenario of return to ramp and crew change at the gate.
We assume that the flight has left the gate (after aobt.xml from the regular example)
The first message describes the intention to return to ramp, this would be communicated while the aircraft is not docked in again yet.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="MVA" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="RR" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
                endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
          <returnLeg  returnNumber="1" >
            <estimatedTimes inBlock="2014-03-14T07:50:00" />
            <actualTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T07:43:00" />
          </returnLeg>
          <operation>
            <estimatedTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T08:05:00" inBlock="2014-03-14T09:28:00" />
          </operation>
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | ret1 | GOT | 07:41 | 07:50 | 07:43 |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | sched |  | 08:05 | 09:28 |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (short conn in FRA) | Assign info shows: |  | | | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | GOT | 07:43 | 07:50 | RET | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 08:05 | 09:28 | OK | GOT | FRA | 08:05 | 09:28 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | OK | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 |

After the aircraft is docked again the return event is updated with actual times.
Since there have not been any actual take-off or landing times this is a ground return.
If we had got the same messages after atot.xml, then the return leg had
inherited this information and we would know its a return to base.

Note that the return number in the message is not matching the atom number in the flight.

Note that only a return at the departure station is considerd a return event of the given leg.
If the aircraft moves at the destination after landing, this is either a return event of the next leg
or it can be handled as a separate operational leg of the current flight if this is the final destination.
The interface applies some chekcs on the provided times to detect this situation and will reject the message in that case.

####### 18.15.1.3. Diversion and rerouting

The following examples show cases of diversion or rerouting.

In the first scenario we assume that the flight has not started yet when the information arrives that a landing in FRA is not possible.
The flight is rerouted (schedule update) through DUS instead.
The trip will be updated to contain the new leg, but cancelled legs are not automatically removed.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="SSM" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="RPL" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <cancelLegs>
        <cancelLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" 
                endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:13:00" />
      </cancelLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
                endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
          <reschedule startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:45:00" 
                      endStation="DUS" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:25:00" isOperational="true" />
        </setLeg>
        <setLeg startStation="DUS" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:55:00" 
                endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:58:00" >
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | DUS | 07:45 | 09:25 | rertd |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | DUS | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (infeasible) | Assign info shows: |  | | | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | DUS | 07:45 | 09:25 | RRT | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | NOP | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | DUS | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 | OK | CGN | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 |

In the next scenario we assume the first leg is not rescheduled but only diverted, the effect on the trip are basically the same.
Whether the change gets applied before or after start only affects the presence of actuals in this case
( and thus there wouldn’t be a new estimated departure )

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="SSM" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="RPL" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <cancelLegs>
        <cancelLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" 
                endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:13:00" />
      </cancelLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
                endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:04:00" >
          <operation effectiveArrivalStation="DUS" >
            <estimatedTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T07:45:00" 
                            inBlock="2014-03-14T09:25:00" />
          </operation>
        </setLeg>
        <setLeg startStation="DUS" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:55:00" 
                endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:58:00" >
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | div | DUS | 07:45 | 09:25 |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | DUS | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

If the information is sent in separate requests, the final result will be the same,
the trip gets infeasible as soon as the first change is handled but the type of the first alert might differ depending on the order of the emssages.
Typically the rerouting of the first leg would come first and break the connection at FRA, the cancellation of the second leg creates a “NOP” and
this is not fixed automatically by insertion of the DUS-MUC leg. The planner will have to remove the FRA-MUC leg manually.

In the next scenario we assume that the flight has started. Sending a reschedule at this point is an error, a started leg cannot be rescheduled.
The rerouting message will have the same effect as in the first scenario, only that the actuals for off block and take off are kept,
so that the update to the estimations doesnt impact the case.
Of course normally we would not expect to get a new estimated off block time for a started flight,
but that is not explicit handled as error since it doesn’t effect the application logic.

####### 18.15.1.4. Cancellation and reinstation

The following examples show the effect of cancellations an reinstations.

If the whole flight is cancelled at once all legs in the flight are cancelled.
Any trips containing them become infeasible as they contain NOP (not operational) activities.
A message that contains explicit cancellation of all legs in the flight would have the same effect.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="SSM" created="2014-03-14T07:03:55"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="CNL" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <cancelFlight reason="HELL_HIWATER" />
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt | cancel\_code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | HELL\_HIWATER |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | HELL\_HIWATER |

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (infeasible) |  | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | NOP |  |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK |  |

If the legs are cancelled one by one, then the change occurs in several steps but the final effect is the same.

                      version="5" >

    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >

        <cancelLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
                endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00"
                reason="SNOW" />

    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>

| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | SNOW |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | OK |  |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK |  |
