Reinstation must explicitly state all legs, an empty setFlight message is will not have any effect.
Assume the current state has both legs cancelled,
then the following messages will restore the flight to its original state.

Reinstate both legs at once:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="ASM" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="RIN" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <reinstateFlight />
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

Reinstantiate the legs separately:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="ASM" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="RIN" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <reinstateLegs>
        <reinstateLeg startStation="GOT" endStation="FRA" />
      </reinstateLegs>
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="ASM" created="2014-03-14T07:05:52"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="RIN" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <reinstateLegs>
        <reinstateLeg startStation="FRA" endStation="MUC" />
      </reinstateLegs>
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

####### 18.15.1.5. Equipment changes

The following examples show some options to provide equipment information for legs. During operation, normally that means providing actual tail names.
In the first of the following messages, a flight is created/updated with its both legs assigned to an aircraft with the registration “LNBRH”.

The difference in behavior only shows when sending several legs at once, in the setLeg case the legs are grouped within the flight,
in the equipment request each leg is its own entity.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="SSM" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="EQT" 
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
      <setLegs>
        <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
                endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
          <equipment aircraft="LNBRH" />
        </setLeg>
        <setLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" 
                endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:13:00" >
          <equipment aircraft="LNBRH" />
        </setLeg>
      </setLegs>
    </setFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

In the second message, the aircraft tail name is updated for all legs in the flight:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/FlightInput/v5"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      timeModeIsUTC="true" 
                      eventType="EQT"
                      version="5" >
  <action>
    <updateFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101">
      <setFlightEquipment aircraft="LNRCZ" />
    </updateFlight>
  </action>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

The original tail assignment will be replaced, as the interface assumes that any leg is always planned to be operated by a single aircraft.

###### 18.15.2. ARINC 620-8 OOOI messages

This section provides examples of using the interface when processing ARINC 620 OOOI messages transmitted by ACARS to JCMS for a flight.

In the regular operation case JCMS receives a flow of ACARS messages for each out of gate, off the ground, on the ground and into gate event occurring for the flight leg.
The examples show the flow for flight leg JJ 101 scheduled on 27MAR2014 between GOT-FRA.

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | eobt | aobt | etot | atot | eldt | aldt | sibt | eibt | aibt | offblock fuel | take-off fuel | landing fuel | inblock fuel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 27MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 10:50 | 10:55 |  | 11:00 |  |  |  | 12:15 | 12:20 |  |  |  |  |  |

Following message is sent by the aircraft when doing pushback from gate.

```
QU ANPOCF9
.DDLXCXA 271101
DEP
FI JJ101/AN LZHTR/DA ESGG/DS EDDF/OT 1100/FB  251/BF      
DT DDL CVG 271101 M06A
-  ,,
```

The actual off block time and fuel is updated in JCMS. Estimated times are adjusted accordingly, reflecting the difference
between the actual time and the estimated time before the message was received. For the landing, there is no estimate so a new estimated
landing time is calculated using the default taxi time. In this example, the default taxi time is 15 minutes.

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | eobt | aobt | etot | atot | eldt | aldt | sibt | eibt | aibt | offblock fuel | take-off fuel | landing fuel | inblock fuel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 27MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 10:50 | 10:55 | 11:00 | 11:05 |  | 12:10 |  | 12:15 | 12:25 |  | 11385 |  |  |  |

Following message is sent by the aircraft when taking off.

```
QU ANPOCF9
.DDLXCXA 271109
DEP
FI JJ101/AN LZHTR/DA ESGG/DS EDDF/OF 1108
DT DDL CVG 271109 M07A
-   250,142112
```

The actual take-off time is updated in JCMS. Estimated landing and in-block times are adjusted.

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | eobt | aobt | etot | atot | eldt | aldt | sibt | eibt | aibt | offblock fuel | take-off fuel | landing fuel | inblock fuel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 27MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 10:50 | 10:55 | 11:00 | 11:05 | 11:08 | 12:13 |  | 12:15 | 12:28 |  | 11385 |  |  |  |

Following message is sent by the aircraft when landing.

```
QU ANPOCF9
.DDLXCXA 271216
ARR
FI JJ101/AN LZHTR/DA ESGG/DS EDDF/ON 1216
DT DDL CVG 271216 M07A
-   ,
```

The actual landing time is updated in JCMS. Estimated in-block time is updated.

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | eobt | aobt | etot | atot | eldt | aldt | sibt | eibt | aibt | offblock fuel | take-off fuel | landing fuel | inblock fuel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 27MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 10:50 | 10:55 | 11:00 | 11:05 | 11:08 | 12:13 | 12:16 | 12:15 | 12:31 |  | 11385 |  |  |  |

Following message is sent by the aircraft at gate or stand arrival.

```
QU ANPOCF9
.DDLXCXA 271232
ARR
FI JJ101/AN LZHTR/DA ESGG/DS EDDF/IN 1232/FB  156/LA  /LR N
DT DDL RSW 271232 M59A
-  O
```

The actual in-block time and fuel is updated in JCMS.

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | eobt | aobt | etot | atot | eldt | aldt | sibt | eibt | aibt | offblock fuel | take-off fuel | landing fuel | inblock fuel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 27MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 10:50 | 10:55 | 11:00 | 11:05 | 11:08 | 12:13 | 12:16 | 12:15 | 12:31 | 12:32 | 11385 |  |  | 7076 |

The aircraft can send ACARS messages for return to gate events in case of irregular operations.
The examples show the flight leg JJ 101 scheduled on 27MAR2014 between GOT-FRA.

| flight id | atom | status | dep | arr | eades | sobt | eobt | aobt | etot | atot | eldt | aldt | sibt | eibt | aibt | offblock fuel | take-off fuel | landing fuel | inblock fuel |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 27MAR2014 | 0 | S | GOT | FRA |  | 10:50 | 10:55 |  | 11:00 |  |  |  | 12:15 | 12:20 |  |  |  |  |  |

There is a technical problem and the aircraft returns to gate. The following ACARS message is sent by the aircraft when returning to gate.

```
QU ANPOCF9
.DDLXCXA 271119
RTN
FI JJ101/AN LZHTR/DA ESGG/DS ----/OT 1100/RI 1119/FB   51
DT DDL PHL 271119 M00A
```

A new return event is created for the flight leg in JCMS with the following values:

| return nr. | sobt | sibt | aobt | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 10:50 | 12:15 | 11:00 | 11:19 |

A return atom is created for the leg and a new atom is created for the continuation leg:

### Flight State


This chapter describes the standard Flight State interface that can be used for retrieving the complete information about flights stored in JCMS.
This interface is strictly leg oriented, i.e. there is nothing in the structure of the messages that tie together individual legs in
multi-leg flights. Consequently, there is no guarantee that all legs in a multi-leg flight are contained in one and the same message.

The interface provides the full state of flight legs in terms of their properties and related entities such as delays, passenger data, flight plan
code shares and return events (as mentioned above). Properties and elements with undefined or non-existing information are output with “null”
values. Null values are represented differently depending on protocol.

Any flight leg instance within the JCMS data model is included, regardless if they are cancelled, code share duplicates or considered non-operational
due to any other reason. However wait-at-gate, return-to-ramp or airborne return events are not represented as flight legs in their own right (even
if stored as flight leg instances internally in the JCMS data model). Also, deleted flight leg instances are not included (internally represented
as *implicitly cancelled*).

The current version of this interface is 1.beta.

[Link to FlightState\_1\_beta.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/FlightState_1_beta.xsd)

##### 19.1. Interface capabilities

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* getFlightsInPeriod
  :   Get complete flight leg information as a state for all flight legs within a given period.
* updateFlights
  :   Only used as client i.e. when producing flight state messages based on a trigger in JCMS (see [Flight State Events](flight_state_events.html#stdif-flight-state-events)).

##### 19.2. Supported time modes

All times are provided in UTC.

##### 19.3. Selection of flight legs

Based on a requested period, the interface responds with all flight legs having scheduled departure time within the period. The period start
time counts as within the period while the end time is considered outside the period. Any flight legs regardless of operational status are included.

##### 19.4. Customization patterns

In general terms, standard techniques for extending SMOG based interfaces apply for adding custom information to the interface or
changing the mapping of existing information in the standard interface. In situations where certain aspects of the core mapping logic needs to
be modified, typically the interface handler **std\_interfaces.flight\_types\_mave2.FlightStateOutputInterfaceHandler** is subclassed in order to
override specific methods, e.g. *find\_legs\_in\_period* for changing which flight legs are extracted based on a requested period.

##### 19.5. IOService builder configuration

Service FlightState version 1.beta:

```
<ioservice pattern="requestresponse">
  <smog-service name="FlightState" version="1.beta" protocol="plainxml|plainjson">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/mapping_requested.xml"/>
  </smog-service>
</ioservice>
```

### Flight State Events


This chapter describes the standard interface for publishing flight leg state information to external systems when changes occur in JCMS to
flight leg properties or related entities such as delays, passenger data, flight plan code shares and return events. One message per flight
leg is published, therefore, since the trigger processes all changes in a *changeset* (a data model refresh cycle), one *changeset* may result
several messages.

The interface is prepared to be used with both *Subscription Management* and *Message Receivers* patterns, see [Interface Implementation Patterns](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-impl-patterns).
It uses the **std\_interfaces.common.NativeProtocolFormatter** as default receiver.

See [IOService builder configuration](#ioservice-builder-config) for an example how to use the *Subscription Management* pattern to set up the interface for a combined
batch/delta feed. Note that when a flight leg is deleted (internally represented with cancel status *implicitly cancelled*) this results in
a change in the delta feed. Deleted flight leg instances are however not included in the batch feed.

##### 20.1. Customization patterns

###### 20.1.1. Configuring message receivers

It’s possible to configure the receivers this interface should use when sending event messages by updating the default SMOG service-mapping
and call the `generator.add_receiver` method.

```
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
  <include href="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/mapping_event.xml"/>

  <output-mapping struct="flight_state.FlightsStateMsg">
    <call name="add_my_custom_receiver" expr="generator.add_receiver('from_ioservice_FlightState_1_event.mycustom', std_interfaces.ext.MyCustomFormatter())"/>
  </output-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

The `generator.add_receiver` method registers a new a receiver for messages on a specific format.
Each receiver is associated with a specific message queue and a formatter that determines the format
and formatting options of the generated messages for that receiver.

The custom formatter should be a subclass of `std_interfaces.common.MessageFormatter` and implement the `format` method.

```
from std_interfaces.common import MessageFormatter

class MyCustomFormatter(MessageFormatter):
    """
    Formatter generating messages containing the flight number of updated flights.
    """

    def format(self, payload, headers):
        """
        @param payload: Request message(s) created by client mapping.
        @type payload:  Smog struct or list of Smog struct
        @param headers: Dictionary of headers passed with the incoming request message
        @type headers:  dict or list of dicts
        @return:        Tuple of two lists of equal length, one with output messages content and one with message header attributes
        @rtype:         (list of string, list of dict)
        """
        :
        return contents, headers
```

### Flight Schedule State


This chapter describes the interface used for importing and exporting complete flight schedules to/from the JCMS.
A complete flight schedule comprises all flights operated by an administrative carrier for a given time period. The schedule itself
is not represented in the JCMS system as a unit of its own right, instead the interface rolls out the schedule and creates a set of
dated flight legs. When importing schedules, the interface is based on the principle that each message corresponds to a single database
transaction. This means that if an error is raised when processing a message, then the whole message is discarded and no flight legs have
been created.

In general the systems providing flight schedule information are regarded master relative to JCMS and the interface is implemented as
publish/subscribe.

The current version of this interface is 4.

[Link to FlightScheduleState\_4.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/FlightScheduleState_4.xsd)

##### 21.1. Interface capabilities

The Flight Schedule State interface is designed for importing schedules in future planning periods. It is not designed for importing
schedules within the operational time window while it doesn’t apply any operational checks on existing flight legs in the plan.
For schedule changes during day of operation please utilize the corresponding capabilities of the [Flight Input](flight_input.html#stdif-flight-input) interface.
The importing of a flight schedule is a state operation which means that any flights already existing in the JCMS data model within
the imported plan period are marked as deleted (a state represented internally as *implicitly cancelled*) if they don’t match any flight in
the imported schedule. By means of a custom *flights layer* (see [Configuration](#stdif-flight-schedule-state-config)) it is possible to restrict
which flights are deleted, thus protecting e.g. flights that have been manually created or have been imported ad-hoc from another source.

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* putFlightScheduleState
  :   Supersede all existing flight information covering schedules for the specified carriers and periods (one-way request without any response message).
* putFlightScheduleStateWithAck
  :   Supersede all existing flight information covering schedules for the specified carriers and periods (with acknowledge response on successful update).
      The acknowledge response message contains a summary describing number of flights that was affected in JCMS by the schedule.
* getFlightScheduleState
  :   Extract a flight schedule for the given carrier and period, optionally filtered by aircraft type and service type.
* getSSIM
  :   Extract a flight schedule on IATA SSIM format for the given carrier and period, optionally filtered by aircraft type and service type.

###### 21.1.1. Supported time modes

The schedules can either be based on UTC time or local time. This is specified separately for each schedule.
Internally, JCMS always stores the arrival and departure times based on UTC. When importing a schedule based on
local time, all times are converted to UTC using the built-in time zone information. Conversely, when exporting
to a schedule based on local time, all times are converted from UTC.

##### 21.2. Importing schedules

The operation putFlightScheduleState replaces existing flights in JCMS with new data according to the flight schedules
defined in the request. Each schedule in the request specifies a number of schedule pattern records (period and weekdays)
during which a certain flight leg should be rolled out.
If a new period is scheduled, all legs are created new in JCMS. If the schedule replaces an already
scheduled period, or if the schedule period partly overlaps a previous schedule, then the interface
finds all existing flights for the carrier, having a scheduled departure date within the period. A flight is considered included
in the schedule period if its scheduled departure date (of the first leg in the flight), in the time mode (UTC or local time)
stated in the schedule, is between the period start date and end date (both start and end date inclusive). It updates the legs of
those flights that are still in the schedule with new information, creates new legs if needed and deletes (implicitly cancels)
legs which are no longer part of the schedule.
If scheduled departure/arrival times are updated, any existing aircraft assignment times are updated too, to reflect the new
schedule times of the leg.

The putFlightScheduleState operation is normally used in batch mode to provide initial or updated schedules for one
or more carriers, for a given period, in a similar way as sending a new IATA SSIM file would.
It is expected that no other updates for the flights in the same scope are coming in close to this batch,
i.e. there are no ordering or concurrency constraints.

###### 21.2.1. Date of Origin schemes

The date of origin (UDOR) for each rolled out flight is by default set to the UTC date of departure
of the first leg in the flight. However, by means of a configuration setting (see below), the behavior
can be changed such that all UDOR’s are based on the local departure date instead.

###### 21.2.2. Time offset checking

All time and date values are written in the UTC time zone. Local time
values are converted to UTC. If there is a mismatch between what the
message says is the time offset for a specific airport and what the
database says for the same airport, then an error is raised. This means that
the whole message is discarded. However, this behavior can be overridden by means of a configuration setting (see below).
By using this configuration feature a log warning message is issued if a
time offset mismatch is detected, and the processing of the message continues.
Time offsets are always checked whenever provided in the message, regardless if the schedule(s) in the incoming request
are based on UTC or local time.

In connection with DST switches, if the system detects that a specified local time departure or arrival time
of a flight leg is ambiguous or missing, then the interface falls back to calculating the UTC
departure/arrival time based on the specified local time and offset. This special case of using the
specified UTC offset only applies if the specified schedule pattern period inly comprises ONE flight leg
instance. If an UTC offset is not explicitly specified for the departure/arrival time in question, or if
the schedule pattern period covers more than one day of operation, then an error is raised.

###### 21.2.3. Data consistency checking

The following checks are made on the data in an incoming request message:

> * No departure of the same flight at the same station on the same date are allowed.
> * No arrival of the same flight at the same station on the same date are allowed.
> * Elements of type ScheduledFlightLegPattern must be grouped by flightNumber in the incoming request.
> * An error is raised and the message is discarded if the scheduledStartTime is after the scheduledEndTime of a rolled
>   out leg (after converting the provided time to UTC, if necessary). Although negative activity durations are technically
>   supported in JCMS, it is enforced that flight legs are scheduled with a positive duration.
> * An error is raised and the message is discarded if the operating airline carrier of a ScheduledFlightLegPattern record
>   differs from the carrier stated in the header.
> * An error is raised and the message is discarded if the period stated in the header is invalid, i.e. if periodStart is
>   after periodEnd.
> * An error is raised and the message is discarded if the period stated in the header starts before a
>   configurable number of days after current day of operation (see [Configuration](#stdif-flight-schedule-state-config)).
>   By default, if not overridden by custom configuration, this “Day of operation threshold” is set to 7 days.
> * A log warning message is issued if a ScheduledFlightLegPattern record doesn’t yield any flight leg instances. This may
>   happen if there are no weekdays in the daysOfOperation field that matches the given period of operation. Note however
>   that no warning or error is issued if there are any “unused” weekdays, i.e. some of the weekdays in the daysOfOperation
>   field don’t exist in the given period.

Note that there is no consistency check of the LegSchedulePeriodPattern period in relation to the period
stated in the header of a given schedule. The period in the header is only used when identifying existing legs and aircraft
rotations for canceling/removal.

###### 21.2.4. Ordering of data

For multi-leg flights, the ScheduledFlightLegPattern records are assumed to be
ordered by leg sequence number. If not, the interface is not able to derive the correct UDOR if UDOR is
not based on the same time mode as the schedule data (see [Configuration](#stdif-flight-schedule-state-config)).
E.g. if the schedule is based on local time but UDOR’s should be calculated based on UTC. If this situation
is detected, the interface will raise an error and reject the message.

###### 21.2.5. Creation of Aircraft Rotations

This capability is disabled by default (see [Configuration](#stdif-flight-schedule-state-config) for how to enable it).
Information in the LegScheduleOnwardFlightData element is used for constructing aircraft rotations in JCMS.
Each schedule in an incoming message is processed separately. For aircraft rotations this means that
an aircraft rotation cannot continue across different schedules. If the onward flight of a leg in one
schedule refers to a flight from another schedule, then the rotation will be discontinued and a new
rotation will begin with the referenced flight.
If the onward information is missing it is assumed that the onward flight reference is identical to the
flight identifier of the ScheduledFlightLegPattern record itself. This is the case for legs in multi-leg
flights (except for the last leg). Aircraft rotations are not written to the model on the fly. After all
ScheduleFlightLegPattern records in a message have been processed and thus all leg instances are
created, then the aircraft rotations are calculated and written to the model. Aircraft rotations only containing
one single leg are not written to the model. When constructing aircraft rotations, the following criteria
must be fulfilled for two legs to be linked to each other in the same aircraft rotation:

> * The two legs must belong to the same schedule
> * The first leg must have an onward reference that matches the flight identifier of the succeeding one
> * The arrival airport of the first leg must be the same as the departure airport of the succeeding one
>   (it is assumed that aircraft rotations never continue over co-located airports)
> * Both legs must have the same planned aircraft type
> * The scheduled end time of the first leg must be less than the scheduled start time of the succeeding one

In addition, if aircraftRotationLayover is specified, then there must be a time gap between the two legs
that corresponds to at least the specified aircraftRotationLayover. If there are several possible
succeeding legs that fulfill these criteria, then the best match is selected, i.e. the leg that gives
a gap that is closest to the specified aircraftRotationLayover.

The interface creates aircraft rotations for the given schedule period isolated. It makes no attempts to
merge with existing aircraft rotations from adjacent or overlapping schedule periods. Therefore, aircraft
rotations may not be correctly represented around borders between different schedule periods, something
that may result in incorrect connection time information when creating trips.

Before writing the aircraft rotations to the model for a given schedule, any existing aircraft rotation
assignments for the given carrier and within the
given schedule period is removed. All existing legs having a scheduled start time inside the period stated
in the header are thus detached from any existing aircraft rotation to which they may belong. After that,
all empty rotation objects having “dt” within the schedule period, are removed.

###### 21.2.6. Importing IATA SSIM Schedule Data Set

This interface support receiving IATA messages of type SSIM. IATA messages are automatically converted into an xml equivalent message
before being handled by the interface. The implementation is based on the IATA Standard Schedules Information Manual issued March 2011.

####### 21.2.6.1. Limitations

The following limitations apply when loading an SSIM message.

> * Record 2 - Period of Schedule Validity must not be valid indefinitely using “00XXX00”.
> * All itineraries of SSIM file are processed, even if they start outside the Period of Schedule Validity
>   as specified in Record 2.
> * No support for using Duplicate Airline Designator Marker in Record 2 combined with stating the
>   identity (name) of the airline as free text in General Information.
> * Code Sharing and Wet Lease Handling in Record 3 are ignored.
> * Record 3 - Period of Operation must not be valid indefinitely using “00XXX00”.
> * Joint Operation Airline Designators in Record 3 are ignored.

####### 21.2.6.2. Ignored fields in SSIM messages

Some information in the SSIM message is not deemed necessary for ops control, crew planning or crew tracking applications and is
therefore not passed on to the Flight Schedule State standard interface:

> * Passenger STD/STA
> * Passenger Reservations Booking Modifier PRBM
> * Meal Service Note
> * Minimum Connecting Time International/Domestic Status
> * Traffic Restriction Code.
> * Traffic Restriction Code Leg Overflow Indicator.
> * Secure Flight Indicator

####### 21.2.6.3. Default values

The following default values are applied in accordance with IATA SSIM appendix H:

| Data Element | Default value |
| --- | --- |
| Aircraft Owner | Airline designator (carrier) of the flight |
| Cabin Crew Employer | Aircraft Owner |
| Cockpit Crew Employer | Aircraft Owner |
| Frequency Rate | Weekly |

####### 21.2.6.4. Segment Data Record - Record Type 4

Except from the following Data Element Identifiers (DEI), the associated Data records are passed on to the Flight Schedule State service as
“additionalInformation”:

* DEI 10 - Duplicate Leg Identification, is mapped to the “codeShare” section of the Flight Schedule State schema.
* DEI 106 - Passenger Reservations Booking Designator Exceeding Maximum length
* DEI 108 - Aircraft Configuration/Version Exceeding Maximum length

####### 21.2.6.5. Configuration (deprecated, only applicable to FlightScheduleState version 3.0)

The transformation is invoked by adding the following uri in the route definition between the end points.

> `jython://std_interfaces_adaptors.camel.SSIM_to_putFlightScheduleStateRequest_3_0`

Example route definition which polls a directory for SSIM file, transforms it to putFlightScheduleState request
and forwards the request to the IO-server:

```
<route id="ssim_flightschedule">
  <from file://ssim/import/"/>
  <to uri="jython://std_interfaces_adaptors.camel.SSIM_to_putFlightScheduleStateRequest_3_0" />
  <to pattern="InOnly" uri="jmsbroker:queue:cmsbroker:inbound.scheduled_based_input"/>
</route>
```

Note that for interface versions newer than 3.0 the transformation step described above is obsolete.

##### 21.3. Exporting schedules

Flight schedules can be extracted from JCMS based on existing flights in the plan. An export request specifies
an operating carrier and a time period as a minimum. As a consequence, if the plan contains flights with different
operating carriers, schedules for the different carriers must be exported separately one at a time. It is also possible
to specify whether the exported schedule should be based on UTC or local time mode. If not specified, UTC is default.
The export request may also optionally specify a list of aircraft types and a list of service types in order to further
filter the extracted flights. For multi-leg flights, the interface only looks at the first leg of the flight to determine
if the flight matches the specified filter.

Export is carried out in a flight centric manner such that also multi-leg flights are always included or excluded in their entirety.
Flights with a scheduled departure date (of the first leg) within the given time period are included, where both the start and end
date of the period count as inclusive. Both the departure date and the time period are related to the specified time mode.
Deleted and cancelled flight legs are not included. Flight legs without any aircraft type or service type specified are also
excluded from export.
Note that there may be cases where a multi-leg flight is included in the exported schedule although parts of the flight stretches
beyond the schedule period. As an example, if a flight consists of two legs, the first departing in the evening the 25:th of March
and the second leg just after midnight on the 26:th of March. If the export request specifies the period end date to be the 25:th
of March then also the second leg of that flight will be represented in the exported schedule, even though its scheduled departure
date is outside the period.

The operation getFlightScheduleState extracts a flight schedule for the given carrier and period, optionally filtered
by aircraft type and service type.

The operation getSSIM extracts a flight schedule on IATA SSIM format for the given carrier and period, optionally
filtered by aircraft type and service type. The Days of Operation pattern specified for each itinerary is always repeated
in weekly intervals throughout the itinerary period. Fortnightly intervals are not used. The SSIM export is rejected if there
exists flights within the exported period that do not have any leg with sequence number 1 or multi-leg flights with inconsistent
routing with respect to their leg sequence numbers and departure/arrival stations.

##### 21.4. Configuration

**UDOR based on UTC or local time**
:   Configures the method for calculating UDOR for scheduled flight legs upon import, i.e. whether UDOR
    of flight legs in JCMS should be based on the UTC date or local date of flight departure.
    Default is UDOR based on UTC date. To change to UDOR based on local date, call class method
    FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.set\_udor\_is\_based\_on\_localtime() from a custom mapping.xml.

**Ignore time zone offset mismatch**
:   Configures if incoming request should be rejected or not when there is a mismatch
    between a provided start/end time offset and the offset that results from the
    JCMS time zone information. Default is to reject incoming request upon mismatch.
    To relax checking time zone offset mismatch, call class method
    FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.set\_ignore\_time\_offset\_mismatch() from a custom mapping.xml.

**Day of operation threshold**
:   Configures the minimum allowed days between day of operation and the start of the time period of an
    imported schedule. It is used to safeguard that incoming SSIM (also applies to SSM) do not impact
    flights too close to the day of operation. The default threshold is 7 days. The minimum value is 1 day,
    which means a schedule starting the day after the day of operation can be imported. A schedule which
    starts earlier than that cannot be imported, regardless what the threshold is set to. To change the
    threshold, change the Rave parameter `interfaces_core.ssim_min_days_until_dop_p`.

**Exclude suffix from flight key**
:   If set to True, suffix is not considered part of the flight key when importing a schedule. This allows the
    interface to handle legs with a given flight number both with and without suffixes as being part of the same
    multileg flight. Default is True, to set to False, call class method
    FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.include\_suffix\_in\_flight\_key() from a custom mapping.xml.

**Override of imported schedule period**
:   It is possible to override the original schedule period stated in the request when importing a schedule,
    e.g. in order to only import a subset of an SSIM file.
    The override is done on a per request basis by specifying message header attributes
    ‘period\_start’ and/or ‘period\_end’ in ISO-8601 (e.g. ‘2021-02-05’) or AbsDate (e.g. ‘5FEB2021’) format, and in
    the same time mode as the imported schedule(s). If the override period does not overlap the original schedule
    period, the override period is ignored and the schedule is imported according to its original period as defined
    in the request.
    If the override period restricts an imported schedule period, the same flight centric logic applies as when
    importing a complete schedule. Therefore, multi-leg flights are either imported in their entirety or not imported
    at all, depending on whether the departure date of the first leg is within the restricted period or not. This
    applies even for multi-leg flights where all legs are not on the same scheduled departure date.
    The same logic applies when deleting existing flights that are not in the imported schedule. Thus if a multi-
    leg flight starts within the period, all legs of that flight will be deleted even if some of the legs depart on
    days beyond the schedule period.
    If an override period extends an imported schedule period (i.e. lower and/or upper boundary stretches beyond
    the schedule period), it doesn’t affect the imported period but it does affect the period in which existing
    flights are deleted if they don’t match any flight in the imported schedule.

**Flights layer**
:   By specifying a flights layer when importing a schedule it is possible to restrict which of the existing flight legs
    are being marked implicitly cancelled if they don’t match any flight leg in the imported schedule. The purpose is to
    protect e.g. flights that have been manually created or have been imported ad-hoc from another source. By default,
    without any layer specified, all existing flight legs within the schedule period and with the same operating carrier
    as the one specified with the imported schedule, are marked implicitly cancelled if they don’t exist in the
    imported schedule.
    A flights layer is specified in message header attribute ‘flights\_layer’ as a comma-separated list of data sources.
    Each data source is the name of the source from which flight legs are created. As an example, specifying
    message header attribute ‘flights\_layer’ with value ‘SSIM’ results in that only existing flight legs originating
    from an SSIM import will be subject to being implicitly cancelled if they don’t match any leg in the imported schedule.
    There exists a number of pre-defined data source id’s in JCMS: ‘ACARS’, ‘SSIM’, ‘SSM’.

**Create AC Rotations**
:   Configures if aircraft rotations should be created.
    Default is disabled. To enable, call class method
    FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.enable\_create\_ac\_rotations() from a custom mapping.xml.

<smog-service name="FlightScheduleState" version="4" protocol="plainxml">
  <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/services.xml"/>
  <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/protocol.xml"/>
  <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_schedule_state_4/mapping.xml"/>
</smog-service>
```

##### 21.5. Use cases

The following paragraph describe specific use cases like:

* the usage of the date varation at departure and at arrival,
* the rollout of the onward flight information.

The use cases is based on an example extracted from the SSIM-2011 Standard Schedules Information Manual specification issued in March 2011.

**SSIM format**

The input file used for this example includes some lines as below:

```
3 XX 12340101J15AUG0615AUG061234567 ATL20002000-0500S LGW09000900+0000S 737         ...          01000000
3 XX 12340102J16AUG0616AUG061234567 LGW10301030+0000S FRA13301330+0100  737         ...          11000000
3 XX 12340103J16AUG0616AUG061234567 FRA16001600+0100  SIN04000400+0800  737  ...  XX  614   ...  12000000
3 XX   010101J15AUG0615AUG061234567 AKL10301030+1200  HNL21152115-1000  777         ...          0A000000
3 XX   010102J14AUG0614AUG061234567 HNL23002300-1000  LAX07000700-0700  777  ...  XX  022   ...  A0000000
```

**Flight\_schedule\_state input format**

The time mode in the input file it Local time.

The input file above shows that the two legs of a multi-leg flight number 0001 can have the following attributes:

> * Leg1 has an arrival in the previous day compared to udor,
>   which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘0’ and at arrival that equals to ‘A’,
> * Leg2 has a departure in the previous day compared to udor
>   which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘A’ and at arrival that equals to ‘0’.

It is shown as well that a multi-leg flight 1234 can create 3 legs with the following attributes:

> * Leg1 has an arrival in the next day compared to udor,
>   which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘0’ and at arrival that equals to ‘1’,
> * Leg2 has a departure and an arrival in the next day compared to udor,
>   which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘1’ and at arrival that equals to ‘1’,
> * Leg3 has a departure on the next day and an arrival 2 days after compared to udor
>   which corresponds in the input SSIM file to a date variation at departure that equals to ‘1’ and at arrival that equals to ‘2’.

The resulting transformation of the SSIM file into a flight schedule state input message is the following:

```

The parser is even compatible with older versions of the SSIM format, where the date variation field was not present. When the date variation field is not present (spaces) is assumed that, if the UTC arrival time is less than the UTC departure time, date variation for the arrival time is set to ‘1’, for arrival the next day.

This use case consists of the loadings of two input files with periods that partially overlap. It assumes that the configuration
have overridden the default disabled creation of ac rotations by calling FlightScheduleInterfaceHandler.enable\_ac\_rotations().

This situation is similar to the boundary of 2 consecutive monthly loading for instance.

#### Use cases

### Flightlog


This chapter describes the interface that can be used for providing flight log data to JCMS from external systems.
Flight log data is used for keeping records of flights pilots have flown. A Flight log record typically
include details of the actual flight times including landing details. This interface can be used for providing
flight log records for operational or training flights (real or simulated).

Using this interface, JCMS can receive flight times (off-block and in-block times) according to the pilot in command of operational flights. These times are normally used for
calculations of crew duty time.

The interface can also be used for providing details on flight events such as take-offs, landings and other flight events that occurred on operational or training flights as well as simulators.
Flight events are typically needed for keeping track of recency rules for upholding certain qualifications, for example low visibility procedures.
Events can be provided to JCMS using two different modes:

* **Flight centric**: Flight events are provided to JCMS per flight (real or simulated).
* **Pilot centric**: Flight events are provided to JCMS per pilot, regardless of flight.

The interface allows systems to provide flight events on either mode depending on the data at hand.

Latest version of this interface is 1.

[Link to Flightlog\_1.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.flightlog_1/Flightlog_1.xsd)

[Link to Flightlog\_1.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.flightlog_1/Flightlog_1.wsdl)

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* setFlightlog
  :   Update flight log related information (one-way request without any response message).
* setFlightlogWithAck
  :   Update flight log related information with acknowledge response on successful update.

##### 22.1. Identification of flights

The interface must be able to identify the concerned flight leg in JCMS when flight log information is provided for a flight leg.
One flight might have multiple operational legs in JCMS, a multi-leg flight, and each leg might consist of multiple atoms due to return to ramps.
The properties of the `leg` element in the request message is used for identifying a unique flight leg atom in JCMS.
The `returnCounter` property of the `leg` element should be used for indicating that the flight log concerns a return to ramp and also what
return to ramp event (starting from 1 if multiple returns has been made).

The concerned flight leg atom must exist in JCMS when flight log data is provided on this interface, which means that aircraft
movement and operational flight messages must have been processed by JCMS before the flight log is provided to this interface for the concerned flight.
The interface ignores flight logs and produce an error response if no unique flight leg atom can be found in JCMS. Existing deleted flight leg instances
(represented internally as *implicitly cancelled*) are ignored and not matched against.

It’s possible to configure the interface to use airline specific logic for matching of flights.

##### 22.2. Identification of simulator activities

The interface must be able to identify the concerned simulator activity in JCMS when flight log information is provided for a simulator activity.
The properties of the `simulator` element in the request message is used for identifying a unique simulator activity in JCMS.

Field `name` is normally used as business key for ground tasks in JCMS. However `name` is not mandatory and does not necessarily have to be
unique, if additional fields are also provided as selection criteria. In order to support systems where `name` is not used, basically any
combination of fields that together uniquely identifies a ground task, is allowed.

Unless `name` is provided, fields `activityType` and `station` must match if provided. Other fields are only used as selection criteria if needed
in order to find a unique match.
If `identifierDate` is used for matching, note that the `identifierDate` of the activity in JCMS is the UTC based date of the start time of
the activity as specified when the activity was first created in JCMS. That means, in case the start time has been updated the current start time
does not necessarily match the `identifierDate`.

The concerned simulator activity must exist in JCMS when flight log data is provided on this interface.
The interface ignores flight logs and produce an error response if no unique simulator activity can be found in JCMS.

It’s possible to configure the interface to use airline specific logic for matching of simulator activities.

##### 22.3. Updating flight log data

The interface can be used for setting or updating individual properties of flight log records in JCMS.
Flight log records in JCMS are only updated with the values provided in the request message.
For example, if a flight log only includes the `inBlock` property in request message JCMS would only
update the in-block time and leave other properties of the flight log record untouched.

##### 22.4. Removing flight log data

Once created in JCMS, flight log information is not typically removed or updated. The interface still supports removal
of flight logs and related events trough usage of the `deleteFlightlog` and `clearEvents` elements in request message.
The main usage of the deleteFlightlog and clearEvents elements is for allowing an external system to provide flight log
data as a state, allowing the flight log records in JCMS to exactly match the provided information of the request message.

##### 22.5. Error handling

If a `flightlog` record contains a `pilotInCommand` that is not assigned to the designated flight leg then that record is discarded
and the interface continues processing the next record.
If the `eventsForFlight` or `eventsForPilot` contains an event for which the `activePilot` is not assigned to the designated activity
or the designated activity is not recognized then that event record is discarded and the interface continues processing the next record.
In all other cases where a pilot, an activity or a catalog data item is not recognized, the entire message is discarded.

##### 22.6. Examples

The following example provides a flight log for flight JJ 123 on the 15th of April including information
on pilot in command, take-off and landing.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-15T12:05:00Z">
    <flightlog offBlock="2016-04-15T07:53:00Z" inBlock="2016-04-15T11:58:00Z" pilotInCommand="123456">
        <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2016-04-15" flightNumber="123"/>
    </flightlog>
    <eventsForFlight>
        <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2016-04-15" flightNumber="123"/>
        <event type="T" eventTime="2016-04-15T08:03:00Z" airport="FRA" activePilot="123456"/>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-15T11:54:00Z" airport="GOT" activePilot="123456"/>
    </eventsForFlight>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

The message below updates the in-block time of the flight log. The off-block time is not changed or removed in JCMS since it’s not provided in the request.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-15T12:05:00Z">
    <flightlog inBlock="2016-04-15T12:05:00Z" pilotInCommand="123456">
        <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2016-04-15" flightNumber="123"/>
    </flightlog>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

Events such as take-off and landings can be updated individually without any `flightlog` element in the request message.
Events are identified by using properties (`type`, `airport`, `eventTime`) as a key for the given flight leg.
JCMS creates a new event record if no existing record in JCMS matches the key.

The following message doesn’t update the `eventTime` of existing landing event (created by the first example request), instead a new event record is created in JCMS.
After processing this message, JCMS contains one take-off record and **two** landing records for this flight leg.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-15T12:05:00Z">
    <eventsForFlight>
        <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2016-04-15" flightNumber="123"/>
        <event type="T" eventTime="2016-04-15T08:03:00Z" airport="FRA" activePilot="123456"/>
        <!--  updated eventTime for the landing event -->
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-15T11:58:00Z" airport="GOT" activePilot="123456"/>
    </eventsForFlight>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

The request message must contain the `clearEvents` element if the intention was to update the eventTime of the existing landing event (instead of creating another landing event).
The `clearEvents` element indicates that existing event records for that flight leg should be removed before adding the events in the request message.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-15T12:05:00Z">
    <eventsForFlight>
        <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2016-04-15" flightNumber="123"/>
        <clearEvents /> <!-- removes existing events for this flight leg before adding new ones-->
        <event type="T" eventTime="2016-04-15T08:03:00Z" airport="FRA" activePilot="123456"/>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-15T11:54:00Z" airport="GOT" activePilot="123456"/>
    </eventsForFlight>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

The `clearEvent` element removes all events that are not also provided in the request message.
The `clearEvent` element can further specify what type of flight log events that should be removed, for instance, only
removing events for a specific period, allowing to keep records that exist in JCMS but is not
provided in the request message.

Below is an example where flight log events are provided for a simulator activity on the 18th of April including information
on pilot in command, take-off and landing.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-18T12:05:00Z">
    <eventsForFlight>
        <simulator name="MD80_XYZ123"/>
        <event type="T" eventTime="2016-04-18T08:03:00Z" airport="FRA" activePilot="987654"/>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-18T11:54:00Z" airport="GOT" activePilot="987654"/>
    </eventsForFlight>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

In the next message another flight log event is added to the simulator activity. The message illustrates alternative ways to specify
the simulator activity associated with the flight log events. In this case the simulator activity can be uniquely identified with the
combination of `identifierDate` and `activityType`.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-18T12:05:00Z">
    <eventsForFlight>
        <simulator startTime="2016-04-18T07:00:00Z" activityType="P8"/>
        <event type="T" eventTime="2016-04-18T08:03:00Z" airport="FRA" activePilot="987654"/>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-18T11:58:00Z" airport="GOT" activePilot="123456"/>
    </eventsForFlight>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

The interface also support the **pilot centric** mode, where events instead are provided per pilot instead of per flight leg.
The example message below provides a landing event performed by a specific pilot.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="TestFlightLog" created="2014-03-01T00:01:00Z">
    <eventsForPilot activePilot="123456">
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-15T08:03:00Z" airport="FRA" equipment="777">
            <simulator name="SIM1"/>
        </event>
    </eventsForPilot>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

The message above adds a new landing events in the flight log for crew member with id “123456”.
As in the flight centric mode, events can be updated individually by using properties (`type`, `airport`, `eventTime`) as a key
for the given pilot.

The crew centric mode also provides the `clearEvents` element for external systems to update events as a state as shown in the example below.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="TestFlightLog" created="2014-03-01T00:01:00Z">
    <eventsForPilot activePilot="123456">
        <!-- all landing events performed by this pilot in April 2016 -->
        <clearEvents removeFrom="2016-04-01T00:00:00Z" removeTo="2016-05-01T00:00:00Z" type="L"/>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-02T08:05:00Z" airport="FRA" equipment="777" visibility="ILS-1">
            <simulator name="SIM1"/>
        </event>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-04T02:29:00Z" airport="GOT" equipment="777">
            <simulator name="SIM1"/>
        </event>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-10T12:17:00Z" airport="FRA" equipment="777" visibility="ILS-2">
            <simulator name="SIM1"/>
        </event>
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-14T06:11:00Z" airport="GOT" equipment="777">
            <simulator name="SIM1"/>
        </event>
    </eventsForPilot>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

##### 22.7. Providing invalid enumeration values in request message

Some values in the request message refer to catalog data defined by various tables in JCMS. Example of such properties
are `visibility`, `equipment` (code of aircraft group) and `airport`. The complete message
is rejected in case of providing enumeration values which doesn’t match the catalog data in JCMS.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-15T12:05:00Z">
    <eventsForFlight>
        <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2016-04-15" flightNumber="123"/>
        <clearEvents type="L"/> <!-- removes existing landing events for this flight leg before adding new ones-->
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-15T11:54:00Z" airport="GOT" activePilot="123456" visibility="ILS-A" />
    </eventsForFlight>
</setFlightlogRequest>
```

The message above provides invalid enumeration value for `visibility` element. The message is rejected and no changes are saved in JCMS.
An error message with the following content is provided as response by the interface

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogFault xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="Flightlog" code="MessageError" subcode="ReferenceNotFound" requestId="1">
  <reason>visibility_type with key 'id=ILS-A' not found in FlightLogEvent.visibility</reason>
  <sourceMessage><![CDATA[<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightlogRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/Flightlog/v1" version="1" source="example" created="2016-04-15T12:05:00Z">
    <eventsForFlight>
        <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2016-04-15" flightNumber="123"/>
        <clearEvents type="L"/> <!-- removes existing landing events for this flight leg before adding new ones-->
        <event type="L" eventTime="2016-04-15T11:54:00Z" airport="GOT" activePilot="123456" visibility="ILS-A" />
    </eventsForFlight>
</setFlightlogRequest>]]></sourceMessage>
</setFlightlogFault>
```

The error message states the reason for rejecting the message. In this case the provided value *ISL-A* for property `visibility`
is not found in JCMS catalog data table `visibility_type`.

<smog-service name="Flightlog" version="1" protocol="plainxml|soap">
  <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flightlog_1/services.xml"/>

### Ground activity input


This chapter describes the interface that can be used for providing information about stationary ground tasks to JCMS from external systems.
Some ground tasks, for example flight simulators and other training activities, are usually planned and maintained by other systems.
This interface provides capabilities for keeping such ground tasks synchronized and up to date in JCMS throughout planning and operational phases.
The interface should only be used for managing ground tasks that can be assigned to one or more crewmembers, for example a simulator training where 3 crewmembers must attend.
The interface **doesn’t** manage assignment of crewmembers to ground tasks, crew assignments are instead managed as part of a crew rostering or crew tracking process.
Personal activities, designated for a specific crewmember, that cannot to be shared or assigned to other crewmembers are typically **not** managed with this interface.
Examples of such personal activities are office duty, medical check-up, vacation, sick leave etc.

Latest version of this interface is 1.

[Link to GroundInput\_1.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.ground_input_1/GroundInput_1.xsd)

[Link to GroundInput\_1.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.ground_input_1/GroundInput_1.wsdl)

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* setCrewGroundTasks
  :   Update ground tasks for crew (one-way request without any response message).
* setCrewGroundTasksWithAck
  :   Update ground tasks for crew with acknowledge response on successful update.

##### 23.1. Ownership of data

It’s important to have a clear data ownership of ground tasks for the involved systems, i.e. what system or process that owns and master
what ground tasks for different planning and operational phases.
The recommendation is that each master system owns ground tasks with specific `activityType` codes.

##### 23.2. Identification of ground tasks

Systems must use a business key as identifier for ground tasks managed with this interface.
The field `name` serves as business key and is used for identifying ground tasks in communication between involved systems.
For ground tasks that are owned or mastered by an external system, the `name` shall contain the business key used by that system.
The business key should be set up in such a way that every key value is be unique, or that it is unique within a certain
time period, like within a calendar year.

##### 23.3. Providing ground tasks as a state

The interface can be used for synchronizing a set of ground tasks for a specific time period.
For example, if all ground tasks with `activityType` *SIM* are mastered by an external system, that system can provide
JCMS with all *SIM* activities for a specific month, year, or planning period. The interface would then create, update or cancel ground
activities in JCMS to match the state of the message provided by the source system.
The time period that can be updated in JCMS is limited by the IOServer data context.
It’s not possible to create ground tasks outside the data context period used by the IOServer.
By using the `<setGroundTask>` element, the ground task is updated if it already exists else it is created.
A state update is achieved by combining `<clearGroundTasks>` (see below) and `<setGroundTask>` elements in the same *setCrewGroundTasks* operation,
providing `<setGroundTask>` elements for all ground tasks matching the periods and activity types given in `<clearGroundTasks>`.

##### 23.4. Updating a specific ground task

The interface can be used for setting or updating individual properties of existing ground tasks in JCMS by using the `<updateGroundTask>` element.
Ground tasks in JCMS are only updated with the values provided in the request message.
For example, if a an `<updateGroundTask>` element only includes the `startTime` property JCMS would only
update the start time and leave other properties of the ground task untouched.
An error is raised if the ground task specified by the `<updateGroundTask>` element is not found in JCMS.

##### 23.5. Removing ground tasks

It’s possible to remove all ground tasks with a specific `activityType` and starting within a specific time period by using the `<clearGroundTasks>` element.
Only ground tasks within the IOServer data context can be removed, i.e. if the specified period stretches beyond the IOServer data context then any task starting
outside the data context period are left untouched.
The interface does not actually delete or remove any ground tasks in JCMS. Instead the ground tasks change status to *Cancelled*.

The `<updateGroundTask>` element can be used for removing (cancelling) individual ground tasks by providing the property `isCancelled` as *true*.

##### 23.6. Examples

The following example illustrates how an external source system can provide all ground tasks with activityType *R3* and *SIM* starting within October as a complete state.
The `<clearGroundTasks>` element is used for clearing all existing ground tasks starting at or after 2016-10-01T00:00:00Z but before 2016-11-01T00:00:00Z.

The complete state of each ground task is then provided in a separate `<setGroundTask>` element within same message.
A real message would potentially contain hundreds of ground tasks depending on the period and data being managed.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1" version="1" source="TMS" created="2016-10-15T12:32:55Z">
    <!-- Remove all ground tasks between October 01 and October 10 and replace with the ground tasks listed below.-->
    <clearGroundTasks removeFrom="2016-10-01T00:00:00Z" removeTo="2016-11-01T00:00:00Z">
        <type>R3</type>
        <type>SIM</type>
    </clearGroundTasks>

    <!-- Provide all ground tasks with activity type 'R3' and 'SIM' between October 01 and October 10 -->
    <setGroundTask name="AVD-OCT19#1" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-02T10:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-02T16:00:00Z" venue="Aniara">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="1"/>
            <position name="FP" count="1"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>AVD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="ALD-OCT19#10" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-03T06:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-03T12:00:00Z" venue="Carmen">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="2"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>ALD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="DDA-OCT19#7" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-04T11:15:00Z" endTime="2016-10-04T15:30:00Z" venue="Figaro">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="2"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>DDA</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="PPD-OCT19#5" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-15T17:45:00Z" endTime="2016-10-15T22:00:00Z" venue="Carmen">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="1"/>
            <position name="FP" count="2"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>PPD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="AACC-OCT19#6" type="R3" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-10T11:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-10T17:00:00Z" venue="La Traviata">
        <need>
            <position name="AP" count="20"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>MRE-737</trainingTag>
     </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="AACC-OCT19#3" type="R3" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-15T09:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-15T12:00:00Z" venue="Isolde">
        <need>
            <position name="AP" count="20"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>MRE-737</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="AACC-OCT19#4" type="R3" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-03T08:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-03T13:00:00Z" venue="Isolde">
        <need>
            <position name="AP" count="20"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>MRE-2-737</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="AACC-OCT19#2" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-20T15:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-20T19:00:00Z" venue="Carmen">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="2"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>MRE-2-737</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
</setCrewGroundTasksRequest>
```

JCMS now contains the following ground tasks with activityType *R3* and *SIM* for October.

| Name | start | end | type | station | venue | cancelled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AVD-OCT19#1 | Oct02 10:00 | Oct02 16:00 | SIM | GOT | Aniara | false |
| ALD-OCT19#10 | Oct03 06:00 | Oct03 12:00 | SIM | GOT | Carmen | false |
| AACC-OCT19#4 | Oct03 08:00 | Oct03 13:00 | R3 | GOT | Isolde | false |
| DDA-OCT19#7 | Oct04 11:15 | Oct04 15:30 | SIM | GOT | Figaro | false |
| AACC-OCT19#6 | Oct10 11:00 | Oct10 17:00 | R3 | GOT | La Traviata | false |
| AACC-OCT19#3 | Oct15 09:00 | Oct15 12:00 | R3 | GOT | Isolde | false |
| PPD-OCT19#5 | Oct15 17:45 | Oct15 22:00 | SIM | GOT | Carmen | false |
| AACC-OCT19#2 | Oct20 15:00 | Oct20 19:00 | SIM | GOT | Carmen | false |

Assuming some ground tasks have been updated in the source system and another message is being sent to JCMS.
The example message below is provided for synchronizing ground tasks with activityType *R3* and *SIM* in JCMS starting within October 1 and October 10.

The message contain the following differences compared with previous message:

* The `<clearGroundTasks>` uses the period 2016-10-01T00:00:00Z to 2016-11-01T00:00:00Z since that’s the period the source system is providing in this message.
* Ground task *AVD-OCT19#1* has same state as in previous message.
* Ground task *ALD-OCT19#10* has no venue information.
* Ground task *DDA-OCT19#7* is not provided by any `<setGroundTask>` element.
* Ground task *ALD-OCT19#15* is new and is provided by a new `<setGroundTask>` element.
* Ground task *AACC-OCT19#4* has been rescheduled from October 03 to October 05.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1" version="1" source="TMS" created="2016-10-15T12:32:55Z">

    <!-- Remove all ground tasks for October with the listed activity types before adding the ones below.-->
    <clearGroundTasks removeFrom="2016-10-01T00:00:00" removeTo="2016-10-10T00:00:00">
        <type>R3</type>
        <type>SIM</type>
    </clearGroundTasks>

    <!-- Provide all ground tasks with activity type 'R3' and 'SIM' for October -->
    <setGroundTask name="AVD-OCT19#1" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-02T10:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-02T16:00:00Z" venue="Aniara">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="1"/>
            <position name="FP" count="1"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>AVD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="ALD-OCT19#10" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-03T06:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-03T12:00:00Z">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="2"/>
            <position name="FP" count="1"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>ALD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="AACC-OCT19#4" type="R3" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-05T08:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-05T13:00:00Z" venue="La Traviata">
        <need>
            <position name="AP" count="20"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>MRE-2-737</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
    <setGroundTask name="ALD-OCT19#15" type="SIM" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-08T10:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-08T14:00:00Z" venue="Carmen">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="1"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>MTR-ALD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
</setCrewGroundTasksRequest>
```

JCMS now contains the following ground tasks with activityType *R3* and *SIM* for October.

| Name | start | end | type | station | venue | cancelled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AVD-OCT19#1 | Oct02 10:00 | Oct02 16:00 | SIM | GOT | Aniara | false |
| ALD-OCT19#10 | Oct03 06:00 | Oct03 12:00 | SIM | GOT |  | false |
| AACC-OCT19#4 | Oct05 08:00 | Oct05 13:00 | R3 | GOT | Isolde | false |
| DDA-OCT19#7 | Oct04 11:15 | Oct04 15:30 | SIM | GOT | Figaro | true |
| ALD-OCT19#15 | Oct08 10:00 | Oct08 14:00 | SIM | GOT | Carmen | false |
| AACC-OCT19#6 | Oct10 11:00 | Oct10 17:00 | R3 | GOT | La Traviata | false |
| AACC-OCT19#3 | Oct15 09:00 | Oct15 12:00 | R3 | GOT | Isolde | false |
| PPD-OCT19#5 | Oct15 17:45 | Oct15 22:00 | SIM | GOT | Carmen | false |
| AACC-OCT19#2 | Oct20 15:00 | Oct20 19:00 | SIM | GOT | Carmen | false |

The ground task “DDA-OCT19#7” becomes cancelled in JCMS since no ground task with that name
was provided in the message. Other ground tasks starting at or after October 10 are not or updated since
they where not part of the message.

The `<updateGroundTask>` element can be used for updating properties of specific ground tasks.
The example message below can be sent from the source system for updating the `venue` property of ground task *ALD-OCT19#10*.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1" version="1" source="TMS" created="2016-10-15T12:32:55Z">
    <updateGroundTask name="ALD-OCT19#10" venue="Aniara"/>
</setCrewGroundTasksRequest>
```

The venue is updated for ground task with name *ALD-OCT19#10*.

| Name | start | end | type | station | venue | cancelled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ALD-OCT19#10 | Oct 03 06:00 | Oct 03 12:00 | SIM | GOT | Aniara | false |

The `<updateGroundTask>` element can also be used for cancelling specific ground tasks. The example
message below can be sent by a source system for indicating that ground task *ALD-OCT19#10* has been cancelled.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1" version="1" source="TMS" created="2016-10-15T12:32:55Z">
    <updateGroundTask name="ALD-OCT19#10" isCancelled="true"/>
</setCrewGroundTasksRequest>
```

Ground task with name *ALD-OCT19#10* is now cancelled in JCMS.

| Name | start | end | type | station | venue | cancelled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ALD-OCT19#10 | Oct 03 06:00 | Oct 03 12:00 | SIM | GOT | Aniara | true |

##### 23.7. Providing invalid enumeration values in request message

Some values in the request message refer to catalog data defined by various tables in JCMS. Example of such properties
are `type` and `station`. The complete message
is rejected in case of providing enumeration values which doesn’t match the catalog data in JCMS.

The default configuration of this interface is to automatically create new types for `trainingTag`.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1" version="1" source="TMS" created="2016-10-15T12:32:55Z">
    <setGroundTask name="AVD-OCT19#1" type="GND-TRNG" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-02T10:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-02T16:00:00Z" venue="Aniara">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="1"/>
            <position name="FP" count="1"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>AVD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
</setCrewGroundTasksRequest>
```

The message above provides invalid enumeration value for `type` element. The message is rejected and no changes are saved in JCMS.
A fault message with the following content is provided as response by the interface.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setCrewGroundTasksFault xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1" version="1" source="GroundInput" code="MessageError" subcode="ReferenceNotFound" requestId="1">
  <reason>GroundTask.type, could not find any GroundActivityType with key '('GND-TRNG',)'</reason>
  <sourceMessage><![CDATA[<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<setCrewGroundTasksRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/GroundInput/v1" version="1" source="TMS" created="2016-10-15T12:32:55Z">
    <setGroundTask name="AVD-OCT19#1" type="GND-TRNG" station="GOT" startTime="2016-10-02T10:00:00Z" endTime="2016-10-02T16:00:00Z" venue="Aniara">
        <need>
            <position name="FC" count="1"/>
            <position name="FP" count="1"/>
            <position name="TR" count="1"/>
        </need>
        <trainingTag>AVD</trainingTag>
    </setGroundTask>
</setCrewGroundTasksRequest>
]]></sourceMessage>
</setCrewGroundTasksFault>
```

The fault message states the reason for rejecting the message. In this case the provided value *GND-TRNG* for property `type`
is not found in JCMS catalog data table `GroundActivityType`.
