### Plan synchronization


This chapter describes the JCMS standard interface that can be used for synchronizing the state (snapshot) of a complete plan
(rosters, trips, flights etc. for a certain period) in JCMS with external systems.
The interface is used for both importing/exporting the state of a plan to/from JCMS. Synchronization typically occurs periodically, for example
the plan from the tracking system might be synchronized on a daily bases to a rostering system as carry-in data,
while the plan from a roster system might be synchronized on a monthly basis to the tracking system when rosters are published.
This interface is intended to be used for synchronizing the full state of a complete plan (or a well defined sub set of a plan) and can not
be used for synchronizing delta changes or changes of individual planning entities, for instance a change to a specific flight, trip or a roster.
It is however possible to import individual rosters by using import option ‘scope\_rosters\_crewid’ (see [Import options](#stdif-plan-synch-import-options)).
The interface is bidirectional and uses the same message format for importing/exporting data to/from JCMS.

The current version of this interface is 3.

[Link to PlanSync\_3.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.plansync_3/PlanSync_3.xsd)

Previous versions of this interface

[Link to PlanSync\_2.xsd (version 2)](contract/std_interfaces.plansync_2/PlanSync_2.xsd)

[Link to PlanSync\_1\_0.xsd (version 1.0)](contract/std_interfaces.plansync_1_0/PlanSync_1_0.xsd)

##### 24.1. Interface capabilities

The interface can export the current state of the live plan from JCMS to a message, which external systems can consume for synchronizing the plan.
It can also import a message from external system into the live plan in JCMS. The message contains the following planning entities for describing the plan:

* **Flight legs**

  Carries basic flight leg properties (departure/arrival airports, scheduled/operational times, etc.),
  including return-to-ramp, wait-at-gate and other flight duty related events for all (non-deleted) leg instances.
* **Tasks**

  Carries information for representation of various stationary activities that doesn’t involve flying but must be planned,
  for example personal activities (vacation, sick leave, etc.), ground tasks (simulator training, stand-by, etc.).
  A task can optionally have a crew need, specifying the number of crew positions required for performing the activity.
  In general, all ground tasks have a crew need, while personal activities don’t. Personal activities should not be included in any trips, but assigned directly to the crew member while ground tasks should be included in trips.
  Each activity must have a code that describes the type of activity, i.e. what kind of training, standby, office duty, etc.,
  the task represents. It’s recommended that the activity type codes are shared between the systems that are synchronized, but it’s possible
  to configure custom specific mapping of activity types as part of an implementation project (see also [Catalog data](#stdif-plan-synch-catalog-data)).

  > + A ground task is “wrapped” inside a trip internally in JCMS, and the crew member is assigned to the wrapper trip instead of to the activity
  >   directly. The interface creates the wrapper trip automatically for ground tasks.
  > + A personal activity is directly assigned to the crew member without being “wrapped” inside a trip.
* **Ground transports**
  Represents ground transport activities for crew (taxi, bus, train, shuttle etc.) that doesn’t involve flying. Ground transport activities are always
  included in trips and can not be assigned directly to a roster.
* **Trips**

  Basic representation of the crew pairings in the plan. This entity contains a list of activities (flight legs, ground tasks and ground transports)
  that makes up the pairing. Derived values, such as duty start, report times, rest time before/after etc. are not included since it’s assumed that
  each system can derive these values separately.
  The interface requires each trip to have a unique business key
  which is known by the systems that are synchronized. The business key is used for matching trips when importing a message.
  The business key to use can be configured, see [Matching of Planning Objects](introduction.html#stdif-intro-matching-objects) for default behavior.
* **Rosters**

  Basic representation of crew member rosters. This entity contains a list of the trips and tasks assigned
  to the crew member.

The plan in a message is always fully self contained, i.e. if the message contains a trip entity with five legs, it must also contain all five
flight leg entities in that trip. Likewise, all trips referenced from all rosters in a message must also be contained in the message.

The interface is not intended to be used for synchronizing crew data (addresses, passports, qualifications, etc.).
As with all standard interfaces, it’s possible to add or extend the message format with additional planning entities by configuration
as part of an implementation project.

Available operations are:

* **loadPlan**
  :   Updates the plan in the data model in JCMS with information from the provided message. Additional import options can be specified as message headers
      for defining the import scope, detailing what information in data model that should be synchronized (see [Import options](#stdif-plan-synch-import-options)).
      The provided message might contain more information than actually is being updated in the data model.
      This operation returns a response message providing the status of the import, i.e. if the import was successful or not, how many objects that were
      created, updated or deleted in the data model. The whole message is always rejected and no changes are applied to the JCMS data model if the import
      fails.
* **getPlanState**
  :   Exports the plan from the data model in JCMS for a given time period. Additional export options can be specified as message headers for
      defining the export scope, detailing what information in data model that should be exported.
      This operation returns a message which can be processed by the **loadPlan** operation.

##### 24.2. Catalog data

The plan data sent through this interface contains references to Catalog data (a.k.a Master data). However the interface doesn’t provide any
mechanism for synchronizing the catalog data itself between JCTE and the external system. Processes need to be established for keeping catalog
data up-to-date between systems but that is outside the scope of the interface itself. Also, the interface doesn’t contain any standard support
for translating catalog data between systems. Should such translation or mapping be needed as part of an implementation project, it is recommended
to be implemented in the adaptors of the external system, preferably in a way that can be shared and reused between the sending and receiving
adaptors.

The following catalog data is used:

* Activity type codes
* Activity group codes
* Roster assignment Roles
* Airlines (normally IATA or ICAO codes)
* Airports (normally IATA or ICAO codes)
* Trip categories\*
* Crew homebases
* Aircraft types (normally IATA or ICAO codes)
* Crew categories
* Activity training types\* (training tags for flight legs and ground tasks)
* Trip training types\* (training tags for trips)
* Crew assignment training types\* (training tags specific for crew members assigned to a certain trip or activity)
* Crew assignment tag types\* (roster tags used to indicate some additional information on a crew assignment)

[\*](#id1)Note that trip categories, training types and crew assignment tag types are optional properties in the JCMS data model
and thus only relevant for the interface if such data is actually used in a specific implementation project.

When exporting Tasks, additional attributes describing whether is is a personal activity, on-duty or a transport, are also exported.
These are defined in the Activity group codes catalog data.

##### 24.3. Supported time modes

The interface supports only UTC time mode. All times in the message must be in UTC time zone.

##### 24.4. Importing a plan

When importing a plan, the data model in JCMS is updated to match the planning entities in a given message.
Changes are only applied for the specified time period, defining the period scope of the import.
By providing additional options, it’s possible to further detail the scope of the import. This means it is possible
to control what planning entities in the JCMS data model that should be synchronized when importing a given message,
e.g. to only import rosters for a certain crew category.

Entities in JCMS data model are either created, updated, deleted or left unchanged when importing a plan. It’s important that
entities in the data model and entities in the message can be matched by the interface in order to decide whether a specific
entity should be created, updated, deleted or remain unchanged in JCMS data model. See sections below for for further details
on matching of planning entities.

###### 24.4.1. Import options

The following options apply when importing a given message in JCMS. Some options control the scope of the imported data,
others control the way the imported plan data is synchronized with existing plan data in the data model.
If more than one scope option is specified a logical AND is applied to define a resulting scope.
Additional options for further detailing the import scope, can be added as part of an implementation project.

| Option | Description | Default value | Comment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| scope\_period\_start | Optional. Defines the period start of data to be imported from message to data model. Activities and assignments starting at or after this value are imported from message to data model. | periodStart defined in message | Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g. ‘2017-03-01T00:00:00Z’, ‘01MAR2017 00:00’. Import fails if the scope period doesn’t overlap with the period defined in the message. |
| scope\_period\_end | Optional. Defines the period end of data to be imported from message to data model. Activities and assignments starting before this value are imported from message to data model. | periodEnd defined in message | Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g. ‘2017-03-01T00:00:00Z’, ‘01MAR2017 00:00’. Import fails if the scope period doesn’t overlap with the period defined in the message. |
| scope\_homebase | Optional. Defines the rosters/trips to be imported from message to data model by homebase. Don’t consider homebase if value is empty. | empty | Homebase code, e.g. ‘ZHR’ or ‘GNV’. Fails if the data model doesn’t contain the specified homebase. Homebase in data model is used for deciding if roster/trip should be imported or not. Criterion for importing a roster is that crew is based at the provided homebase at any time of the scope-period. Criterion for importing a trip is that the trip’s homeBase property matches the specified homebase. A crew’s roster is imported for the full scope-period even if crew is based at the provided homebase for a part of the scope-period. |
| scope\_crewcategory | Optional. Defines the rosters/trips to be imported from message to data model by crew category. Don’t consider crew category if value is empty. | empty | Crew category code, e.g. ‘COC’ or ‘CAB’ Fails if the data model doesn’t contain the provided crew category. Crew category in data model is used for deciding if roster/trip should be imported or not. Criterion for importing a roster is that crew belongs to the provided category at any time of the scope-period. When applied to a trip, crewcategory is derived from the trip’s crew complement. A crew’s roster is imported for the full scope-period even if crew belongs to the provided category for a part of the scope-period. |
| scope\_planning\_area (added in version 3) | Optional. Specifies a planning area that the imported data belongs to. For each imported roster Rave is queried about which time window should be updated (i.e. during which part of the scope-period the crew member belongs to the planning area). The returned time window is then used as scope-period when importing the crew members roster. Multiple sub-periods is not supported, i.e. crew may not switch back and forth between planning areas within the same planning period. | empty | Planning area name, e.g. ‘FD\_737’ Planning area is a pure Rave calculated property of a roster or trip, representing an arbitrary partitioning of a plan. This feature thus enables importing plan data for different planning areas independently from each other. The provided import data defines the state of the plan for the specified planning area within a certain period (see Description) therefore no filtering is carried out on the imported data w.r.t. planning area. N.B. A roster/trip may belong to more than one planning area. |
| scope\_rosters | Optional. Specifies whether or not to import rosters. | true | By setting this option to ‘false’, any rosters in the message are ignored and only trips are synchronized. If set to ‘false’, the scope parameters control the subset of trips being imported/synchronized. |
| scope\_rosters\_crewid | Optional. Defines specific rosters to be imported from message to data model by crewId. This option is ignored if ‘scope-rosters’ is ‘false’. | empty | Comma separates string of crewIds, e.g. ‘12345, 23423, 43534’. Fails if the message doesn’t contain the provided crewIds. |
| create\_flightlegs\_operational | Optional. Whether missing flight legs should be created as operational or not in the data model. A flight leg is missing if it exists in the message but doesn’t match any flight leg in the data model. | false | ‘true’ or ‘false’ By default, missing flight legs are created as non-operational (operational status N) and are annotated with the text “Missing when importing plan <name>” for providing additional information why leg is cancelled. By setting this option to ‘true’, missing legs are instead created as operational with normal scheduled status. |
| delete\_trips | Optional. Whether to delete trips, inside the given scope, that exists in the data model but not in the message. | true | ‘true’ or ‘false’. A trip is only deleted from model if it is not assigned to any roster. |
| update\_carryin\_trips | Optional. Whether carry-in trips and roster assignments to such trips should be updated or not. | false | ‘true’ or ‘false’. Carry-in trips are trips overlapping *scope\_period\_start*. |
| delete\_assignments | Optional. Whether to delete assignments, inside the given scope-period, that exists in the data model but not in the message. This means that assignments for crew not in the message will be deleted. | false | ‘true’ or ‘false’. Assignments for all crew NOT in the message will be deleted, for the given scope-period. Even personal activities for these assignments will be deleted. Locked assignments will be removed, also for obsolete assignments, for crew in the message. |
| delete\_orphan\_tasks | Optional. Whether to delete personal activities and ground transports inside the given period, that exists in the data model but not in the message. | true | ‘true’ or ‘false’. An activity is only deleted from model if it is not assigned to any trip or roster. Ground tasks (ground duties) are never removed. |
| allow\_missing\_rosters | Optional. Whether the import should allow missing rosters (crew members) or not. A roster is missing if it exists in the message but not in the data model. This option should only be used for test purposes. In a production environment a feed should normally be rejected if a roster cannot be imported. | false | All missing crew members are always detected and reported in response message. The import fails when this option is false and crew members are missing in the model. |
| check\_plan\_period | Optional. Whether the import should be rejected if the import scope period is partly or fully outside the IOserver plan period. This option must NEVER be set to false in a production system. | true | The import fails when this option is true and the import scope period is not completely enclosed in the plan period loaded in the IOServer. The purpose of disabling this data range check is to populate historical roster data into an empty plan as an initial step in commissioning a JCMS system. |
| allow\_missing\_training\_tags (added in version 3) | Optional. Whether the import should allow missing types for training tags or not. A type is missing if a training tag in the message does not exist in the data model | false | ‘true’ or ‘false’ Import fails if message contains missing types for training tags when this option is ‘false’. New types for training tags are automatically added to data model if this option is ‘true’. |
| update\_activity\_training\_tags (added in version 3) | Optional. Whether training tags for trips, flight legs and ground tasks in data model should be updated to match the training tags in the message. Training tags for crew-assignment are not effected by this option. | true | ‘true’ or ‘false’ Activity training tags in the data model are updated to match the training tags provided in message when this option is ‘true’. This means that existing training tags are removed from activities in the data model if none are provided in the message. The purpose of this options is to keep training for activities in the model as they are, even if none are provided in the message. |

###### 24.4.2. Synchronization of flight legs

Flight legs are matched by the extended IATA leg key (dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix, startStation, endStation) plus eventNumber.
Existing deleted flight leg instances (represented internally as *implicitly cancelled*) are ignored and not matched against.
If no match is found using this key, an extended match is made allowing some time deviation (1 hour by default) for the scheduled times.
The default time deviation is defined as class variable `scheduledTimesMatchSlack` in `std_interfaces.common.RequestHolder`, available
for override if needed.
JCMS is assumed to be the one of the two synchronized systems that holds the most recent state of flight legs. As a consequence, existing
flight legs in JCMS are not updated if schedule times or other attributes differ from the corresponding flight leg in the message. Nevertheless,
for various reasons, the external system may contain flight activities that were not included in the original flight plan. Therefore,
JCMS will create such missing flight legs and by default mark them as ‘non operational’ (operational status ‘N’).
If a carrier in a Flight leg is not in own\_carrier, is treated as OAG flights, and AirTransport is matched/created instead of a FlightLeg. The own\_carrier
is defined by Rave definitions, see [Rave definitions](#rave-definitions). If an AirTransport was created from the interface, it will not be removed by the interface,
even though a new load without the FlightLeg not matching own\_carier is made for the same period.
Only flight legs referenced by trips within the import scope, are synchronized.

###### 24.4.3. Synchronization of tasks and ground transports

Ground activities are matched primarily by their name. Activities without name are matched by the alternative key (activityType, startStation,
endStation, scheduledStartTime, scheduledEndTime). If no match is found using this key, an extended match is made allowing some time deviation
(1 hour by default) for the scheduled times. The default time deviation is defined as class variable `scheduledTimesMatchSlack` in `std_interfaces.common.RequestHolder`, available
for override if needed. Only tasks and ground transports referenced by trips or rosters within the import scope, are synchronized.

The external system is assumed to be the master of tasks. Therefore tasks are always created if missing in the JCMS data model, and updated
if any attribute differ from what is specified in the message.

The data model in JCMS is updated to only contain *one* instance per task entity refId in the message. This means that it’s possible to express
that the *same* task should be used in different trips or rosters, for example if several crew participates on same training or transport activity.
It also means that identical tasks entities in the message must be duplicated, with different refID, if they should be represented as more than one
instance in JCMS. For example, two identical task entities, with different refId, are needed in the message if two crew members have vacation during
same period since each vacation instance in JCMS should be personal and it should be possible to update one without affecting the vacation of the other
crew member. In general, one task entity with unique refId, is needed in the message for each activity that is personal and should not be shared among
several rosters.

If option ‘delete-trips’ is ‘true’, tasks contained in a deleted trip may become orphans, i.e. if not assigned to any other trips or rosters.
Such activities are automatically deleted in JCMS unless they are ground tasks (ground duties), if option ‘delete\_orphan\_tasks’ is set to ‘true’ otherwise such orphan activities
are left untouched in JCMS. Tasks spanning over the planning period are split into planning period chunks. The planning period is defined by Rave definitions,
see [Rave definitions](#rave-definitions).

###### 24.4.4. Synchronization of trips

It is assumed that each trip in the message has a unique business key which can be used for matching.
Trips are not matched based on the activities in the trip. By default, matching of trips follows the general rules described in the introduction,
see [Matching of Planning Objects](introduction.html#stdif-intro-matching-objects).

Missing trips are created in JCMS. Conflicting trips are updated according to the imported version of the trip. A conflicting trip is one where the set of
assigned activities in the trip differ between the message and the JCMS data model.

Properties of a trip are updated in JCMS to match what is specified in the message. By default, existing trips within the given scope, that are not
included in the message, are deleted in JCMS. Trips starting between *scope\_period\_start* and *scope\_period\_end* are synchronized by default.

The option *update\_carryin\_trips* can be used for also including carry-in trips, trips overlapping *scope\_period\_start*.
The following logic applies for synchronizing carry-in trips:

* Carry-in trips are matched using the trip business key. If no matching trip is found, the interface tries to match carry-in trips using trip activities and crew composition.
* Carry-in trips matching a carry-in trip in the message are updated to match the imported version of the trip for activities starting after *scope\_period\_start*.
* Carry-in trips in the plan not matching any carry-in trip in the message are not updated or deleted.
* Carry-in trips in the message not matching any carry-in trip in the plan are partly created as new trips, only containing the trip activities starting after *scope\_period\_start*.

![../_images/update_carryin_trips.png](../_images/update_carryin_trips.png)

###### 24.4.5. Synchronization of rosters

Rosters are matched by crewId which is assumed to be the same in JCMS and the external system. It is also assumed that the crewId is not changing
over time for crew members. Each roster in a message is regarded as the complete state for the specified period, i.e.
all existing assignments on the roster in the data model is replaced with the roster in the message within the period scope.
The roster layering concept described in [Roster layer concept](roster_input.html#stdif-roster-layer-concept) applies and it can be used for configuring how roster updates should be applied,
e.g. to define a filter for certain activity types. By default, without any configuration, the entire roster is replaced.
Rosters that exists in JCMS data model, but not in a given message are never cleared (deleted), even if the roster belongs to the specified scope in
the data model, unless the option *delete\_assignments* is True.

Rosters in JCMS are updated to contain the tasks assignments as specified in the message. The same activity is assigned to different rosters in JCMS if
the different rosters in the message refer to the same task, regardless if the activity type of the task is personal or not.
It is possible to mark an assignment as *locked*, and thereby it will be updated in the plan as a locked assignment.

The option *update\_carryin\_trips* can be used for synchronizing crew assignments to carry-in trips, overlapping *scope\_period\_start*.
Note that *scope\_period\_start* in this context may be individual per roster if using import option *scope\_planning\_area*.
The following logic applies for synchronizing crew assignments to carry-in trips:

* Assignments to carry-in trips are not created, updated or deleted if a matching trip is found in the plan.
* Assignments to carry-in trips are created if no matching trip is found in the plan.

###### 24.4.6. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the PlanSync standard interface:

* `interfaces_core.%plansync_in_pp_start_at_time_utc%(AbsTime t)`: Defines the start time of the planning period at time t, used for splitting long tasks into planning period chunks.
* `interfaces_core.%plansync_in_pp_end_at_time_utc%(AbsTime t)`: Defines the end time of the planning period at time t.
* `interfaces_core.%plansync_in_split_margin%`: Defines a margin the task have to start before planning period start or end after planning period end, for it to be split. Used to avoid splitting tasks that only exceeds planning period with this margin.
* `interfaces_core.%is_own_carrier%(String carrier)`: Defines the carriers that belongs to this Airline. If a carrier from a flightLeg does not belong to own\_carrier, an AirTransport is searched/created instead of a FlightLeg.
* `interfaces_core.%crew_belongs_to_planning_area_from_utc%(String planningArea, AbsTime periodStart, AbsTime periodEnd)`: Returns start of interval within the given period, in which the crew member belongs to the given planning area. Default periodStart.
* `interfaces_core.%crew_belongs_to_planning_area_to_utc%(String planningArea, AbsTime periodStart, AbsTime periodEnd)`: Returns end of interval within the given period, in which the crew member belongs to the given planning area. Default periodEnd.
* `interfaces_core.%trip_belongs_to_planning_area%(String planningArea)`: Returns True if the trip belongs to the planning area with the given name. Default True.
* `interfaces_core.%planning_areas%`: Returns a comma separated list of available planning areas. Default “”.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline.

###### 24.4.7. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most of the standard interfaces, i.e. to reject
the incoming message if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. In such cases one or more error
messages are also issued in the log file, containing detailed information about the error.

If the interface encounters several errors, all errors belonging to the same message are collected before
the processing is terminated.

| Error | Error message type | code | subCode | reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Roster not found | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | Crewmembers not found ‘XXXXXXX’ |
| Illegal import/export scope period | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Scope-period-start > scope-period-end |
| Invalid import scope period | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Import scope period XXX->XXX does not match the exported period as specified in the message. |
| Invalid option scope\_period\_start | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid option scope-period-start ‘XXX’ |
| Invalid option scope\_period\_end | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid option scope-period-end ‘XXX’ |
| Invalid option scope\_homebase | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | Invalid option. Could not find any homebase with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| Invalid option scope\_crewcategory | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | Invalid option. Could not find any crewcategory with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| Invalid option scope\_planning\_area | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | Planning area ‘XXX’ not found |
| Invalid option scope\_rosters | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid option scope-rosters ‘XXX’ Expected [true/false] |
| Invalid option scope\_rosters\_crewid | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | Could not find any Crewmember with key ‘(‘XXXXXX’,)’ |
| Invalid option create\_flightlegs\_operational | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid option create-flightlegs- operational ‘XXX’. Expected [true/false] |
| Invalid option delete\_trips | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid option delete-trips ‘XXX’ Expected [true/false] |
| Invalid option delete\_assignments | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid option delete-assignments ‘XXX’ Expected [true/false] |
| Invalid option allow\_missing\_rosters | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | Invalid option allow-missing-rosters ‘XXX’. Expected [true/false] |
| Message inconsistency. Referenced trip not in message. | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectNotFound | Cannot find trip with reference ‘XXXXXX’ |
| Message inconsistency. Referenced flight leg not in message. | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectNotFound | Cannot find flight leg with reference ‘XXXXXX’ |
| Message inconsistency. Referenced task not in message. | ServiceError | MessageError | ObjectNotFound | Cannot find task with reference ‘XXXXXX’ |
| Invalid catalog data in message | ServiceError | MessageError | ReferenceNotFound | Could not find any <catalog data type> with key ‘(‘XXX’,)’ |
| Invalid import scope period | ServiceError | MessageError | ValueError | StartTime <time> and EndTime <time for <context> must be within planning period start <time> and end <time>. |
| Non unique trip identifier in message. | ServiceError | MessageError | InvalidMessage | Combination of trip name and dateOfOrigin is not unique. |

##### 24.5. Exporting a plan

The full state of the plan in JCMS is exported to as a single message. The plan is exported
for the specified scope (see [Export options](#stdif-plan-synch-export-options)).
As a minimum, the scope is defined by the exported period. By providing additional scope options, it’s possible to further detail the scope of the export.
This means it is possible to control what planning entities in the JCMS data model that should be exported to the message, e.g. export only rosters that
belong to a given homebase or crew category.
In addition, the roster layering concept described in [Roster layer concept](roster_input.html#stdif-roster-layer-concept) applies and it can be used for e.g. defining a filter to only export
certain activity types. By default, without any configuration, the entire roster is exported.

All activities (trips, flight legs, ground tasks etc.) within a given eport scope are exported irrespective of activity status, i.e. regardless if
cancelled or not. Open time tasks (i.e. ground tasks with unfulfilled need) are always exported, if within the exported period.

###### 24.5.1. Export options

The following options apply when exporting the plan from JCMS data model to a message. Additional options can be added as part of an implementation project.
All options are part of the request message, see the XSD.

Note that for the options controlling the exported scope, roster scope overrides trip scope such that a trip that is outside the scope is included in the
export anyway if assigned to a roster that is within the scope.

| Option | Description | Default value | Comment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| periodStart | Mandatory. Defines the period start of data to be exported from data model to message. Activities and assignments starting at or after this value are exported. |  | Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g. ‘2017-03-01T00:00:00Z’, ‘01MAR2017 00:00’ Export fails if value doesn’t fall within the plan period of the data context. |
| periodEnd | Mandatory. Defines the period end of data to be exported from data model to message. Activities and assignments starting before this value are exported. |  | Date time or AbsTime value in UTC, e.g. ‘2017-03-01T00:00:00Z’, ‘01MAR2017 00:00’ Export fails if value doesn’t fall within the plan period of the data context or if value is before scope-period-start. |
| homeBase | Optional. Defines the rosters/trips to be exported from data model by homebase. Don’t consider homebase if value is empty. | empty | Homebase code, e.g. ‘ZHR’ or ‘GNV’. Fails if the data model doesn’t contain the specified homebase. Homebase in data model is used for deciding if roster should be exported or not. Criterion for exporting a roster is that crew is based at the provided homebase at the start of the scope-period. A crew’s roster is imported for the full scope-period even if crew is based at the provided homebase for a part of the scope-period. |
| crewCategory | Optional. Defines the rosters/trips to be exported from data model by crew category. Don’t consider crew category if value is empty. | empty | Comma separates string of crew categories, e.g. ‘COC, CAB’. Fails if the data model doesn’t contain the provided crew categories. Crew category in data model is used for deciding if roster/trip should be exported or not. Criterion for exporting a roster is that crew belongs to the provided category at the start of the scope-period. When applied to a trip, crewcategory is derived from the trip’s crew complement. A crew’s roster is exported for the full scope-period even if crew belongs to the provided category for a part of the scope-period. |
| planningArea (added in version 3) | Optional. Defines the rosters/trips to be exported from the data model by planning area. Don’t consider planning area if value is empty. | empty | Name of planning area, e.g. ‘FD\_737’ Only rosters/trips belonging to the specified planning area are exported. The exported planning area is specified as a property ‘planningArea’ of the plan element in the exported data. N.B. The entire roster for the exported period is included even if the crew member only belongs to the specified planning area for a part of the exported period. |
| exportRosters | Optional. Specifies whether or not to export rosters. | true | By setting this option to ‘false’, only trips are synchronized. If set to ‘false’, the scope parameters control the subset of trips being imported/synchronized. |

##### 24.6. Use cases

###### 24.6.1. Importing a trip with flight activities

The plan synch interface can be used for synchronizing trips with an external system. In this example, a trip is created in JCMS,
referencing the following three existing flight legs:

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 2019 04JUL2015 | CPH | ZRH | 04:05 | 04:25 | sched |
| JJ 2020 04JUL2015 | ZRH | MAD | 05:05 | 07:25 | sched |
| JJ 2021 04JUL2015 | MAD | CPH | 08:05 | 10:20 | sched |

Applying the following message, using all default import options:

```
<syncPlanState xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/PlanSync/v3" source="JCR" version="3" created="2017-02-23T12:06:46.175567">
  <plan periodStart="2015-07-01T00:00:00+00:00" periodEnd="2015-07-31T00:00:00+00:00">
    <flightLegs>
      <flightLeg eventNumber="0" endStation="ZRH" flightNumber="2019" scheduleStatus="N" scheduledStartTime="2015-07-04T04:05:00+00:00" carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04" scheduledEndTime="2015-07-04T04:25:00+00:00" startStation="CPH" refId="1"/>
      <flightLeg eventNumber="0" endStation="MAD" flightNumber="2020" scheduleStatus="N" scheduledStartTime="2015-07-04T05:05:00+00:00" carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04" scheduledEndTime="2015-07-04T07:25:00+00:00" startStation="ZRH" refId="2"/>
      <flightLeg eventNumber="0" endStation="ZRH" flightNumber="2021" scheduleStatus="N" scheduledStartTime="2015-07-04T08:05:00+00:00" carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04" scheduledEndTime="2015-07-04T10:20:00+00:00" startStation="MAD" refId="3"/>
    </flightLegs>
    <tasks/>
    <groundTransports/>
    <trips>
      <trip refId="4" homeBase="CPH" name="2020_110" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04">
        <crew count="1" role="FC"/>
        <crew count="1" role="FP"/>
        <activity role="DH">
          <legRef id="1"/>
        </activity>
        <activity>
          <legRef id="2"/>
        </activity>
        <activity>
          <legRef id="3"/>
        </activity>
      </trip>
    </trips>
    <rosters/>
  </plan>
</syncPlanState>
```

results in the following trip:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | dep | arr | status | start time | end time | crew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 04JUL2015 | 2020\_110 | 04JUL2015 | CPH | CPH | CPH | OK | 04JUL2014 04:05 | 04JUL2014 10:20 | 1FC/1FP |

###### 24.6.3. Importing a trip with task activities

In this example, a trip is created in JCMS, consisting only of one ground activity. The ground activity does in this case not
exist previously in JCMS but is created together with the trip.

Applying the following message, using all default import options:

```

    </flightLegs>

        <activity role="FC">
          <taskRef id="2"/>
```

###### 24.6.7. Importing trips and rosters

By default, the plan synch interface will import roster information if included in the message. In this example,
rosters for two crew members with mixed content (both flight and ground activities) is imported. The crew members
doesn’t have any previous assignments within the specified plan period.

Applying the following message, using all default import options:

```
<syncPlanState xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/PlanSync/v3" source="JCR" version="3" created="2017-02-23T12:06:46.175567">
  <plan periodStart="2015-07-01T00:00:00+00:00" periodEnd="2015-07-31T00:00:00+00:00">
    <flightLegs>
      <flightLeg eventNumber="0" endStation="ZRH" flightNumber="2019" scheduleStatus="N" scheduledStartTime="2015-07-04T04:05:00+00:00" carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04" scheduledEndTime="2015-07-04T04:25:00+00:00" startStation="CPH" refId="2" startTimeOffset="PT2H" aircraftType="34S"/>
      <flightLeg eventNumber="0" endStation="MAD" flightNumber="2020" scheduleStatus="N" scheduledStartTime="2015-07-04T05:05:00+00:00" carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04" scheduledEndTime="2015-07-04T07:25:00+00:00" startStation="ZRH" refId="3" startTimeOffset="PT2H" aircraftType="34S"/>
      <flightLeg eventNumber="0" endStation="ZRH" flightNumber="2021" scheduleStatus="N" scheduledStartTime="2015-07-04T08:05:00+00:00" carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04" scheduledEndTime="2015-07-04T10:20:00+00:00" startStation="MAD" refId="4" startTimeOffset="PT2H" aircraftType="34S"/>
    </flightLegs>
    <tasks>
      <task station="CPH" activityType="SIM" startTime="2015-07-09T06:15:00+00:00" endTime="2015-07-09T15:30:00+00:00" refId="5">
        <need count="1" position="FC"/>
        <need count="1" position="AP"/>
      </task>
      <task station="CPH" activityType="SIM" startTime="2015-07-10T06:15:00+00:00" endTime="2015-07-10T14:45:00+00:00" refId="6">
        <need count="1" position="FC"/>
      </task>
    </tasks>
    <groundTransports/>
    <trips>
      <trip refId="1" homeBase="CPH" name="2020_110" dateOfOrigin="2015-07-04">
        <crew count="1" role="FC"/>
        <crew count="1" role="FP"/>
        <activity role="DH">
          <legRef id="02"/>
        </activity>
        <activity>
          <legRef id="03"/>
        </activity>
        <activity>
          <legRef id="04"/>
        </activity>
      </trip>
    </trips>
    <rosters>
      <roster crewId="04873">
        <assignment role="FC">
          <tripRef id="1"/>
        </assignment>
        <assignment role="FC">
          <taskRef id="5"/>
        </assignment>
        <assignment role="FC">
          <taskRef id="6"/>
        </assignment>
      </roster>
      <roster crewId="02905">
        <assignment role="AP">
          <taskRef id="5"/>
        </assignment>
      </roster>
    </rosters>
  </plan>
</syncPlanState>
```

results in the following assignments:

| typ | crew | id | dep | arr | start | end | role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trip | 04873 | 2020\_110 | CPH | CPH | 04JUL2015 04:05 | 04JUL2015 10:20 | FC |
| task | 04873 | SIM | CPH | CPH | 09JUL2015 06:15 | 09JUL2015 15:30 | FC |
| task | 04873 | SIM | CPH | CPH | 10JUL2015 06:15 | 10JUL2015 15:30 | FC |
| task | 02905 | SIM | CPH | CPH | 09JUL2015 06:15 | 09JUL2015 15:30 | AP |

The simulator task at the 09JUL (refId=5) has a need of two crew members. JCTE creates only one instance of this activity, but it must be assigned
to two crew members for the crew need to be covered. The two rosters in the message contains assignment to the same task (refId=5), hence
the two crew members are assigned to the same simulator activity, but with different roles.

Also the referenced trip is created in JCMS as a result of the message, since it didn’t exist prior to the import:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | dep | arr | status | start time | end time | crew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 04JUL2015 | 2020\_110 | 04JUL2015 | CPH | CPH | CPH | OK | 04JUL2015 04:05 | 04JUL2015 10:20 | 1FC/1FP |

###### 24.6.9. Importing a roster with personal (non-production) activities

In this example, rosters for two crew members with personal (non-production) activities is imported. The crew members
doesn’t have any previous assignments within the specified plan period.

Applying the following message, using all default import options:

```
<syncPlanState xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/PlanSync/v3" source="JCR" version="3" created="2017-02-23T12:06:46.175567">
  <plan periodStart="2015-07-01T00:00:00+00:00" periodEnd="2015-07-31T00:00:00+00:00">

    </flightLegs>

      <task activityType="OFF" startTime="2015-07-15T00:00:00+00:00" endTime="2015-07-16T00:00:00+00:00" station="CPH" refId="2" />
      <task activityType="OFF" startTime="2015-07-15T00:00:00+00:00" endTime="2015-07-16T00:00:00+00:00" station="CPH" refId="3" />
    </tasks>
    <groundTransports/>
    <trips>
    </trips>
    <rosters>
      <roster crewId="04873">
        <assignment>
          <taskRef id="1"/>
        </assignment>
        <assignment>
          <taskRef id="2"/>
        </assignment>
      </roster>

        <assignment>
          <taskRef id="3"/>
        </assignment>

```

results in the following assignments:

In this case crew member with id 04873 has vacation between 03JUL and 09JUL and also a day off on JUL16.
Crew member with id 02905 also has an identical day off on JUL16, but since these activities are personal and should not be shared, the message must contain unique instances
of the OFF tasks with different refId (refId=2 and refId=3). These type of tasks doesn’t have any need in the message since they are non-production activities.

| typ | crew | id | dep | arr | start | end | role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| task | 02905 | OFF | CPH | CPH | 15JUL2015 00:00 | 16JUL2015 00:00 | none |
| task | 04873 | OFF | CPH | CPH | 15JUL2015 00:00 | 16JUL2015 00:00 | none |
| task | 04873 | VAC | CPH | CPH | 03JUL2015 00:00 | 09JUL2015 00:00 | none |

###### 24.6.11. Importing rosters with relaxed check for missing crew members

In this example, the plan synch message contains a crew member (id=23447) that doesn’t previously exist in JCMS. By default

However, by setting option *allow-missing-rosters=true* rosters for missing crew members are ignored but the rest of the
message content is processed as normal.
In this case it would result in creation of the same objects as in example [Importing trips and rosters](#stdif-plan-synch-usecase-import-rosters),
given that none of these objects existed before importing the message.
This option is not recommended to use in a production environment as it may lead to inconsistent plan state between JCMS
and the external system.

### Trip Input


This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to provide trip data to the JCMS.
The information can be transferred via publish/subscribe if the sending system is considered master of the provided information.
The same kind of messages can be used for inbound service with “ack” or state response if JCMS is regarded master.
It is in this case strongly recommended for the sending system to attach the JCMS state indicator for conflict detection purposes.

The current version of this interface is 3.

[Link to TripStateInput\_3.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.trip_input_3/TripStateInput_3.xsd)

##### 25.1. Interface capabilities

Since trips are business objects with a fixed scope of data content they are most commonly updated based on new state information.
A message provides the new state of a (set of) trip(s). The “setTrips” operation can be used in batch or online mode.
Whether an online flow can be parallelized depends on the presence of a state reference,
either the JCMS cid (in case of a service) or a corresponding attribute from the source system (custom attribute).
When a state reference is present then the messages can be handled in parallel and out of order conditions will be detected.

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* setTrips
  :   Creates or updates trips in JCMS with information from the provided message (one-way request without any response message).
* setTripsWithAck
  :   Same as setTrips but with an acknowledge response on successful operation (request/response).

For the matching of trips, general rules described in the introduction apply, see [Matching of Planning Objects](introduction.html#stdif-intro-matching-objects).
By default, only “name” and “dateOfOrigin” in TripMatch elements are used for trip matching, other attributes (“category”, “homeBase”
“startStation”, “endStation”, “startTime”, “endTime”) are not used for matching and will be removed in future version of this interface.

A trip always has a home base (where it starts and ends) and a set of roles to be filled (the CrewComplement).
A trip can have a category, which is a classification inside JCMS to distinguish different types of trips, e.g. production trips from simulator setups.
The category can be to indicate e.g. ownership or source of the trip. It is a static enumeration, so it can’t be used to indicate dynamic grouping of trips.

The trip then consists of a set of activity (e.g. flight leg, ground task, etc.) assignments,
a role is only given per activity if it deviates from the trip’s CrewComplement (typically set to DH, deadhead).
For each activity it is possible to provide the stations and times that are the planned status of this activity in this trip.
If these are given they are represented in JCMS as so called “planned assignment attributes” and they are used to detect deviation from planned state
(e.g. for alert generation) as well as for some rules.
JCMS will use the current state (at time of the message evaluation) of the assigned activities to fill the assignment attributes (stations and times),
i.e. JCMS will assume that the current state of the activities defines the planned state of the trip.
In the same manner also planned stations on the trip level itself can be included and will be used if present.
At the initial trip creation, the date attribute dateOfOrigin is used as an original value for times. Later when processing the message,
JCMS will use the current state (at time of the message evaluation) of the assigned activities to fill the trip times.
For example, the start time of a trip will be derived from the start time of the first flight leg.

The following assumptions are made regarding existence of activities referenced in a trip message:

* Flight legs are expected to exist, regardless whether they are of the own carrier or of some other carrier (e.g. OAG deadheads).
  However if a leg is missing, the trip is still accepted and the leg is created but marked cancelled. Scheduled leg times are optional
  as parameters. They are not used for matching of flight legs but they are needed when creating new flight legs.
* Any non-flight activity (task) will be created if it is not already assigned to the trip. For tasks requiring a need, the need will be
  derived from the trip’s crew composition. If several trips share the same task, e.g. a simulator activity, one instance of the task
  is created for each trip, i.e. the crew need of a particular task instance only reflects the crew composition of the trip it belongs to.
* It is considered as an error when an activity in a trip has the start time after the end time. As a result, the message is disregarded.
* The interface is primarily designed for planning usage. Flight legs’ return or wait events are not supported by the interface.

It is possible to configure the interface so that any changes to a trip, which is assigned to crew, are also acknowledged automatically
for each crew.

Training information can optionally be provided to indicate that a trip is used for training, and possibly also
what kind of training is performed. This is done by providing training tags that are defined in the customization layer.
Training tags are updated as a state, i.e. the trip in JCMS is updated to match the training tags in the inbound message.
All training tags are removed from the trip in JCMS if the inbound message doesn’t have any training tags, even if the tags
were added by some other user or process.

All other information is normally calculated, but published (frozen) information can be provided in customizations.
How to do that depends on the type of information.
In many cases there are custom attributes on the assignment or trip object level that are used as overrides.
In other cases separate elements are needed.

##### 25.2. Use cases

###### 25.2.1. Create a new trip

If the trip provided in a setTrips message doesn’t exist it is created. The status code of the trip activity is scheduled.
Times of the trip or assignment level are derived from the actual flight content.
If a referenced flight doesn’t exist, it is represented as a non-operating leg.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setTripsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/TripStateInput/v3"
                    version="3"  source="BB" created="2013-11-25T23:13:44" >
  <trip name="1546" homeBase="CPH" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14">
    <crew role="FC" count="1" />
    <crew role="FP" count="1" />
    <assignment role="DH" >
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" startStation="GOT" endStation="CPH" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00"  />
    </assignment>
    <assignment>
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="995" startStation="CPH" endStation="PEK" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T16:13:00"  />
    </assignment>
    <assignment>
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-15" flightNumber="996" startStation="PEK" endStation="CPH" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-15T08:40:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-15T15:25:00"  />
    </assignment>
  </trip>
</setTripsRequest>
```

This will result in a new trip:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | dep | arr | status | start time | end time | crew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14MAR2014 | 1546 | 14MAR2014 | CPH | GOT | CPH | OK | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 | 1CP/1FO |

containing the following assignments:

| flight | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | status | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | CPH | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP | DH | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 14MAR2014 09:05 |
| JJ 995 14MAR2014 | CPH | PEK | 09:35 | 16:13 | OK | CP/FO | 14MAR2014 09:35 | 14MAR2014 16:13 |
| JJ 996 15MAR2014 | PEK | CPH | 08:40 | 15:25 | OK | CP/FO | 15MAR2014 08:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 |

Trips can contain ground activities as well, for example personal activities.

```

  <trip name="1547" homeBase="CPH" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14">
    <crew role="FC" count="1" />
    <crew role="FP" count="1" />
    <assignment>
      <task activityType="IN" startStation="CPH" endStation="CPH" 
           startTime="2014-03-14T00:00:00" endTime="2014-03-15T00:00:00"  startTimeOffset="PT1H" endTimeOffset="PT1H" />
    </assignment>
    <assignment>
      <task activityType="IN" startStation="CPH" endStation="CPH" 
           startTime="2014-03-15T00:00:00" endTime="2014-03-16T00:00:00"  startTimeOffset="PT1H" endTimeOffset="PT1H" />
    </assignment>
  </trip>
</setTripsRequest>
```

This will result in a new trip:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | dep | arr | status | start time | end time | crew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14MAR2014 | 1547 | 14MAR2014 | CPH | CPH | CPH | OK | 14MAR2014 00:00 | 16MAR2014 00:00 | 1CP/1FO |

containing the following newly created supp ground activities:

| activity | dep | arr | start | end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IN | CPH | CPH | 14MAR2014 00:00 | 15MAR2014 00:00 |
| IN | CPH | CPH | 15MAR2014 00:00 | 16MAR2014 00:00 |

###### 25.2.2. Cancel a trip

If the trip provided in a cancelTrip message exists:
\* The trip is marked as cancelled (Not Operating any longer but NOT removed).
\* The work coverage provided by the given trip is reset which means the crew complement is set to Null. The consequence is that the corresponding crew need is now shown in Open time.
If the trip provided in a cancelTrip message doesn’t exist an error is generated.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setTripsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/TripStateInput/v3"
                    version="3"  source="BB" created="2013-11-25T23:13:44" >
  <cancelTrip name="1546" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" />
</setTripsRequest>
```

This will result in cancelled trip:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | dep | arr | status | start time | end time | crew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14MAR2014 | 1546 | 14MAR2014 | CPH | GOT | CPH | NOP | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 | 0CP/0FO |

containing the following assignments:

| flight | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | status | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | CPH | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP | DH | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 14MAR2014 09:05 |
| JJ 995 14MAR2014 | CPH | PEK | 09:35 | 16:13 | OK | CP/FO | 14MAR2014 09:35 | 14MAR2014 16:13 |
| JJ 996 15MAR2014 | PEK | CPH | 08:40 | 15:25 | OK | CP/FO | 15MAR2014 08:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 |

###### 25.2.3. Update a trip

If the trip provided in a replaceTrip or trip message, already exists, the trip is updated.
If the trip provided in a replaceTrip message doesn’t exist an error is generated.

If we have the following trip:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | dep | arr | status | start time | end time | crew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14MAR2014 | 1546 | 14MAR2014 | CPH | GOT | CPH | OK | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 | 1CP/1FO |

containing the following assignments:

| flight | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | status | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | CPH | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP | DH | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 14MAR2014 09:05 |
| JJ 995 14MAR2014 | CPH | PEK | 09:35 | 16:13 | OK | CP/FO | 14MAR2014 09:35 | 14MAR2014 16:13 |
| JJ 996 15MAR2014 | PEK | CPH | 08:40 | 15:25 | OK | CP/FO | 15MAR2014 08:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 |

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setTripsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/TripStateInput/v3"
                    version="3"  source="BB" created="2013-11-25T23:13:44" >
  <trip name="1546" homeBase="CPH" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14">
    <crew role="FC" count="1" />
    <crew role="FP" count="1" />
    <assignment>
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="995" startStation="CPH" endStation="PEK" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T16:13:00"  />
    </assignment>
    <assignment>
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-15" flightNumber="996" startStation="PEK" endStation="CPH" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-15T08:40:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-15T15:25:00"  />
    </assignment>
  </trip>
</setTripsRequest>
```

###### 25.2.4. Update a cancelled trip

The original trip is marked as Cancelled. This trip could have been marked as cancelled from a cancelTrip message or from the UI.

If the input provided is a setTrip or updateTrip then the existing cancelled trip will be marked as scheduled again and updated accordingly.
If the input provided is an addTrip message of the same matching trip then it will fail and an error will be generated.

If we have the following cancelled trip:

###### 25.2.5. Create a new trip with annotation

If the trip provided in a setTrip message doesn’t exist it is created.
Times that are provided at the trip or assignment level will be stored independently from the actual flight content.
If a referenced flight doesn’t exist, it is represented as a non-operating leg.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setTripsRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/TripStateInput/v3"
                    version="3"  source="BB" created="2013-11-25T23:13:44" >
  <trip name="1546" homeBase="CPH" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14">
    <crew role="FC" count="1" />
    <crew role="FP" count="1" />
    <assignment role="DH" >
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" startStation="GOT" endStation="CPH" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00"  />
    </assignment>
    <assignment>
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="995" startStation="CPH" endStation="PEK" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T16:13:00"  />
    </assignment>
    <assignment>
      <leg carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-15" flightNumber="996" startStation="PEK" endStation="CPH" 
           scheduledStartTime="2014-03-15T08:40:00" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-15T15:25:00"  />
    </assignment>
    <annotation annotation="Test annotation" createdBy="Jeppesen" creationTime="2014-11-15T11:15:00" />
  </trip>
</setTripsRequest>
```

This will result in a new trip:

| TRIP date | name | dor | base | dep | arr | status | start time | end time | crew |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14MAR2014 | 1546 | 14MAR2014 | CPH | GOT | CPH | OK | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 | 1CP/1FO |

containing the following assignments:

| flight | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | status | role | asmt start | asmt end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | CPH | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP | DH | 14MAR2014 07:40 | 14MAR2014 09:05 |
| JJ 995 14MAR2014 | CPH | PEK | 09:35 | 16:13 | OK | CP/FO | 14MAR2014 09:35 | 14MAR2014 16:13 |
| JJ 996 15MAR2014 | PEK | CPH | 08:40 | 15:25 | OK | CP/FO | 15MAR2014 08:40 | 15MAR2014 15:25 |

and the following annotation:

| code | annotation | created\_by | creation\_time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PUBLIC | Test annotation | Jeppesen | 15Nov2014 11:15 |

Note that trip annotations created from this interface are always given the predefined annotation code PUBLIC.
The PUBLIC annotation code has attribute ‘is\_public’ set to True in the data model, meaning that it is visible
to crew members. There may be other annotation codes defined in the system with attribute ‘is\_public’ set to True,
but in the Trip Input interface it is currently not possible to specify an annotation code, hence the default
code PUBLIC is assigned.

###### 25.2.6. Update a trip with annotation

Note that all trip annotations for crew (PUBLIC), will be replaced by the updated annotation.

### Trip Output


This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to get trip information from JCMS.
Trip information is normally sent when explicitly requested by an external user or system
(request/response pattern). The information can also be sent spontaneously by JCMS, either on changes or
on a scheduled basis (publish/subscribe pattern). The latter requires however a service trigger to be
configured inside JCMS. Such triggers are not provided out of the box by the standard interface but must
be added as part of an implementation project. In addition, it is also possible, as a part of
implementation project customization, to add mechanisms to enable e.g. a Tracking user to manually request
trip information to be sent out to predefined destinations.

The current version of this interface is 3.

[Link to TripStateOutput\_3.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.trip_output_3/TripStateOutput_3.xsd)

[Link to TripStateOutput\_3.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.trip_output_3/TripStateOutput_3.wsdl)

Previous versions of this interface

[Link to TripState\_2\_0.xsd (version 2.0)](contract/std_interfaces.trip_output_2_0/TripState_2_0.xsd)

[Link to TripStateSoap\_2\_0.wsdl (version 2.0)](contract/std_interfaces.trip_output_2_0/TripStateSoap_2_0.wsdl)

##### 26.1. Interface capabilities

The interface supports three request types:

* The operation “getTripsByMatch” delivers the list of trips that are identified by the TripMatch elements
  inside the request.
  For the matching of trips, general rules described in the introduction apply, see [Matching of Planning Objects](introduction.html#stdif-intro-matching-objects).
  If no matach is found for a TripMatch element or if the match is ambiguous, then the operation will fail.
  If several TripMatch elements matches same trip object, then the delivered
  list only contains one instance of that trip.
  By default, only “name” and “dateOfOrigin” in TripMatch elements are used for trip matching, other attributes (“category”, “homeBase”
  “startStation”, “endStation”, “startTime”, “endTime”) are not used for matching and will be removed in future version of this interface.
* The operation “getTripsInPeriod” delivers the list of all trips that start within the requested time
  period. In addition to the time period, it is also possible to specify one or more of the optional
  selection criteria crewCategory, crewRank, homeBase and trip category. The operation then delivers trips
  matching both the specified period and all other given criteria. A trip matches a crewCategory/crewRank if its
  crew complement contains at least one role belonging to that category/rank. A trip that has roles for both
  cabin and cockpit crew will be selected in both categories - the reported crew complement is not
  filtered by crew category or rank.
* The operation “getOpenTimeTripsInPeriod” is identical to “getTripsInPeriod” except that it only
  delivers the list of all open time trips that match the given criteria. An open time trip is a trip where
  not all roles are filled with crew, the crew complement of an open time trip in the interface will
  reflect only the open positions and only these will be regarded when selecting by crewCategory/crewRank, e.g. if
  open time trips for cabin crew are requested then only trips with open cabin positions are included.
  A trip that has unassigned slices for both cabin and cockpit crew will be selected in both categories -
  the reported crew complement is not filtered by crew category or rank.

###### 26.1.1. Scope and content of returned trip state

In both request types “getTripsInPeriod” and “getOpenTimeTripsInPeriod” it is required to specify a request
period. The interface responds with the state of all matching trips for the requested time period, as
described above. Note that it is the start time of the trip that matters here, not the dateOfOrigin.
The trip start time must be defined by specific Rave variables, see [Rave definitions](#rave-definitions). A trip
is considered inside the requested period if (periodStart <= startTime < periodEnd).

Trips are always included in their entirety such that also duties and/or activities outside the
requested period are included as long as some piece of the trip is inside the period.
Empty trip objects, which doesn’t contain any duties or activities, are not included in the export.

Trips with an undefined crew complement or a crew complement without any roles defined are always excluded
from the trip state, regardless of which request type is used. The role does not however need to be an
active one, thus pure deadhead trips are included in the trip state. Hence, a pure deadhead trip is also
considered open time if all its deadhead “positions” are not assigned. However, the deadhead role is
normally not associated with any particular crew category, therefore those trips will be excluded whenever
a crewCategory criterion is specified in the request.

By default, training trips are not regarded as open time trips even if they have an unfulfilled need.
This behavior may be customized as part of an implementation project. A training trip is a trip that has
one or more training tags associated with it.

The following types of activities can be included in a trip:

* Flight Leg (including return-to-ramp and wait-at-gate events)
* Air Transport
* Ground Task
* Ground Transport

Note that for Air Transports normally very limited information is available. Although represented
by the same data type as normal Flight Legs in the interface schema, some of the fields like e.g.
effectiveEndStation, estimatedStartTime and actualStartTime are never included for Air Transports.

Export of annotations is limited to annotations that are intended to be shared with crew members, such annotations
have an annotation code that is internally tagged with the attribute ‘is\_public’ set to True.

Internally in JCMS, all Ground Tasks that are not part of any trip are technically “wrapped” inside a trip
when stored in the database. Such internal trips are however not included in the outbound trip state
since they are not regarded as trips by external systems nor handled as trips in the planning process
at large. The system distinguishes wrapper trips from real trips by using a special trip category reserved
exclusively for internal usage.

The delivered list of trips is ordered primarily by trip startTime and secondly by trip name. The ordering
may however easily be customized as part of an implementation project.

###### 26.1.2. Supported protocols

The interface supports requests using both plain XML and SOAP. The SOAP service is primarily intended for
supporting external WEB services. For use with internal triggers the plain XML form of the service is
normally used.

###### 26.1.3. Rave definitions

The following Rave variables are defined in the CARMSYS and used by the Trip Output standard interface:

* interfaces\_core.%trip\_out\_trip\_start\_utc%: Defines the start time of a trip, used for identifying whether a trip starts in the requested period or not.
* interfaces\_core.%trip\_out\_trip\_end\_utc%: Defines the end time of a trip, not used by current version of this interface.

The business logic behind these Rave variables need to be implemented in a CARMUSR to comply with the
expected behavior of each individual airline.

###### 26.1.4. Error handling

The interface conforms to the same error handling strategy as most interfaces, i.e. to reject the message
if it cannot be entirely and completely processed. Concretely for the Trip Output interface it
means e.g. that if it fails to find or process any of the trips matching a “getTripsByMatch” request, it
will respond with an error message.

##### 26.2. Use cases

The examples below all use the plain XML service, the same use cases can be executed in the SOAP service
but then a SOAP envelope and the SoapAction header are required.
