### Operational Flight Input


This chapter describes the interfaces that can be used to provide flight data to the JCMS during operation. The functionality of this interface is also
available in the [Flight Input](flight_input.html#stdif-flight-input) interface. It is preferred to use that interface instead.
Short before and during operation there will usually be frequent updates to the flight information, capturing the estimated or actual movements of the
aircraft or any disturbances to the planned flow. The picture of clearly identified planned legs is no longer valid since all atomic events that affect
the aircraft, crew and passengers must be taken care of. The JCMS system has a quite pragmatic view on the leg entities that focusses on the actual events
and not on the question which movements or events belong to “the same official leg”. Groupings of events into legs or flights are only relevant to determine
the initial assignment of potential new items to resources - e.g. a return to ramp event is assigned to the same aircraft and crew as the leg that was
attempted. To change crew or equipment before the actual take off of the “main leg” is then an explicit operational decision.
The standard interfaces for operational flight updates reflect the pragmatic view of leg identity by using the scheduled departure as part of the key
(to avoid issues with uniqueness in case of rerouting back to departure airport) and formulating some operations in term of “atoms” rather than legs.

The operations are collected in the “FlightOperation” service. This services main operation is “updateFlights”.
For convenience the FlightOperation service also contains the “setFlightsEqipment” operation described above.

The current version of this interface is 3.0.

[Link to FlightOperation\_3\_0.xsd](contract/std_interfaces.flight_input_3_0/FlightOperation_3_0.xsd)

The normal operation mode for these interfaces is online and ordering per flight must be preserved.
For robustness reasons it is recommended to always provide all available information which will lead to some
extend of “self-healing” in case of processing errors since all provided information is applied.

In general the systems providing flight information are regarded master relative to JCMS and the interfaces are
implemented as publish/subscribe interfaces.

##### 27.1. Interface capabilities

###### 27.1.1. Common principles

The standard interfaces are completely UTC based, all dateTime values are expected to be in the UTC time zone.
There are two points in the flight interfaces where this could lead to issues.
One is the handling of “day of origin” as part of the flight key.
IATA standard prescribes it to be the UTC day of departure of the first leg; that is not strictly required by the JCMS system.
The value is never interpreted as time-zoned, it is used purely for identification purpose. As long as all connected systems
use the same date to identify the flight it will work, no time-zone conversion for 0:00 UTC is needed.
The other point is with the scheduled departure time if a sending system is working completely local time based.
Since the JCMS has its own storage of the time-zone information to be able to fix the data without help from external vendors
there is a risk that the local time offset that the external system uses is not the same as what JCMS has.
That would lead to the fact that the transferred times do not match in local time in reality.
To be able to detect that situation the flight interfaces contain optional fields for time-zone offsets
for scheduled departure and arrival times. It is recommended to set these values if the data is transferred from a local-time based system to JCMS.
If the values are provided and if they differ from the values that JCMS has for the same airport at the same UTC time,
then this is regarded an error and the data is not stored to the database.

The standard flight interfaces do not normally check that information arrives in the order that would be expected during normal operation.
It is for example OK to send an actual landing time even though no take off time is present (yet) and the actual departure is accepted
even though a landing is already present. This allows the source system to also send corrected or lacking information later,
e.g. based on manual flight log handling. Any constraints that are implemented
are described together with the affected use cases, e.g. return to ramp and rescheduling.

The standard flight interfaces will take care of already existing assignments of flight legs when changes to the flights are coming in.
Existing assignments are kept even when flights are renamed, and new legs (and operational events) in existing flights
are assigned to the same crew and trips as the original legs. If a multi-leg flight contained a change of crew,
then the system will assume that the change shall happen at the same station as planned if that station is still touched.

###### 27.1.2. Identification of flights and legs

As already in the schedule phase, a dated flight is the set of all atoms that share the same
IATA flight key (dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix).
A single leg is the set of atoms that share the extended IATA leg key
(dateOfOrigin, carrier, flightNumber, suffix, startStation, endStation, scheduledStartTime, scheduledEndTime).
Within each leg the leg\_atom\_number is expected to be unique and the number 0 identifies the “main atom” - performing the actual flight segment.
Other atoms can be Return or Wait events.
When looking up a leg for processing the interface always first identifies all atoms of the flight, then filters them with the
information given in the leg element. While both stations must be matched identical there is an accepted deviation for the provided times
to allow for robustness in the face of rescheduling. Schedule times are however only used for matching in case there are more than
one main atom with matching startStation and endStation.
The accepted deviation is not applicable for the addLeg operation, as it is assumed that if the source system issues an addLeg operation, the leg
should be added, unless there already exist a leg, with exact same scheduled times.

###### 27.1.3. Update Flights

This operation allows flexible formulation of updates that affect the operation for certain planned flights and legs by providing
the new expected state of a set of flight atoms (including return atoms).
Note that return atoms share the scheduled station and time information with the main leg.
If the source system does create new objects with diverging scheduled properties these must be communicated as separate legs instead.
Given the identification of a single flight (and of the leg inside the flight) update Flight messages can contain updates to
the scheduled information such as renaming or canceling the flight. It can also provide operational data like new estimates or actual times,
can express reroutes or return to base/ramp and define new follow-up legs. Note that in the case of cancel, the operation will not fail
even if the flight doesn’t exist in JCMS. This is a deviation from the semantics of a ‘cancel’ operation as described in [Naming Conventions](introduction.html#stdif-intro-naming-conventions).
The message is designed to be semantically clear to the
expected effects of the input and all information shall be actually present in the message itself;
for example when getting a reroute any following connection legs must be explicitly given,
they will not be created based on the assumption that the flight shall continue to its original destination.

###### 27.1.4. Provide Equipment Information for Flights

The equipment information can be updated together with leg in the updateFlights operation.
The operation “setFlightsEqipment” allows the transfer of equipment updates only with less other leg attributes present and
can be used when major changes to equipment are transferred without other flight information.

##### 27.2. Future enhancements (preview)

###### 27.2.1. Flight Events

This operation will allow efficient transmission of operational events if the sender is not aware of enough state information to use
the state based operation. This might for example be the case when translating from IATA MVT or similar event-focused messages.

For each group of events the message contains all information that might be required to describe the event and its knock-on effects.
Besides the use of different elements the semantic is similar to the state based operation for most of the cases,
only return atoms and delay code information is handled in a different way.

The different event groups contain potentially different information sets,
“cancel” cancels the whole flight, “rename” provides a new identifier,
“move” deals with estimated and actual times and
“return” allows formulation of new return to Ramp/Gate/Base events as well as
providing updated estimates/actuals for those that are currently ongoing.

Since identification of delay code information and return events is implicit a failure to process one of these messages
might have side effects on later messages concerning the same flight.
This is a general robustness issue in event based interfaces. One possible re-sync mechanism is to send a state message for the
affected flight or leg if the source system is capable of that. Otherwise the data might be corrected manually within JCMS.

##### 27.3. Use cases

The base for the following examples is a two-leg flight that has the following state before operation:

* dep = departure airport
* arr = arrival airport
* sobt = scheduled departure time
* sibt = scheduled arrival time
* state = type/status of the flight atom
  + sched : scheduled leg
  + canc : cancelled leg
  + rertd : rerouted leg (changed scheduled arrival station)
  + retim : retimed leg (changed scheduled times)
  + div : diverted (changed effective arrival)
  + ret#n : a return event with atom nuber n
  + wt#n : a wait event (change crew at gate) with atom number n
* earr = effective arrival station
* eobt = estimated offblock time
* eibt = estimated inblock time
* aobt = actual offblock time
* atot = actual take off time
* atol = actual touch down time
* aibt = actual inblock time

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

and is scheduled in a trip like this

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (legal) | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | OK |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | OK |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK |

###### 27.3.1. state oriented communication

This section provides examples how typical operational situations would be reflected when using a state-oriented communication pattern.
That pattern uses the “setFlight(cancelLeg|setLeg)” messages and provide all available information.
The variation lies in how much information is provided in a single message and examples of this variation are given where relevant.

####### 27.3.1.1. regular operation

In the regular operation case JCMS receives a flow of updates to the legs that reflect the current state of operation.
The examples show the flow for the first leg GOT-FRA.

####### 27.3.1.2. Return to Ramp

The following flow shows a scenario of return to ramp and crew change at the gate.
We assume that the flight has left the gate (after actual offBlock from the regular example)
The first message describes the intention to return to ramp, this would be communicated while the aircraft is not docked in again yet.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      version="3.0" >
  <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
    <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
            endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
      <returnLeg  returnNumber="1" >
        <estimatedTimes inBlock="2014-03-14T07:50:00" />
        <actualTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T07:43:00" />
      </returnLeg>
      <operation>
        <estimatedTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T08:05:00" inBlock="2014-03-14T09:28:00" />
      </operation>
    </setLeg>
  </setFlight>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | ret1 | GOT | 07:41 | 07:50 | 07:43 |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | sched |  | 08:05 | 09:28 |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (short conn in FRA) | Assign info shows: |  | | | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | GOT | 07:43 | 07:50 | RET | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 08:05 | 09:28 | OK | GOT | FRA | 08:05 | 09:28 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | OK | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 |

After the aircraft is docked again the return event is updated with actual times.
Since there have not been any actual take-off or landing times this is a ground return.
If we had got the same messages after actual takeoffTime, then the return leg had
inherited this information and we would know its a return to base.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      version="3.0" >
  <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
    <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
            endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
      <returnLeg  returnNumber="1" >
        <actualTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T07:43:00" inBlock="2014-03-14T07:53:00" />
      </returnLeg>
    </setLeg>
  </setFlight>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

If the flight has to return to gate again the return event ends up in the second trip.
Note that the return number in the message is not matching the atom number in the flight.
The interface logic is aware that wait events are not communicated with flight systems.

      </returnLeg>

| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 08:10 | wt2 | GOT |  |  | 08:05 |  |  |  |

Note that only a return at the departure station is considerd a return event of the given leg.
If the aircraft moves at the destination after landing, this is either a return event of the next leg
or it can be handled as a separate operational leg of the current flight if this is the final destination.
The interface applies some chekcs on the provided times to detect this situation and will reject the message in that case.

####### 27.3.1.3. Diversion and rerouting

The following examples show cases of diversion or rerouting.

In the first scenario we assume that the flight has not started yet when the information arrives that a landing in FRA is not possible.
The flight is rerouted (schedule update) through DUS instead.
The trip will be updated to contain the new leg, but cancelled legs are not automatically removed.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      version="3.0" >
  <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
    <cancelLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" 
            endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:13:00" />
    <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
            endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
      <reschedule startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:45:00" 
                  endStation="DUS" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:25:00" />
    </setLeg>
    <setLeg startStation="DUS" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:55:00" 
            endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:58:00" >
    </setLeg>
  </setFlight>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | DUS | 07:45 | 09:25 | rertd |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | DUS | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (infeasible) | Assign info shows: |  | | | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | DUS | 07:45 | 09:25 | RRT | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | NOP | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | DUS | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 | OK | CGN | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 |

In the next scenario we assume the first leg is not rescheduled but only diverted, the effect on the trip are basically the same.
Whether the change gets applied before or after start only affects the presence of actuals in this case
( and thus there wouldn’t be a new estimated departure )

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      version="3.0" >
  <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
    <cancelLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" 
            endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:13:00" />
    <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
            endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
      <operation effectiveArrivalStation="DUS" >
        <estimatedTimes offBlock="2014-03-14T07:45:00" 
                        inBlock="2014-03-14T09:25:00" />
      </operation>
    </setLeg>
    <setLeg startStation="DUS" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:55:00" 
            endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:58:00" >
    </setLeg>
  </setFlight>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | div | DUS | 07:45 | 09:25 |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | DUS | MUC | 09:55 | 10:58 | sched |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

If the information is sent in separate requests, the final result will be the same,
the trip gets infeasible as soon as the first change is handled but the type of the first alert might differ depending on the order of the emssages.
Typically the rerouting of the first leg would come first and break the connection at FRA, the cancellation of the second leg creates a “NOP” and
this is not fixed automatically by insertion of the DUS-MUC leg. The planner will have to remove the FRA-MUC leg manually.

In the next scenario we assume that the flight has started. Sending a reschedule at this point is an error, a started leg cannot be rescheduled.
The rerouting message will have the same effect as in the first scenario, only that the actuals for off block and take off are kept,
so that the update to the estimations doesnt impact the case.
Of course normally we would not expect to get a new estimated off block time for a started flight,
but that is not explicit handled as error since it doesn’t effect the application logic.

####### 27.3.1.4. Cancellation and reinstatiation

The following examples show the effect of cancellations an reinstantiations.

If the whole flight is cancelled at once all legs in the flight are cancelled.
Any trips containing them become infeasible as they contain NOP (not operational) activities.
A message that contains explicit cancellation of all legs in the flight has the same effect.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:03:55"
                      version="3.0" >
  <cancelFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" />
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:05:44"
                      version="3.0" >
  <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
    <cancelLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
            endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" />
    <cancelLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" 
            endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:13:00" />
  </setFlight>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

| flight id | dep | arr | sobt | sibt | state | earr | eobt | eibt | aobt | atot | atol | aibt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | canc |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (infeasible) |  | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | GOT | FRA | 07:40 | 09:05 | NOP |  |
| JJ 101 14MAR2014 | FRA | MUC | 09:35 | 10:13 | NOP |  |
| JJ 202 14MAR2014 | MUC | GOT | 12:40 | 14:55 | OK |  |

If the legs are cancelled one by one, then the change occurs in several steps but the final effect is the same.

```

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Trip 154 GOT-GOT: 1CP/1FO (infeasible) |  | | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Reinstantiation must explicitly state all legs, an empty setFlight message is will not have any effect.
Assume the current state has both legs cancelled,
then the following messages will restore the flight to its original state.

            endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" />
    <setLeg startStation="FRA" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T09:35:00" 
            endStation="MUC" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T10:13:00" />
  </setFlight>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

Reinstantiate the legs separately:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>

```

####### 27.3.1.5. Equipment changes

The following examples show the options to provide equipment information for legs. During operation, normally that means providing actual tail names.
The following messages both result in the first leg of our flight being assigned to the aircraft with the registration “LNBRH” .
The difference in behavior only shows when sending several legs at once, in the setLeg case the legs are grouped within the flight,
in the equipment request each leg is its own entity.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<updateFlightsRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      version="3.0" >
  <setFlight carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101" >
    <setLeg startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
            endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" >
	<equipment aircraft="LNBRH" />
    </setLeg>
  </setFlight>
</updateFlightsRequest>
```

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<setFlightsEquipmentRequest xmlns="http://flight_operation_input_3.service.jcms.jeppesen.com"
                      source="FLIGHTOPS" created="2014-03-14T07:36:44"
                      version="3.0" >
  <equipment carrier="JJ" dateOfOrigin="2014-03-14" flightNumber="101"
             startStation="GOT" scheduledStartTime="2014-03-14T07:40:00" 
             endStation="FRA" scheduledEndTime="2014-03-14T09:05:00" 
             aircraft="LNBRH" />
</setFlightsEquipmentRequest>
```

If a message with another tail name arrives then the assignment will be replaced,
the interface assumes that any leg is always planned to be operated by a single aircraft.

### Maintenance Info Input


This chapter describes the Maintennce Info Input interface. This in an inbound interface used for sending aircraft maintenance related information to JCMS from external systems.

It currently supports sending defect information (maintenance items) to JCT.

Latest version of this interface is 1.beta.

[Link to MaintenanceInfoInput\_1\_beta.wsdl](contract/std_interfaces.maintenance_info_input_1/MaintenanceInfoInput_1_beta_1.wsdl)

Available operations are:

* ping
  :   Pings the service without doing anything (for test purposes).
* addMaintenanceItem
  :   Add a new maintenance item (one-way request without any response message).
* addMaintenanceItemWithAck
  :   Add a new maintenance item with acknowledge response on successful update.
* updateMaintenanceItem
  :   Update an existing maintenance item (one-way request without any response message).
* updateMaintenanceItemWithAck
  :   Update an existing maintenance item with acknowledge response on successful update.
* setMaintenanceItem
  :   Update or create a maintenance item (one-way request without any response message).
* setMaintenanceItemWithAck
  :   Update or create a maintenance item with acknowledge response on successful update.
* deleteMaintenanceItem
  :   Delete a maintenance item (one-way request without any response message).
* deleteMaintenanceItemWithAck
  :   Delete a maintenance item with acknowledge response on successful update.

##### 28.1. Maintenance items

A maintenance item is a typically a defect that can occur on an aircraft.
It is often referred to in everyday language as a “MEL”, but MEL is only one of a handful of maintenance item categories.

The following maintenance item categories exist:

* MEL (Minimum Equipment List)
* CDL (Configuration Deviation List)
* NEF (Nonessential Equipment and Furnishings)
* DMI (Deferred Maintenance Item)
* SEL (Special Equipment List)

The maintenance item is represented by a code (the “type” of the maintenance item). For each aircraft type, a large number of such codes are defined.
Different aircraft types have different sets of codes.

Ideally the codes should be part of the catalog data in a customer implementation, but the interface will automatically create missing codes.

###### 28.1.1. The life cycle of maintenance items

When a maintenance item is created, an expiry time is normally set. The maintenance item has to be fixed before the expiry time.

When the maintenance item has been fixed, it is cleared. An actual fix time is set.

A maintenance item can be extended, i.e. the expiry time can be prolonged.

A previously cleared maintenance item can be reopened. The actual fix time is reset.

A maintenance item can be deleted. This is different from clearing an item.
Clearing an item will set the fix time and keep the item in the database, while deleting an item will remove it from the database.

Clearing, extending and reopening maintenance items can all be done using the update operation, with arguments set to appropriate values.
To support all these operations, some of the interface attributes are nullable.

![../_images/maintenance_info_lifecycle.png](../_images/maintenance_info_lifecycle.png)

###### 28.1.2. Identification of aircraft

The client can use any combination of nose id, registration id and serial number for identification of the aircraft.
All given parameters must match the values stored in JCMS for a match to be successful.

###### 28.1.3. External references

It is possible to define an optional external reference id when creating a maintenance item.
The interface will behave differently depending on whether or not the external reference is used:

the following applies if external references are not sent by the client system:

* Only one item of the same type may be open at the same time.
* When updating or deleting a maintenance item, the interface will pick the item with the latest fix time if an open item does not exist.

##### 28.2. Examples

###### 28.2.1. Maintenance items

The following example illustrates how a new maintenance item is created.

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/MaintenanceInfoInput/v1.beta">
	<soap:Body>
		<addMaintenanceItemRequest version="1.beta" 
								   source="TestMaintenanceInfoInput" 
								   created="2016-09-01T00:00:00Z" 
								   aircraftRegistrationId="LNMEL" 
								   cat="MEL" 
								   type="52-30-01" 
								   isGrounded="false" 
								   isRepaired="false" 
								   remark="SEAT 27 ABC LIGHTS INOP">
			<effective>2016-09-10T12:00:00Z</effective>
			<expiry>2016-09-13T12:00:00Z</expiry>
		</addMaintenanceItemRequest>
	</soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

JCMS now contains the following maintenance item:

| aircraft | code | effective | expiry | is\_repaired | actual fix | remark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LNMEL | 52-30-01 | 10SEP2016 12:00 | 13SEP2016 12:00 | false |  | SEAT 27 ABC LIGHTS INOP |

The next example show how the maintenance item is extended:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/MaintenanceInfoInput/v1.beta">
	<soap:Body>
		<updateMaintenanceItemRequest version="1.beta" 
		                              source="TestMaintenanceInfoInput" 
		                              created="2016-09-01T00:00:00Z" 
		                              aircraftRegistrationId="LNMEL" 
		                              cat="MEL" 
		                              type="52-30-01" 
		                              isGrounded="false" 
		                              isRepaired="false" 
		                              remark="EXTENDED 24H">
			<expiry>2016-09-14T12:00:00Z</expiry>
		</updateMaintenanceItemRequest>
	</soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

| aircraft | code | effective | expiry | is\_repaired | actual fix | remark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LNMEL | 52-30-01 | 10SEP2016 12:00 | 14SEP2016 12:00 | false |  | EXTENDED 24H |

The maintenance item is cleared with the following message:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/MaintenanceInfoInput/v1.beta">
	<soap:Body>
		<updateMaintenanceItemRequest version="1.beta" 
		                              source="TestMaintenanceInfoInput" 
		                              created="2016-09-01T00:00:00Z" 
		                              aircraftRegistrationId="LNMEL" 
		                              cat="MEL" 
		                              type="52-30-01" 
		                              isGrounded="false" 
		                              isRepaired="true" >
			<actualFix>2016-09-13T18:45:00Z</actualFix>
		</updateMaintenanceItemRequest>
	</soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

| aircraft | code | effective | expiry | is\_repaired | actual fix | remark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LNMEL | 52-30-01 | 10SEP2016 12:00 | 14SEP2016 12:00 | true | 13SEP2016 18:45 | EXTENDED 24H |

A cleared maintenance item can be reopened:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/MaintenanceInfoInput/v1.beta">
	<soap:Body>
		<updateMaintenanceItemRequest version="1.beta" 
		                              source="TestMaintenanceInfoInput" 
		                              created="2016-09-01T00:00:00Z" 
		                              aircraftRegistrationId="LNMEL" 
		                              cat="MEL" 
		                              type="52-30-01" 
		                              isGrounded="false" 
		                              isRepaired="false" >
			<actualFix xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:nil="true"/>
		</updateMaintenanceItemRequest>
	</soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

| aircraft | code | effective | expiry | is\_repaired | actual fix | remark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LNMEL | 52-30-01 | 10SEP2016 12:00 | 14SEP2016 12:00 | false |  | EXTENDED 24H |

Finally, the example below shows how to delete a maintenance item:

```
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/MaintenanceInfoInput/v1.beta">
	<soap:Body>
		<updateMaintenanceItemRequest version="1.beta" 
		                              source="TestMaintenanceInfoInput" 
		                              created="2016-09-01T00:00:00Z" 
		                              aircraftRegistrationId="LNMEL" 
		                              cat="MEL" 
		                              type="52-30-01" 
		                              isGrounded="false" 
		                              isRepaired="false" >
			<actualFix xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:nil="true"/>
		</updateMaintenanceItemRequest>
	</soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
```

### Flight Chat


This chapter describes the standard interfaces for publishing flight and assignment
information to the Flight Chat system when relevant changes occur in JCMS.
Flight Chat exposes a REST API to receive this information.

The interfaces publish information for flights that are scheduled to start during
a *moving subscription* window which is by default moved daily.
Every relevant change to any flight leg inside the subscription window or its crew assignments
will generate a message to the Flight Chat REST API. When the window moves,
a full load of the new window is sent.

The flight output interface is based on the Flight Event service (see [Flight Events](flight_events.html#stdif-flight-events))
and the assignment output is based on the Crew On Flight Updates service
(see [Crew On Flight Events](crew_on_flight_events.html#stdif-crew-on-flight-updates)). They utilize the
message receivers pattern (see [Message Receivers](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-receivers-pattern)) to adapt to the
Flight Chat output format, and the Subscription Management pattern (see [Message Receivers](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-receivers-pattern))
to manage the subscriptin configuration.

FlightChat receivers

* FlightChat Flights
* FlightChat CrewOnFlight

##### 29.1. FlightChat Flights formatter

This formatter generates messages on the FlightChat format from the Flight Events interface. Note that this formatter suppresses any events
concerning deleted flight leg instances (represented internally as **implicitly cancelled**).

**Sink**: `from.ioservice.FlightChat_event`

**Class**: `std_interfaces.flightchat.formatters.FCFormatterFlight`

**Options**:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fc\_client\_module | string | name of the generated FlightChatData client module to use,  can be used to override the default client mapping,  default: `ioservice_impl.flightchat.FlightChatData_2_client` |

Example of using custom client module:

```
<!-- in service-mapping XML -->
<assign name="formatter" expr="formatters.FCFormatterFlight(service_logger, fc_client_module='<custom_module_name>')"/>
```

##### 29.2. FlightChat CrewOnFlight formatter

This formatter generates messages on the FlightChat format from the Crew On Flight Updates interface.

*Sink*: `from.ioservice.FlightChat_event`

*Class*: `std_interfaces.flightchat.formatters.FCFormatterCrewOnFlight`

*Options*:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fc\_client\_module | string | name of the generated FlightChatData client module to use,  can be used to override the default client mapping,  default: `ioservice_impl.flightchat.FlightChatData_2_client` |

Example of using custom client module:

```
<!-- in service-mapping XML -->
<assign name="formatter" expr="formatters.FCFormatterCrewOnFlight(service_logger, fc_client_module='<custom_module_name>')"/>
```

##### 29.3. Configuration

###### 29.3.1. IOService builder configuration

Exporting Flight Events to Flight Chat:

```
<ioservice name="FlightChat_event" pattern="repeatingtrigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.flightchat.flight_trigger">
  <description>Trigger for flightchat Flight data Subscription.</description>
  <subscription allow_requests="true" />
  <delta-service name="FlightInput" version="5" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/flightchat/mapping_flights_delta.xml"/>
  </delta-service>
  <load-service name="FlightInput" version="5" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/flightchat/mapping_flights_load.xml"/>
  </load-service>
  <dependencies>
  <smog-service name="FlightChatData" version="2" protocol="openapi">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/flightchat/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/flightchat/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/flightchat/mapping_client.xml"/>
  </smog-service>
  </dependencies>
</ioservice>
```

Exporting Crew On Flight Updates to Flight Chat:

```
<ioservice name="FlightChat_event" pattern="repeatingtrigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.flightchat.asmt_trigger">
  <description>Trigger for flightchat asignments data Subscription.</description>
  <subscription allow_requests="true" />
  <delta-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml">

  <load-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml"/>

### Subscription Manager Service


This chapter describes the interface that can be used to observe and modify the
configuration of supported outbound subscription services at runtime. For an
introduction to the Subscription Management pattern see [Subscription Manager Service](#stdif-subscription-management).

The current version of this interface is 1.beta.

[Link to SubscriptionManagement\_1\_plainxml.xsd](contract/subscription_config/SubscriptionManagement_1_plainxml.xsd)

##### 30.1. Use cases

The interface can be configured as plainxml, SOAP or REST service.
At the moment the recommendation is to use SOAP because it is the easiest way to
configure the service in the integrator.

All examples below are formulated as plainxml for simplified reading.
In response to any request, the subscription management service will always produce
the current (potentially updated) configuration of the matching subscriptions.

```
<configResponse xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/SubscriptionManagement/v1"
    version="1" source="test" created="2021-01-30T10:00:58Z">
  <subscription name="FlightChat_event" block_requests="false">
    <active updated="2021-01-30T00:30:00Z">
      <schedule schedule="gliding">
        <gliding before="0:00" after="24:00" floor="day" />
      </schedule>
      <filter filter="period">
        <period period_start="30JAN2021 00:00" period_end="31JAN2021 00:00" />
      </filter>
    </active>
  </subscription>
</configResponse>
```

###### 30.1.1. Get the current configuration for managed subscriptions

The *getSubscriptionConfig* operation allows retrieval of the current configuration,
including schedule and active filters.

```
<getConfigRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/SubscriptionManagement/v1"
    version="1" source="test" created="2021-01-30T10:00:58Z" />
```

This request will produce a response listing the current configuration of all
managed subscriptions. It is possible to include a list of names or glob expresssions
to filter only matching subscription names.

```
<getConfigRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/SubscriptionManagement/v1"
    version="1" source="test" created="2021-01-30T10:00:58Z" >
  <subscription>FlightChat*</subscription>
</getConfigRequest>
```

###### 30.1.2. Clear an active subscription configuration

The *clearSubscriptionConfig* operation allows to reset the active configuration
of a managed subscription. There are two modes for this operation, *filter\_only*
or full clear.

```
<clearConfigRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/SubscriptionManagement/v1"
    version="1" source="test" created="2021-01-30T10:00:58Z">
    <clear name="FlightChat_event" filter_only="true" />
</clearConfigRequest>
```

In *filter\_only* mode, this request will delete the active filter parameters,
but keep the filter type and schedule intact. In the next run, the service will
recalculate the filter and behave as if this was the first run for the given
filter, i.e. a moving schedule will trigger a new load while a gliding schedule
will just send the changes that match the new filter. Note that for request based
subscriptions, this action will deactivate the subscription, because there is no
automated filter calculation.

In *full clear* mode, the whole subscription configuration is cleared, so that the
default configuration kicks in again (if there is any).

###### 30.1.3. Update a subscription configuration

The *setSubscriptionConfig* operation allows the requester to update the
configuration of a managed subscription. For request based subscriptions this is
the only way to modify the subscription filter. For moving and gliding
subscriptions it can be used to change the schedule. The requested configuration
will be activated the next time the service serving the subscription is run.

The following example sets a gliding daily schedule with period filter.

```
<setConfigRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/SubscriptionManagement/v1"
    version="1" source="test" created="2021-01-30T10:00:58Z">
    <subscription name="FlightChat_event">
      <schedule schedule="gliding">
        <gliding before="0:00" after="24:00" floor="day" />
      </schedule>
      <filter filter="period" />
    </subscription>
</setConfigRequest>
```

The following example sets a moving daily schedule with period filter.

```
<setConfigRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/SubscriptionManagement/v1"
    version="1" source="test" created="2021-01-30T10:00:58Z">
    <subscription name="FlightChat_event">
      <schedule schedule="moving">
        <moving before="0:00" after="24:00" floor="day" time_of_day="3:00" />
      </schedule>
      <filter filter="period" />
    </subscription>
</setConfigRequest>
```

The following example sets request based subscription filter to a specific period.

```
<setConfigRequest xmlns="http://service.jcms.jeppesen.com/SubscriptionManagement/v1"
    version="1" source="test" created="2021-01-30T10:00:58Z">
    <subscription name="FlightChat_event">
      <filter filter="period">
        <period period_start="30JAN2021 00:00" period_end="31JAN2021 00:00" />
      </filter>
    </subscription>
</setConfigRequest>
```

##### 30.2. IOService builder configuration

Exporting Flight Events to Flight Chat:
Note that the ioservice\_builder at the moment doesn’t support repeatingtrigger,
so the actual pattern has to be adopted in the generated file.

```
<ioservice pattern="requestresponse">
      <description>Subscription Manager service.</description>
      <smog-service name="SubscriptionManagement" version="1" protocol="soap">
        <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/subscription_management_1/services.xml"/>
        <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/subscription_management_1/protocol.xml"/>
        <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/subscription_management_1/mapping.xml"/>
      </smog-service>
</ioservice>
```

### NavBlue Flight Planning


This chapter describes the standard interface for publishing flight information to NavBlue Flight Planning when flight related events occur in JCMS.

The interface publish event messages for updates of scheduled flights, before day of operation, as well as aircraft movements, diversions,
return-to-ramp events etc. during day of operation.

Event messages are published by the interface when flight information is updated in the JCMS database (delta) or for a certain period (load).

Two types of messages are sent to NavBlue:

* Import Flight - main leg information.
* Flight Status - updated OOOI times.

The messages have three main sections:

* User information - customer related information
* Leg key - unique key for the leg in NavBlue
* Message body – updated leg information

The properties that are sent to NavBlue are:

| Type | Section | Property | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Import Flight, Flight Status | User | Environment carrier | Customer environment carrier code |
| Import Flight, Flight Status | User | User id | Sending system identifier. |
| Import Flight, Flight Status | Leg Key | Carrier code (ICAO) | The ICAO carrier code of the leg |
| Import Flight, Flight Status | Leg Key | Flight Number + Flight Suffix | Concatenated flight number and suffix of the leg |
| Import Flight, Flight Status | Leg Key | Scheduled departure time | Scheduled departure time of the leg |
| Import Flight, Flight Status | Leg Key | Scheduled departure station (IATA) | Scheduled departure station of the leg |
| Import flight | Message body | Scheduled arrival time | Scheduled arrival time of the leg |
| Import flight | Message body | Scheduled arrival station (IATA) | Scheduled arrival station of the leg |
| Import flight | Message body | Aircraft identifier | The aircraft / tail identifier that the leg is assigned to |
| Import flight | Message body | Estimated departure time | Estimated departure time of the leg |
| Import flight | Message body | Service type (ICAO) | The service type of the leg |
| Import flight | Message body | AtcCallSign | The aircraft call sign of the leg (if known) |
| Flight Status | Message body | Cancelled | If the leg is cancelled or not |
| Flight Status | Message body | New scheduled departure time | Updated scheduled departure time for a leg |
| Flight Status | Message body | Actual off block time | Actual off block time |
| Flight Status | Message body | Off block time fuel | Amount of fuel upon off block time |
| Flight Status | Message body | Actual out time | Actual take off time |
| Flight Status | Message body | Out time fuel | Amount of fuel upon take off |
| Flight Status | Message body | On time | Landing time |
| Flight Status | Message body | On time fuel | Amount of fuel upon landing |
| Flight Status | Message body | Actual in block time | Actual in block time |
| Flight Status | Message body | In block time fuel | Amount of fuel upon in block time |

NavBlue uses FlightNumber, Suffix, Scheduled departure station and Scheduled departure times as key. If the FlightNumber, Suffix or Scheduled
departure station changes an Import Flight and a Flight Status message are sent with the updated information. An additional Flight Status
message is also sent that cancel the old flight leg.

If the Scheduled departure time is changed, the updated scheduled departure time is sent in the Flight Status message. Any subsequent updates
for the same flight uses the updated key.

The following table provides an overview of the message that carries the information for different types of events.
Note however that both an Import Flight and a Flight Status message is sent even if no information is changed since last sent message.

The interface supports a concept of *receivers*. Multiple receivers can be configured in the Flight Events interface where each receiver
is associated with a specific message format, events of interest and other options.

The interface generates event messages for each *receiver* when flight events occur in JCMS.
A *receiver* should rather be seen as a “logical receiver”, and is not necessarily the same as an external system receiving the event messages
since there might be several external systems receiving same event messages for one and the same *receiver*. For NavBlue interface typically
only one receiver is needed.

Default receivers:

* Native (Navblue FlightPlanning version 1)

| Event in JCMS | Native Receiver | NavBlue message type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flight created | X | Import Flight |
| Leg added to multi-leg flight | X | Import Flight |
| Leg cancelled or removed | X | Flight Status |
| Leg re-instated | X | Flight Status |
| Flight renamed (Flight number, Suffix, Scheduled departure station updated) | X | Import Flight (new flight)  Flight Status (Cancel old flight) |
| Scheduled departure time updated | X | Flight Status |
| Any actual times updated | X | Flight Status |
| Estimated departure time updated | X | Import Flight |
| Tail assignment updated | X | Import Flight |
| Service type updated | X | Import Flight |
| Return to ramp | X | Import Flight |
| Return from airborne (forced return) | X | Import Flight |
| Diversion | X | Import Flight |

##### 31.1. Rave user extensions

* The environment aircraft carrier used in NavBlue to identify the
  customer is read from a Rave variable,
  interfaces\_core.%environment\_aircraft\_carrier%. It is possible to
  redefine it in the user. If no value are defined the carrier code for
  the flight leg is used.
* The sending system identifier. The value is read from a Rave variable,
  interfaces\_core.%user\_id%, and is possible to redefine in the user.
  If no value are defined the value ‘joc’ will be sent.

##### 31.2. Configuring message receivers

It’s possible to configure the receivers this interface should use when sending event messages by updating the default SMOG service-mapping
and call the `generator.add_receiver` method.

```
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
  <include href="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.navblue_flight_planning_1/mapping_client.xml"/>

  <output-mapping struct="flight_input.FlightsUpdateMsg">
    <call name="add_receiver_navblue_delta" expr="generator.add_receiver(None, navblue.DeltaFormatterM(service_logger, local_time=True))"/>
    <call name="add_receiver_navblue_load" expr="generator.add_receiver(None, navblue.LoadFormatterM(service_logger, local_time=True))"/>
    output-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

##### 31.3. Custom formatter

It’s possible to configure new message formatters by adding a subclass of the `MessageFormatter` to the configuration layer and
implementing the `format` method.

```
from std_interfaces.common import MessageFormatter

class MyMessageFormatter(MessageFormatter):
    """
    Formatter generating messages containing the flight number of updated flights.
    """

    def format(self, payload, headers):
        """
        @param payload: Object containing updated flight data.
        @type payload:  ioservice_impl.air2_mave2.FlightInput_5_client.FlightsUpdateMsg
        @param headers: Dictionary of headers passed with the incoming request message
        @type headers:  dict
        @return:        Tuple of two lists of equal length, one with output messages content and one with message header attributes
        @rtype:         (list of string, list of dict)
        """
        contents = list()
        headers = list()
        for action in payload.action:
              contents.append(str(action.setFlight.flightNumber))
              headers.append(dict())
        return contents, headers
```

Receivers can be configured for messages generated by the custom formatter by passing instances of it to the `generator.add_receiver` method as described in [Configuring message receivers](#configuring-message-receivers).

##### 31.4. Delta formatter

This formatter produces Import Flight and Flight Status upon any change of legs within the subscription period window. If the leg key for the leg is change an additional
Flight Status message is created.

*Class* `std_interfaces.navblue_flight_planning_1.formatters.DeltaFormatter`

##### 31.5. Load formatter

This formatter produces Import Flight and Flight Status messages for all legs starting in the subscription period window.

*Class* `std_interfaces.navblue_flight_planning_1.formatters.LoadFormatter`

##### 31.7. IOService builder configuration

### Jeppesen Crew Request


This interface is responsible for extracting data from the Atrium system and send it to the Jeppesen Crew Request application.

The current version of CrewRequestData is 1, `std_interfaces.crewrequest_1`.

##### 32.1. Overview of the business process

The Jeppesen Crew Request system allows some crew members to submit certain requests regarding their schedule. The tracker will try to fulfill those requests considering the efficency of the schema.
For example, crew members that are scheduled for reserve tomorrow, will be offered to request either to fly (tomorrow-trips that currently are in open time), to be on standby at the airport or to have a day off if possible.
The day before their scheduled reserve duty, there will be a time window opened during which the corresponding crew group will be able to place the above mentioned requests. Crew members are divided in groups usually based on their rank and base.
Once the time window is closed, the requests will be fetched by the trackers who will grant or decline them.
Once the granting deadline is reached i.e. granting window closes, the granting result is sent to the Crew Request system and the crew members will be able to see whether their requests have been granted or declined.

###### 32.1.1. Export from Atrium to Jeppesen Crew Request

The Jeppesen Crew Request application can be considered as an “empty” application meaning that its necessary data has to be fed into it in order to function.
Exports are meant to be scheduled on regular basis. Most of them can also be initialized from the Information Center.

* Account Data
  Contains the crew members that are allowed to place requests.
  Process name: `CrewRequestData.getAccountData`
* Crew Export
  Process name: `CrewRequestData.getCrewData`
  Contains crew IDs of those crew that will be able to place requests. The feed contains also crew specific details as qualifications
* Window Period data
  Process name: `CrewRequestData.getRequestWindowData`
  Exports information about when each crew group can place request and in which period.
* Trips in the Open Time
  Process name: `CrewRequestData.getTripData`
  Contains the trips that can be requested.
* Destination data
  Process name: `CrewRequestData.getDestinationData`
  Contains information about destination stations of the trips that can be requested.

##### 32.2. Configuration

* Rave
  Rave module``interfaces\_core`` contains a number a of `%crewrequest_*%` that needs to be redefined. For more details regarding each of them please have a look at the module.
* Queues
  Configuration is placed in `$CARMUSR/etc/ccf.xml`
* IOServer Template
  Configuration is placed in `$CARMUSR/etc/programs/ioservices/datafeeds/CrewRequestData_1_plainxml.xml`
* Location Data
  Configuration is placed in `$CARMUSR/etc/crewrequest/locationdata.xml`

###### 32.2.1. IOService builder configuration

Service CrewRequestData version 1

```
<ioservice pattern="requestresponse">
  <description>Crew request</description>
  <smog-service name="CrewRequestData" version="1" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/jeppesen_crewrequest/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/jeppesen_crewrequest/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/jeppesen_crewrequest/mapping.xml"/>
  </smog-service>
</ioservice>
```

### Jeppesen AOC bookshelf Maintenance message input


This chapter descibes the standard interface adapter to receive maintenance related information in AOC bookshelf message format.
The adapter is used as a pre-processor in the maintenance info input interface. It does accept a subset of MX messages and extracts the
relevant information into a native SMOG structure to be processed by the native interface.

Example:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<AOCMessage xmlns="http://www.jeppesen.com/aoc" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.jeppesen.com/aoc ../AOC/AOCMessage.xsd ">
	<header>
		<trackingId>String</trackingId>
		<msgClass>PUBLISH</msgClass>
		<msgName>MX001</msgName>
		<owner>customer</owner>
		<version>2</version>
		<timestamp>2011-08-02T09:30:47.0Z</timestamp>
	</header>
	<message>
		<maintenance>
			<dmiReport>
				<airlineCode>
					<iata>WN</iata>
					<icao>SWA</icao>
				</airlineCode>
				<access>
					<name>user2</name>
					<key>acessKey</key>
				</access>
				<dmiParent>true</dmiParent>
				<dmiId>
					<dmiClass>MEL</dmiClass>
					<ataCode>CF33</ataCode>
					<controlNumber>97685e</controlNumber>
					<aircraftId>
						<serialNumber>N1234</serialNumber>
					</aircraftId>
				</dmiId>
				<dmiData>
					<position>forward galley</position>
					<multiplier>1</multiplier>
					<effectiveTime>2011-08-04T09:30:47.0Z</effectiveTime>
					<expirationTime>2011-08-07T09:30:47.0Z</expirationTime>
					<aircraftGroundedIndicator>No</aircraftGroundedIndicator>
					<dmiText>Warmer in forward galley is nonfunctional</dmiText>
				</dmiData>
			</dmiReport>
		</maintenance>
	</message>
</AOCMessage>
```

The following table lists the messages currently supported and their mappings to native messages:

| ID | Message | JCMS mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MX001 | DMI Report | addMaintenanceItem |
| MX002 | Update DMI Report | updateMaintenanceItem |
| MX003 | Clear DMI | updateMaintenanceItem (set fix time) |
| MX004 | Delete DMI | deleteMaintenanceItem |
| MX005 | Reopen DMI | updateMaintenanceItem (clear fix time) |
| MX006 | Extend DMI | updateMaintenanceItem (update expiry time) |

### Jeppesen AOC bookshelf message events


This chapter describes the standard interfaces for publishing flight
information to other systems that support the Jeppesen AOC bookshelf messages.

The interfaces publish information for flights that are scheduled to start during
a *moving subscription* window which is by default moved daily.
Every relevant change to any flight leg inside the subscription window
will generate an AOC bookshelf message. When the window moves, a full load of the new window is sent.

The flight output interface is based on the Flight Event service (see [Flight Events](flight_events.html#stdif-flight-events))
and the assignment output is based on the Crew On Flight Updates service message
receivers pattern (see [Message Receivers](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-receivers-pattern)) to adapt to the AOC bookshelf message formats,
and the Subscription Management pattern (see [Subscription Manager Service](subscription_management.html#stdif-subscription-management)) to manage the subscription
configuration.

The AOC bookshelf message for crew assignment changes can be configured as an extra receiver in the CrewOnFlight trigger mapping.
(see [Crew On Flight Events](crew_on_flight_events.html#stdif-crew-on-flight-updates)).

Jeppesen AOC receivers

* Jeppesen AOC Flights
* Jeppesen AOC Crew Assignments

##### 36.1. Jeppesen AOC Flights formatter

This formatter generates messages on the AOC OCxxx formats from the Flight Events interface.

*Sink*: default sink, typically `from.ioservice.JeppesenAoc_event`

*Class*: `std_interfaces.jeppesen_aoc.aoc_formatters.AOCMessageFormatter`

*Options*:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| logger | logging.Logger | logger to use for debugging information |
| AOC\_OWNER | environment variable | AOC message field “owner” must be the same for outgoing and incoming messages, also it must be different on the test/prod system so JSI can distinguish |

##### 36.2. FlightChat Crew Assignments formatter

This formatter generates messages on the FlightChat format from the Crew On Flight Updates interface.
Note that this formatter suppresses any events concerning deleted flight leg instances (represented internally as *implicitly cancelled*).

*Sink*: default sink, typically `from.ioservice.JeppesenAoc_event`

*Class*: `jeppesen_aoc.aoc_formatters.AOCMessageFormatter_Crew`

*Options*:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| logger | logging.Logger | logger to use for debugging information |
| AOC\_OWNER | environment variable | AOC message field “owner” must be the same for outgoing and incoming messages, also it must be different on the test/prod system so JSI can distinguish |

###### 36.2.1. Use cases

##### 36.3. Daily Batch

Every day at the time defined by the subscription schedule (default 0:30), an OC001 message is emitted for every flight leg
with a scheduled departure time within the subscription period, (default today 0:00 - 24:00).
Note that there is currently no handling of overlapping subscription windows, i.e. OC001 is emitted for all flights
in the window with no check whether such a message was emitted for that flight before.

##### 36.4. New or Updated Flights

If flight information is updated in JOC, a corresponding AOC OCxxx message is emitted.

| Event in JCMS | AOC message type |
| --- | --- |
| Flight created | OC001 |
| Leg added to multi-leg flight | OC001 |
| Leg cancelled | OC002 |
| Leg deleted | OC003 |
| Leg re-instated | OC004 |
| Flight renamed | OC018 |
| Planned aircraft type updated | OC011 |
| Service type updated | N/A |
| Tail assignment updated | OC011 |
| Scheduled times updated | OC010 |
| Scheduled departure station updated | not yet supported |
| Scheduled arrival station updated | not yet supported |
| Onward flight updated | N/A |
| Passenger terminal updated | N/A |
| Seat configuration updated | N/A |
| Estimated departure times updated | OC012 |
| Delay information updated | N/A |
| Actual departure times updated | OC023, OC015 |
| Return to ramp | OC018 + OC005 + OC001 Rename and Divert the old leg then create new leg |
| Estimated arrival times updated | OC012 |
| Actual arrival times updated | OC016, OC024 |
| Internal times updated | N/A |
| Return from airborne | OC020 |
| Diversion | OC018 + OC005 + OC001 |
| Payload updated | WB002 |

###### 36.4.1. IOService builder configuration

Exporting Flight Events to Jeppesen AOC:

```
<ioservice name="JeppesenAoc_event" pattern="repeatingtrigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.jeppesen_aoc.flight_trigger">
  <description>Trigger for AOC Flight data Subscription.</description>
  <subscription allow_requests="true" />
  <delta-service name="FlightInput" version="5" protocol="plainxml">
      <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/services.xml"/>
      <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/protocol.xml"/>
      <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/jeppesen_aoc/mapping_flights_delta.xml"/>
  </delta-service>
  <load-service name="FlightInput" version="5" protocol="plainxml">
      <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/services.xml"/>
      <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_input_5/protocol.xml"/>
      <service-mapping location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/jeppesen_aoc/mapping_flights_load.xml"/>
  </load-service>
</ioservice>
```

##### 36.5. FlightChat Crew Assignments formatter

This formatter generates messages on the FlightChat format from the Crew On Flight Updates interface.

*Sink*: default sink, typically `from.ioservice.JeppesenAoc_event`

*Class*: `jeppesen_aoc.aoc_formatters.AOCMessageFormatter_Crew`

*Options*:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| logger | logging.Logger | logger to use for debugging information |

###### 36.5.1. Use cases

##### 36.6. Daily Batch

Every day at the time defined by the subscription schedule (default ?:??), a CT001 message is emitted for every flight leg
with a scheduled departure time within the subscription period,(default today 0:00 - 24:00).
Note that there is currently no handling of overlapping subscription windows, i.e. CT001 is emitted for all flights
in the window with no check whether such a message was emitted for that flight before.

##### 36.7. Updated Crew Assignments

If Crew Assignments are updated in JOC, a corresponding AOC CT001 message is emitted.

###### 36.7.1. Mapping configurations

Delta service:

```
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
  <include href="../../../../../../../src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/mapping_trigger_delta.xml"/>
  <input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest">
    <import alias="formatters_aoc" name="std_interfaces.jeppesen_aoc.aoc_formatters"/>
    <!-- Default values for configurable values parameters, set the correct value on the configuration layer -->
    <!-- Message Owner, use owner name or function to determine owner name which will be used by JSI to filter messages -->
    <assign name="owner_value" expr="'owner'"/>
    <!-- HiMin Qualification Name, use the name defined for the HiMin Qualification, if the crew has said qualification the system will add HiMin to the CT001 -->
    <assign name="hi_min_qual_name" expr="'AAA'"/>
    <assign name="aoc_formatter" expr="formatters_aoc.AOCMessageFormatter_Crew(service_logger, owner_value, hi_min_qual_name)"/>
    <call name="add_formatter_aoc" expr="generator.add_receiver('from.ioservice.JeppesenAoc_event', aoc_formatter)"/>
  </input-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

Load service:

```
<service-mapping xmlns="http://namespace.jeppesen.com/smog/v2" target="air2_mave2" language="Python">
  <include href="./mapping_aoc_delta.xml"/>
  <input-mapping struct="flight_output.CrewOnFlightRequest">
    <!-- find affected flights-->
    <call-last name="find_flights" expr="flights.extend(generator.find_all_flights())"/>
  </input-mapping>
</service-mapping>
```

###### 36.7.2. IOService builder configuration

Exporting Crew Assignments to Jeppesen AOC:

```
<ioservice name="CrewOnFlight_4_event" pattern="repeatingtrigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4.trigger">
  <description>Trigger for AOC Crew Assignments Subscription.</description>
  <subscription allow_requests="true" />
  <delta-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml" >
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces/crew_on_flight_4/trigger/config/mapping_aoc_delta.xml" />
  </delta-service>
  <load-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml">
    <service-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml"/>
    <protocol-spec location="$CARMSYS/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml"/>
    <service-mapping location="$CARMUSR/data/config/smog/v2/std_interfaces/crew_on_flight_4/trigger/config/mapping_aoc_load.xml" />
  </load-service>
</ioservice>
```

### Jeppesen FliteBrief events


This chapter describes the standard interfaces for publishing flight and assignment
information to Jeppesen FliteBrief system.

The interfaces publish information for flights that are scheduled to start during
a *moving subscription* window which is by default moved daily.
Every relevant change to any flight leg inside the subscription window or its crew assignments
will generate a Flitebrief SCH001 message. When the window moves, a full load of the new window is sent.

The flight output interface is based on the Flight State service (At the time of implementation, this service in beta version)
and the assignment output is based on the Crew On Flight Updates service
(see [Crew On Flight Events](crew_on_flight_events.html#stdif-crew-on-flight-updates)). They utilize the
message receivers pattern (see [Message Receivers](implementation_patterns.html#stdif-receivers-pattern)) to adapt to the
Flitebrief SCHO001 message formats,
and the Subscription Management pattern (see [Subscription Manager Service](subscription_management.html#stdif-subscription-management))
to manage the subscription configuration.

Jeppesen Flitebrief receivers

* Jeppesen Flights
* Jeppesen Crew Assignments

##### 37.1. Jeppesen Flights formatter

This formatter generates messages on the Flitebrief SCH001 format from the Flight State interface.

*Sink*: default sink, typically `from.ioservice.FlightState_1_beta_event.fb`

*Class*: `std_interfaces.jeppesen_flitebrief.formatters.FBFormatterFlight`

*Options*:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| logger | logging.Logger | logger to use for debugging information |

##### 37.2. FlightChat Crew Assignments formatter

This formatter generates messages on the Flitebrief SCH001 format from the Crew On Flight Updates interface.

*Sink*: default sink, typically `from.ioservice.CrewOnFlight_4_event.fb`

*Class*: `std_interfaces.jeppesen_flitebrief.formatters.FBCrewOnFlightFormatter`

*Options*:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| logger | logging.Logger | logger to use for debugging information |

###### 37.2.1. Use cases

##### 37.3. Daily Batch

Every day at the time defined by the subscription schedule (default 0:30), an Flitebrief SCH001 message is emitted for every flight leg
with a scheduled departure time within the subscription period,(default today 0:00 - 24:00).
Note that there is currently no handling of overlapping subscription windows, i.e. Flitebrief SCH001 is emitted for all flights
in the window with no check whether such a message was emitted for that flight before.

##### 37.4. New or Updated Flights

If flight information is updated in JOC, a corresponding Flitebrief SCH001 message is emitted.

| Event in JCMS | FB message type |
| --- | --- |
| Flight created | SCH001 |
| Leg added to multi-leg flight | SCH001 |
| Leg cancelled or removed | SCH001 |
| Leg re-instated | SCH001 |
| Flight renamed | SCH001 |

###### 37.4.1. IOService builder configuration

Exporting Flight State to Jeppesen Flitebrief:

```
<ioservice name="FlightState_1_beta_event" pattern="trigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.jeppesen_flitebrief.flight_trigger">
    <description>Output flight leg state, on-event updates.</description>
    <subscription>
      <filter name="all" />
    </subscription>
    <delta-service name="FlightState" version="1.beta" protocol="plainjson">
      <service-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/services.xml"/>
      <protocol-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/protocol.xml"/>
      <service-mapping location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/jeppesen_flitebrief/mapping_flights_delta.xml"/>
    </delta-service>
    <load-service name="FlightState" version="1.beta" protocol="plainjson">
      <service-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/services.xml"/>
      <protocol-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.flight_state_1/protocol.xml"/>
      <service-mapping location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/jeppesen_flitebrief/mapping_flights_load.xml"/>
    </load-service>
  </ioservice>
```

Exporting Crew On Flight Updates to Jeppesen FliteBrief:

```
<ioservice name="CrewOnFlight_4_event" pattern="trigger" handler_module="std_interfaces.jeppesen_flitebrief.asmt_trigger">
  <description/>
  <subscription allow_requests="true" />
  <delta-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml" >
      <service-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml" />
      <protocol-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml" />
      <service-mapping location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/jeppesen_flitebrief/mapping_asmts_delta.xml"/>
  </delta-service>
  <load-service name="CrewOnFlight" version="4" protocol="plainxml" >
      <service-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/services.xml" />
      <protocol-spec location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/std_interfaces.crew_on_flight_4/protocol.xml" />
      <service-mapping location="$BASEDIR/src/resources/smog/v2/jeppesen_flitebrief/mapping_asmts_load.xml"/>

</ioservice>
